sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: Breaking the Safe Passing Law and causing bodily injury brings a five hundred dollars fine and two points, while a violation without injury brings a one hundred dollars fine and no points.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: What three visibility items must a bicycle carry after dark—and what caution still applies to drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: A bicycle ridden after dark must have front and rear lights and a rear reflector, though these can still be hard for drivers to see.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: Whom must a motorist signaling a right turn let pass through the intersection first?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: A driver signaling a right turn must yield to bicyclists, skateboarders and inline skaters going through the intersection.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: How do your responsibilities toward cyclists and skaters work on right turns compared with left turns?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: When turning right, wait for cyclists and skaters to clear and avoid cutting in front of them, but when turning left, yield to oncoming cyclists and skaters and let one ahead of you in the turn lane finish first.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.front: How may a bicyclist or skater position themselves in traffic lanes to make a left turn?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.expected_back: A cyclist or skater turning left may use the traffic lanes like a vehicle and may ride along the right edge of the turn lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: What mechanical feature, top speed, and lane-position rule define a moped in New Jersey?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Mopeds are low-speed two-wheelers with pedals that may not go faster than twenty-five miles per hour and must ride on the right with the flow of traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: What wheel count, speed window, and fuel restriction define a New Jersey low-speed vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: A low-speed vehicle has four wheels and can reach more than twenty miles per hour but no more than twenty-five miles per hour on pavement, and it cannot run on gas or diesel.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: May motorized scooters ride on New Jersey public streets or sidewalks—and what is the lone exception?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: Riding a motorized scooter on public roads or sidewalks is illegal, with the only exception being designated municipal or county property.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: What registration, insurance, and minimum-age rules govern motorized scooters in New Jersey?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: A motorized scooter must be registered where the owner lives and insured, and no one under twelve, or the local minimum age, may operate one.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.front: Which four mini rigs count as motorized scooters—and which four electric or mobility vehicles do not?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.expected_back: Pocket bikes, mini choppers, mini motorcycles and motorized skateboards count as motorized scooters, but e-bikes, low-speed vehicles, motorized wheelchairs and mobility scooters for people with disabilities do not.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.front: On which posted streets—and up to what scooter speed—may someone with a mobility disability operate certain motorized scooters?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.expected_back: A person with a mobility-related disability may use certain motorized scooters on streets posted at twenty-five miles per hour or less, and on streets posted up to thirty-five miles per hour if the local government approves, with a top scooter speed of fifteen miles per hour

sec13-card-sec13-R18.front: What road-use ban, crossing allowance, and paperwork rules apply to snowmobiles, ATVs, and dirt bikes?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.expected_back: Snowmobiles, ATVs and dirt bikes may not ride on public roads with other traffic, but they may cross certain roads when it is safe, and their operators must carry proof of insurance and display registration.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: How far can a fifty-five-mile-per-hour freight train travel before stopping, and who holds right of way?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: A freight train going fifty-five miles per hour can need a mile or more to stop, and trains always have the right of way.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.front: What schedule, track-direction, and visual-speed realities explain why you must never race a train?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.expected_back: Trains can run on any track, in either direction, at any time, and they are closer and faster than they appear, so never race one to a crossing.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: When is it safe to pull onto railroad tracks, and how far do trains overhang beyond the steel rails?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: Only enter a railroad crossing when there is room to clear the tracks completely on the far side, since a train can stick out three feet or more beyond the rails on each side.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.front: Within what distance of a railroad crossing is passing banned, and what manual-gear rule applies on the rails?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.expected_back: Do not pass other vehicles within one hundred feet of a railroad crossing, and do not shift gears on the tracks in a manual transmission vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.front: Which roadside sign shape-and-color and pavement markings warn that railroad tracks lie ahead?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.expected_back: A yellow round railroad advance warning sign and white railroad pavement markings tell you a crossing is ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.front: Why is driving or walking across railroad tracks outside a designated crossing illegal as well as dangerous?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.expected_back: Crossing tracks anywhere except a designated crossing is dangerous and illegal because railroad property is private.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.front: What maximum speed applies when approaching or passing a horseback rider or horse-drawn vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.expected_back: When approaching or passing someone riding a horse or driving a horse-drawn vehicle, slow to twenty-five miles per hour or less and go carefully.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: Besides slowing to twenty-five or less near horses, what must you do if an oncoming rider raises a hand?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Drivers must slow to twenty-five miles per hour or less near a horse, and must stop completely and wait if a rider coming the other way raises a hand or signals.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.front: Under which three time, visibility, or weather conditions must a horse-drawn vehicle display a front light?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.expected_back: A horse-drawn vehicle must show a front light from thirty minutes after sunset to thirty minutes before sunrise, whenever visibility is five hundred feet or less, and in fog, mist or smoke.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.front: Why should you avoid swerving sharply for an animal, and what visual habit protects you instead?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.expected_back: Swerving to dodge an animal often causes a crash with something else or a rear-end hit, so watch both sides of the road ahead and be ready for sudden movement.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Which three types of valid documents must every motorist carry whenever driving in New Jersey?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Anyone driving in New Jersey must carry a valid license, a valid probationary license, or a validated New Jersey permit, and must also carry valid insurance and registration cards.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Who must always ride along whenever you drive using a validated New Jersey permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: A driver using a validated New Jersey permit must always have an appropriately licensed driver along.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: If wording in the driver manual ever conflicts with an actual statute or state regulation, which controls?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: When the manual and a statute or regulation disagree, the statute or regulation is what governs.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: How soon after moving—even out of state—must a motorist report the new address to the MVC?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: After moving, a motorist has one week to report the new address to the MVC, and this rule also covers people moving out of the state.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Within what deadline must you report a legal name change from marriage, divorce, or court order to the MVC?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: A legal name change, such as through marriage, divorce or a court order, must be reported to the MVC within two weeks.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How does New Jersey's address-change deadline compare with its legal name-change deadline?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: An address change must be reported within one week of moving, while a legal name change gets two weeks; the two deadlines are easy to swap.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: How long does a new resident holding a valid out-of-state car license have to apply in New Jersey?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: A new resident holding a valid out-of-state license must apply for a New Jersey license within sixty days, or before the old license expires if that is sooner.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: How soon must a new resident transfer a commercial driver license, and what happens to the old card?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: The newcomer deadline for a commercial driver license (CDL) is thirty days, and the out-of-state license is surrendered once the New Jersey license is received.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: For how long may a motorist legally drive in New Jersey using a valid license from another country?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: A motorist whose valid license comes from another country may drive on it for up to one year.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How do the timelines compare for regular out-of-state transfers, CDL transfers, and valid foreign licenses?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: A new resident with a regular out-of-state license has sixty days to apply in New Jersey, a CDL holder has only thirty days, and a driver with a license from another country may drive on it for up to one year.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Which step-by-step program must every applicant complete if they have never held a driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: Anyone who has never held a driver license must complete the Graduated Driver License (GDL) Program, which phases in privileges after a stretch of supervised driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: What signed paperwork must any license applicant younger than eighteen bring in?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: A license applicant under eighteen must present a consent form that a parent or guardian has completed and signed.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: Which drivers under twenty-one must display two MVC reflective GDL decals, and where are they mounted?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Drivers under twenty-one holding an examination permit, special learner's permit or probationary license must show two reflective GDL decals, supplied by the MVC, on the vehicle's license plates.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: What New Jersey credential must a motorist already hold before applying for a commercial driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Commercial vehicle drivers face tougher testing than car or motorcycle drivers and must already hold a valid basic New Jersey license before they apply for a CDL.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: What is the minimum CDL age, and what geographic and endorsement bans apply under age twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: CDL applicants must be at least eighteen, and those under twenty-one may drive only inside New Jersey and cannot receive HAZMAT or passenger endorsements.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: Where are all New Jersey licenses and IDs manufactured since 2021, and what security check fights identity theft?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: Since a two thousand twenty-one security upgrade, every New Jersey license and non-driver ID, Standard or REAL ID, is produced at a secure central facility that uses facial recognition to fight identity theft.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: What do you leave the MVC counter holding, how long is it valid, and how does your plastic card arrive?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: At the transaction you receive a temporary license or ID that is valid for thirty days, and the card itself is mailed to you, with delivery expected within thirty days.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: Which card orientation goes to motorists under twenty-one, and how many years do licenses and IDs last?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: Motorists under twenty-one receive a vertical-format license or non-driver ID card, and licenses and IDs are valid for four years.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: How does the lifespan of your counter-issued temporary license compare with the mailed plastic card?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: The temporary paper license or ID lasts thirty days, while the mailed card itself is valid for four years.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: When do license endorsements expire, and which single endorsement follows a shorter retest schedule?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: An endorsement expires together with the license it is on, except Hazmat, which requires retesting every two years.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: What sets a Hazmat endorsement apart from every other New Jersey license endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: Most endorsements simply expire with the license, but a Hazmat endorsement must be retested every two years.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: How does the MVC calculate the fee when you add an endorsement partway through your current license cycle?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: When an endorsement is added to an existing license, its charge is prorated for the time left until the license expires.

sec01-card-sec01-R20.front: What typical prorated fee applies when returning after one year to upgrade to a Standard or REAL ID license?
sec01-card-sec01-R20.expected_back: A license-chart footnote says a motorist who must return to a Licensing Center after one year to upgrade the license pays a prorated fee, usually nineteen dollars and fifty cents Standard or twenty-nine dollars REAL ID.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: What three punishments can strike someone who alters a license, gets one by fraud, or shows a doctored card?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: Altering a license or ID, obtaining one by fraud, or presenting an altered one can bring loss of driving privileges, fines up to one thousand dollars, imprisonment, or a combination.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: On New Jersey's license requirement chart, what four screenings do the letters K, V, R, and C stand for?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: In the license chart, K means the Knowledge test, V the Vision test, R the Road test and C the Commercial test.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: Which vehicles does a basic Class D auto license cover, and what are its permit and license minimum ages?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: The basic automobile license covers every MVC-registered Class D vehicle except motorcycles, with a minimum age of eighteen and a permit age of sixteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: What are the permit age, minimum license age, permit and decal fees, and license fee on the probationary auto row?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: The probationary automobile license has a minimum age of seventeen with a permit at sixteen, a permit fee of ten dollars plus four dollars for red reflectorized decals, and a sixty-three dollars license fee.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How do the minimum ages for basic and probationary auto licenses compare, and what permit age do both share?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: The basic automobile license requires age eighteen and the probationary automobile license age seventeen, yet both list a permit age of sixteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What permit fee, Standard and REAL ID license fees, and three required screenings appear for a basic auto license?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: The basic automobile license chart lists a ten dollars permit fee and license fees of twenty-four dollars Standard or thirty-five dollars REAL ID, and requires knowledge, vision and road tests.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: Which vehicle types and letter classes fall under a CDL, what does the permit cost, and what extra screening applies?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: A commercial driver license covers large trucks, buses and similar vehicles in Classes A, B and C, carries a one hundred twenty-five dollars permit fee and adds a commercial test.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: What vehicles does Class E cover, what are the two ways it is issued, and what is the minimum age?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: A motorcycle license (Class E) covers most vehicles with fewer than four wheels and is issued either as its own license or as an M endorsement on a basic New Jersey license, with a minimum age of seventeen.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: At what age can unlicensed riders get a moped license, and which existing license holders don't need one?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: A moped license is for unlicensed motorists aged fifteen or older and is not required for anyone who holds a Class A, B, C, D or E license.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: What work is an agricultural license restricted to, which ages qualify, and when does it end?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: An agricultural license is only for farming, may be granted to people aged sixteen to seventeen, and lasts four years or until the holder gets a basic license at eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: How does the starting age for a moped license compare with an agricultural license?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: A moped license starts at age fifteen, while an agricultural license is granted at sixteen to seventeen and is for farming only.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: Who needs a New Jersey boat license, and what certificate must every power-vessel operator present?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: A boat license is for people sixteen or older running a motorboat on fresh, non-tidal waters, and every power-vessel operator must show a Boating Safety Certificate when applying.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: What three core categories of proof must a Standard New Jersey license applicant bring?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: A Standard license applicant provides proof of a Social Security or Taxpayer Identification Number (or an affidavit of ineligibility), one proof of New Jersey address and six points of identification.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: Which document buckets must combine to reach a Standard applicant's six identification points?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: A Standard license applicant needs a mix of documents: one or more primary documents, one or more secondary documents, a total of at least six ID points, and proof of a New Jersey home address.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: Which four major birth, passport, or state cards count as primary identity proofs for a Standard license?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: Primary proofs of identity for a Standard license include a US birth certificate, a US passport or passport card, a passport from the applicant's country of citizenship, and a digitized New Jersey license or non-driver ID.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.front: What extra item must accompany a foreign-issued photo driver license for it to count toward identity?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.expected_back: A foreign-issued photo driver license counts toward identity only when it is presented together with another government-issued document.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.front: For a Standard license, how long past its expiration date can a primary or secondary ID document still count?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.expected_back: For a Standard license, no primary or secondary document may be more than three years past its expiration date.

sec01-card-sec01-F42.front: What is the maximum number of one-point documents a Standard applicant can count toward six points?
sec01-card-sec01-F42.expected_back: Standard license applicants may count no more than two one-point documents toward their six points.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.front: What extra legal-status proof does the Standard document chart note specifically for CDL applicants?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.expected_back: The Standard document chart carries a separate note that CDL applicants must prove US citizenship or lawful permanent resident status.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: What must accompany any identification document that is not written in English?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Identification documents must be written in English or be accompanied by an approved translation.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: What physical condition and official markings are required on identity documents?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: Identity documents must be unlaminated originals or certified copies, in English, and carry the required state or municipal seal.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: How can the MVC respond when submitted documents conflict or look altered, false, or invalid?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: If documents conflict the MVC may ask for more, and it may refuse any permit or license application when a document looks altered, false or invalid.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.front: What details must appear on Standard residency proof, and how recent must utility bills versus pay stubs be?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.expected_back: A Standard license proof of New Jersey residency must show the applicant's name and home address, for example a utility or credit card bill up to one year old or a pay stub up to six months old.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: How many address proofs does a Standard license require, and how old may bank, utility, or government mail be?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: For a Standard license, address proofs such as a bank statement, a utility or credit card bill, or first class government mail may be up to one year old, and only one address proof is needed.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: Which two MVC-issued cards both show your address yet cannot be paired together as two address proofs?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: A valid New Jersey license and a valid New Jersey vehicle registration both show an address, but they cannot be submitted together as address proofs.

sec01-card-sec01-R18.front: Which two bank items cannot be submitted together, and how may you protect private account numbers?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.expected_back: An ATM or debit card and a bank statement cannot be submitted together, and financial details on documents may be blacked out.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: What exact combination of address, Social Security, identity points, and status proof does REAL ID require?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: A REAL ID license applicant provides two proofs of New Jersey address, one proof of the full Social Security number and six points of identification, including proof of lawful presence in the United States.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.front: In what order do REAL ID Steps I, II, and III organize your paperwork?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.expected_back: REAL ID Step I is the two address proofs, Step II is one proof of the full Social Security number, and Step III is the six points from primary and secondary documents.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.front: How many documents may you pick from the REAL ID primary list?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.expected_back: For REAL ID you select one and only one document from the primary list, for example an unexpired US passport or passport card, or a certified US birth certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.front: When can paper proofs already shown in REAL ID Steps I and II count again in Step III?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.expected_back: Paper documents already used in REAL ID Steps I and II may also serve as secondary options in Step III when they appear on that list.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.front: In REAL ID Step III, how many one-point secondary documents can count toward your six-point total?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.expected_back: In REAL ID Step III no more than two one-point secondary documents may be used toward the six points.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: How recent must utility bills, bank statements, and first-class government mail be for REAL ID address proof?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: For REAL ID the address windows are tighter: a utility or credit card bill from the past ninety days, a bank or credit union statement from the past sixty days, or first class government mail from the past six months.

sec01-card-sec01-R19.front: On the REAL ID secondary list, which states qualify for an unexpired photo license versus a non-driver ID?
sec01-card-sec01-R19.expected_back: On the REAL ID secondary list an unexpired standard photo license may come from New Jersey or any state, but an unexpired standard non-driver ID card counts only if New Jersey issued it.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: What must you bring if your current legal name no longer matches your birth certificate?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: If your current legal name differs from your birth certificate, you must show legal proof of the change, such as a certified marriage or civil union certificate, divorce decree, or court order linking the names.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: What two details must appear inside a divorce decree to restore a previous name at the MVC?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: A divorce decree supports going back to a previous name only if it lists both the married and previous names and permits the return to the previous name.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: What exact name change can a marriage or civil union certificate prove compared with a divorce decree?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: A marriage or civil union certificate can be used only to prove a change of last name, while a divorce decree supports only a return to a previous name that it lists.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: How does a Standard applicant without SSN eligibility or an ITIN satisfy that requirement?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: An applicant who cannot get a Social Security number and has no ITIN may file an affidavit, which must be notarized or signed in front of an MVC agency employee.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: What must you bring if the Social Security Administration database cannot verify the number on your application?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: If the Social Security Administration cannot verify the number given on the application, the applicant must bring a document showing the full name and full number, such as a Social Security card or a W-two from the past year.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: What document verification standard must every New Jersey driver license applicant satisfy?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Every applicant for a New Jersey driver license must have all the documents needed to satisfy the six-Point ID Verification.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: What eye screening applies to every motorist, and what two follow-ups may the MVC require for impaired sight?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Every motorist must pass a vision screening; the MVC may send applicants with impaired vision to a physician and may periodically require a recheck.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: What visual acuity standard must basic license applicants meet, with or without corrective lenses?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: Basic license applicants need twenty over fifty vision, with or without corrective lenses.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: What acuity standard and paperwork apply when an applicant has vision in only one eye?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: An applicant who sees with only one eye must have that eye meet the twenty over fifty rule and bring documentation signed by a licensed physician.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: What acuity in both eyes and color-recognition check must CDL applicants pass?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: CDL applicants need twenty over forty vision in both eyes, with or without corrective lenses, and must tell red, green and amber lights apart.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: How does the vision standard for a basic license compare with the vision standard for a CDL?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Basic license applicants need twenty over fifty vision with or without corrective lenses, while CDL applicants need twenty over forty in both eyes plus the ability to tell red, green and amber lights apart.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Which self-certification and medical paperwork must commercial drivers file under federal and state rules?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: Federal law and New Jersey rules require commercial drivers to file a CDL Holder Self-Certification form and, if applicable, a medical examiner's certificate completed by a federally certified medical examiner.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: What must license applicants disclose to the examiner regarding health, and what can follow?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: Applicants must tell the examiner about health problems, and a medical review may be necessary.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: How many scored items appear on the New Jersey knowledge check, and what extra survey item is included?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: The knowledge test has fifty questions, plus a survey question about organ donation.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: What percentage and exact number of right answers out of fifty are needed to pass the written screening?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: To pass the written test, eighty percent of the answers must be correct, which is forty of the fifty questions.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: Along with English and American Sign Language, how wide is New Jersey's written-screening language menu?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: The knowledge test is offered in English and American Sign Language, and also in Albanian, Arabic, Chinese, French, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish and Turkish.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: How does the MVC accommodate an applicant who cannot read in any language?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: An applicant who cannot read in any language is given headphones and takes the knowledge test orally.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: What prerequisite must happen before you can use a state-approved interpreter for an unlisted native language?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: If your native language is not offered you may use a state-approved interpreter, but only after first attempting the test in one of the offered languages.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: How far in advance must you notify the MVC when you need an interpreter for your written screening?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: An applicant who needs an interpreter must tell the MVC at least two weeks before the planned date of the written knowledge test.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: Even though ASL is built in, what two steps precede getting an interpreter for an unlisted foreign language?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: The knowledge test language list includes American Sign Language, but a state-approved interpreter for an unlisted language is arranged only after a failed attempt in an offered language and with at least two weeks' notice.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: Who supplies and pays for approved Deaf or Hard of Hearing interpreters, and what paperwork triggers payment?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: The MVC provides approved interpreters for Deaf or Hard of Hearing applicants and pays the knowledge-test interpreter fees once a completed payment voucher form is submitted.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Which New Jersey court registry determines whether a foreign-language interpreter is state-approved?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: An approved foreign-language interpreter is someone listed on the Registry of Interpreters and Agencies kept by the NJ Administrative Office of the Courts, Language Services Section.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: Which two qualification paths make a Deaf or Hard of Hearing interpreter state-approved?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: An approved deaf or hard of hearing interpreter either holds certification from the National Registry of Interpreters for the Deaf and is on file with the NJ Division of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing, or has been evaluated by that Division and placed on its approved list.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: How is the appointment set once a foreign-language interpreter is secured, and how are Deaf interpreter fees paid?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: Once a foreign-language interpreter is secured, an MVC employee contacts the applicant with the appointment date and time, while for Deaf or Hard of Hearing applicants the MVC pays the knowledge-test interpreter fees after a payment voucher form.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: Which transfer applicants aged eighteen or older can have both knowledge and road screenings waived?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: Knowledge and road tests may be waived for transfer applicants aged eighteen or older with a valid, non-provisional license from any of the fifty states, the District of Columbia, Samoa, Guam, Puerto Rico or the US Virgin Islands.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: Even when screenings are waived, what must an adult out-of-state transfer submit, receive, and surrender?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: Transfer applicants still submit the six-Point ID documents, receive a four-year basic New Jersey license and must surrender the out-of-state license.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: What New Jersey credential and rules apply to an out-of-state transfer aged seventeen to eighteen holding a valid license?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: An out-of-state applicant aged seventeen to eighteen with a valid license receives a probationary license for one year and must follow New Jersey's GDL rules.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: How does the license issued to an eighteen-plus non-provisional transfer differ from a seventeen-to-eighteen transfer?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: A transfer applicant aged eighteen or older with a valid non-provisional license gets a four-year basic license, while one aged seventeen to eighteen gets a probationary license for one year under GDL rules.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: Which screenings must every out-of-country applicant pass, what else may apply, and how long do results last?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: Every out-of-country applicant must pass the knowledge test and vision screening and may also have to pass a road test; the results are valid for two years.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: How do screening waivers differ between U.S. state transfers and foreign-country applicants?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Out-of-state transfer applicants may have the knowledge and road tests waived, but every out-of-country applicant must pass the knowledge test and vision screening.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: When did Nikhil's Law take effect, and what warning did it add into New Jersey's licensing statute?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Signed in August two thousand fifteen and in force from March one, two thousand sixteen, Nikhil's Law amended N.J.S.A. thirty-nine:three-forty-one to stress the dangers of ignoring New Jersey traffic laws.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: What four safe-driving commitments make up the Safety Pledge to Nikhil?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: The Safety Pledge to Nikhil commits drivers to stop completely, stay alert, talk safe with a hands-free system and plan ahead by allowing an extra five minutes for every trip.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: When can eligible citizens start voter registration at the MVC, and how many days before an election is the cutoff?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: Eligible voters can start voter registration at any MVC Licensing Center while applying for or renewing a license or non-driver ID, and the registration deadline is twenty-one days before an election.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: How can someone register to vote or update a voting address without doing an MVC card transaction?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: Someone not doing a license or ID transaction can still register to vote or change a voting address through the New Jersey Division of Elections, which can mail an application.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: How are MVC address changes submitted, and what follow-up question appears during that process?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: Address changes must be done online, and the MVC then asks whether the change should also update your voter record.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: Where does the MVC forward address updates, and whom should you call if no voter confirmation arrives?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: Address changes reported to the MVC online or by mail are forwarded to the New Jersey Division of Elections, and you should contact your local Commissioner of Registration if no confirmation arrives.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: Which address must you legally keep on file with the MVC, and how can your plastic card show it?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: The law requires you to give the MVC your current New Jersey home address, and a replacement license showing the new address can be ordered after the change is processed.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: Which steps must be completed before the MVC validates a permit for practice driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: Once the knowledge test, vision screening and any required behind-the-wheel course are passed, the MVC validates the permit for practice driving.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: How many months, total hours, and dark hours of supervised practice must GDL holders under twenty-one finish before road evaluation?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: GDL permit holders under twenty-one need at least six months of supervised practice with at least fifty hours, ten of them in darkness, before a road test appointment.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: How long must GDL permit holders aged twenty-one or older practice under supervision before a road appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: GDL permit holders aged twenty-one or older need at least three months of supervised practice before a road test appointment.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: How do pre-road-appointment practice minimums compare between GDL permit holders under twenty-one and twenty-one-plus?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Before a road test appointment, GDL permit holders under twenty-one need six months and at least fifty supervised hours with ten after dark, while those twenty-one and older need only three months.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: Which signed form from a parent, guardian, or supervising driver must be handed in at the road appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: A completed BA-CSD form from a parent, guardian or supervising driver must be presented at the time of the road test appointment.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: Which two MVC areas are strictly off-limits for practice driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: Practice driving is not allowed on the road test course or in the parallel parking area.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: Which five original items—covering your ID, permit, and car—must you bring to the road appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: Road test applicants must bring original documents: six points of ID, a legible unlaminated validated permit, a valid inspection sticker or the official card saying none is required, and valid registration and insurance ID cards for the test vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: What exterior GDL markers must already be mounted on a GDL applicant's vehicle at the road appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: GDL applicants must also have two red GDL decals properly mounted on the test vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: What insurance rule applies if you bring a vehicle registered in another state to your New Jersey road appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: A test vehicle registered in another state must meet that home state's insurance identification laws.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.front: Under what contract condition may you use a rental car for your road evaluation?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.expected_back: A rental car is allowed only if the applicant is named as a driver on the rental agreement, and the applicant must arrive with a licensed driver.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.front: Can a permit holder inch the car forward alone in the road-evaluation queue while the accompanying driver steps out?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.expected_back: A licensed driver must stay in the vehicle with the applicant at all times, and the car may not be moved even in the road test line without one.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.front: When must your accompanying licensed driver—rather than you—drive the car to the road-evaluation site?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.expected_back: If the accompanying driver is licensed outside New Jersey or has under three years of experience, that person must drive the vehicle to the road test area.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.front: Does the MVC provide vehicles for road evaluations, and who is allowed inside during the drive?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.expected_back: The MVC does not supply road test vehicles, and only MVC examiners may be in the vehicle during the test.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.front: Besides your driving skills, what else can end your road evaluation before you even roll out?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.expected_back: Many applicants assume only their driving is graded, but the vehicle itself can cause a denial, and an examiner may refuse even an initial road test in an unsuitable or unsafe car.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: What brake access must the right-seat examiner have inside your road-evaluation vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: The examiner must be able to reach the foot brake or a parking brake mounted to the right of the driver.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.front: Which two vehicle types are barred from the road evaluation, and what three visibility or signal items must work?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.expected_back: Autocycles and self-parking vehicles cannot be used, and the signals, brake lights and windshield wipers must all work.

sec03-card-sec03-F43.front: Which five sticker, brake, dashboard-light, or tire issues commonly get a vehicle turned away?
sec03-card-sec03-F43.expected_back: Common road test vehicle rejections include an improper, expired or missing inspection sticker, no examiner access to a brake, poor brakes, a lit brake warning light and unsafe tires.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.front: What paper saves a car that failed inspection, and why does a fast engine idle get rejected?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.expected_back: A vehicle that failed inspection is rejected unless the motorist brings the Vehicle Inspection Report from the inspection station, and a fast engine idle is rejected because speed control cannot be judged.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.front: Starting from which manufacturing date must every vehicle have seat belts to pass pre-drive inspection?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.expected_back: Seat belts are required on all vehicles manufactured after July one, nineteen sixty-six, so missing belts get a test vehicle rejected.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.front: Which four front-tint, mirror, glass, or door defects will get your vehicle rejected?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.expected_back: Window tint on the driver or front door windows, missing interior or driver-door mirrors, broken or cracked glass, and doors or windows that will not work from inside all get a vehicle rejected.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.front: What brake-pedal, lighting, and interior cleanliness standards apply to your road-evaluation car?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.expected_back: Brakes must not fade or sink to the floorboard, the parking brake, brake lights and signal lights must work, and the interior must be reasonably clean.

sec03-card-sec03-R17.front: For motorcycle and moped road evaluations only, which four rider-gear or horn problems cause rejection?
sec03-card-sec03-R17.expected_back: For motorcycle and moped tests only, missing state-required equipment, no helmet, unapproved goggles or face shield, or no bell or horn audible at one hundred feet also cause rejection.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.front: In what two course settings may an MVC examiner ride along to grade your safe driving?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.expected_back: During the road test an MVC examiner rides with the applicant in an off-road test area or on a public road course to confirm the applicant knows the rules and drives safely.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.front: What extra skill will the examiner check if you bring a manual-transmission car?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.expected_back: If the test vehicle has a standard transmission, the examiner will ask the applicant to show correct gear shifting.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.front: Which core driving maneuvers—including reversing, parallel parking, turns, turnarounds, and yielding—appear on the basic road check?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.expected_back: The basic road test covers driving in reverse, following other vehicles, nearing corners and intersections, parallel parking, sitting properly with a seat belt, starting, steering, stopping at signs, stopping smoothly, turning, turning around, using the horn and yielding right-of-way.

sec03-card-sec03-F41.front: What slip do you get upon passing the road evaluation, and what three items go to a Licensing Center?
sec03-card-sec03-F41.expected_back: After passing the road test you receive an authorization for licensing, and the permit, the authorization and six Points of ID must be taken to a Licensing Center.

sec03-card-sec03-F42.front: Which license does a brand-new driver receive, and for how long does the MVC monitor their driving habits?
sec03-card-sec03-F42.expected_back: An applicant never before licensed anywhere receives a Class D basic or probationary license, and the MVC monitors that driver's habits for one year.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: Unless posted otherwise, which three New Jersey zones carry a twenty-five-mile-per-hour speed limit?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Unless another limit is posted, the New Jersey speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour in school zones and in business or residential districts.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: Unless posted otherwise, what default speed limit governs suburban business and residential districts in New Jersey?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Unless another limit is posted, the limit in suburban business and residential districts is thirty-five miles per hour

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How do New Jersey's two lowest unposted speed limits—twenty-five and thirty-five—split up districts?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: The two lowest default limits are easy to swap: twenty-five miles per hour covers school zones and business or residential districts, while thirty-five miles per hour covers suburban business and residential districts.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What default speed limit applies on unposted rural roadways in New Jersey?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Unless another limit is posted, the limit on rural roads without posted limits is fifty miles per hour

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: Which two road categories carry New Jersey's fifty-five-mile-per-hour speed limit?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: The fifty-five miles per hour limit applies to certain state highways, as posted, and to interstates.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: Where is driving sixty-five miles per hour legal in New Jersey?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: The sixty-five miles per hour limit applies only to certain interstate highways where it is posted.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: What distinguishes where fifty-five applies from where sixty-five applies on New Jersey highways?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: The two highway limits are also easy to swap: fifty-five miles per hour applies to certain posted state highways and to interstates, while sixty-five miles per hour applies only to certain posted interstate highways.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: What happens to ticket fines when you go ten or more over—or commit most moving violations—inside a sixty-five zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Going ten miles per hour or more over the sixty-five miles per hour limit doubles the fine, and most other moving violations in a sixty-five miles per hour zone carry doubled fines too.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: How does speeding hurt crash odds, crash violence, and your window to react?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.memory_hook: Higher risk, harder hits, less time
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Speeding raises both the chance of a crash and how severe it is, and it leaves the driver less time to react to hazards or correct mistakes.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: How sensitive are pedestrian injury and survival odds to even small changes in vehicle speed?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: Even a small increase in speed sharply raises the risk that a pedestrian struck in a crash is badly hurt or killed, and lower speeds greatly improve pedestrian survival.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: Can driving at or below the posted speed limit still earn a moving violation in bad weather or heavy traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: Never drive faster than the weather, road or traffic allows, whatever the posted limit says; driving too fast for conditions can bring a moving violation.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: Name the road features, crossings, weather, and sightline conditions that always demand slowing down?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Always slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, at sharp or blind curves, near pedestrians or hazards, on wet or icy roads and when visibility is limited.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.front: When should you shed speed for a curve, and what lane risk must you watch for inside it?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.expected_back: Enter a curve by slowing down beforehand and staying out of other lanes, and watch for vehicles drifting into yours.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: When pavement and traffic are clear and normal, what does New Jersey law say about crawling far below pace?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: When the road surface and traffic are normal, New Jersey law forbids holding up traffic by driving too slowly.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: What should you do if engine trouble keeps your car from maintaining safe traffic speed?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Some crashes are caused by driving too slowly or backing up in traffic; if a vehicle problem keeps you from keeping up, pull safely off the road and turn on the hazard lights.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: What passing rule applies when both yellow centerlines are solid?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: When both center lines are solid, no passing is allowed.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: When one centerline stripe is dashed and the partner stripe is solid, which direction may overtake?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: When one center line is broken, passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: Who may pass when both parallel centerline stripes are broken?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: When both center lines are broken, passing is allowed from either side.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: How do you read solid, mixed, and double-broken centerlines from the driver's seat?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Center line markings read from your own side: two solid lines forbid passing, a broken line on your side permits it, and two broken lines permit it from both sides.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: Before what pavement-marking change must every two-lane pass be completely finished?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: Every pass must be finished before the center lines turn solid again.

sec06-card-sec06-R24.front: When may you legally cross solid no-passing lines between intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.expected_back: Solid lines between intersections mark no-passing zones, but they may be crossed carefully when turning into or out of a driveway in a business or residential area.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Signed in July two thousand three, what penalty rule does New Jersey's Safe Corridors law enforce?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: The Safe Corridors law, signed in July two thousand three, doubles fines on designated state highways for offenses such as speeding and aggressive driving.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: Which two crash statistics put a New Jersey state highway onto the Safe Corridors list?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: Highways are designated Safe Corridors when their crash rate is fifty percent above the state rate and at least one thousand crashes were reported over three years.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: Passing belongs normally on the left—which two narrow situations allow passing on the right?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Passing is normally done on the left; passing on the right is permitted only where the road has more than one lane in your direction and traffic is moving in two or more steady lines, or where the driver ahead is turning left and there is room.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: May you ever drop tires onto the right road shoulder to squeeze past a left-turning vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: Passing on the right shoulder of the road is never allowed and is against the law.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: List the blind terrain, crossings, structures, markings, and pedestrian situations where passing is banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Do not pass on a hill or curve or whenever you cannot see far enough ahead, at an intersection or railroad crossing, on narrow bridges or in underpasses or tunnels, where signs or center lines forbid it, or behind a vehicle stopped to let a pedestrian cross.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: Which half of the road must New Jersey drivers hug, and what are the two exceptions?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: New Jersey law requires driving on the right half of the road, as close as practical to the right edge or curb, except when passing or on a one-way street.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: Which lane is your home lane on a multi-lane New Jersey road when not overtaking or turning left?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: On a multi-lane road, use the available lane nearest the right edge or curb, except when overtaking another vehicle or preparing for a left turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: Which emergency responders and rail vehicles command your right-of-way every time?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Always yield to police cars, fire engines and ambulances that are using sirens or flashing lights, and to a train approaching a railroad crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: Which two public-service vehicles receive right-of-way when pulling back into traffic from the curb?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: Buses and postal vehicles re-entering the flow of traffic are given the right-of-way.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.front: Does a legal crosswalk require white paint—and where do crosswalks exist by default?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.expected_back: Crosswalks may be marked or unmarked, and one exists at every corner of an intersection unless signs prohibit pedestrians from crossing there.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: What exact pedal action does New Jersey require when a pedestrian is inside a marked or unmarked intersection crosswalk?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: A driver must come to a full stop, not merely slow or yield, for a pedestrian in a marked crosswalk or one crossing at an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: Once stopped for a crosswalk pedestrian, how far across must they walk before you roll again?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: Stay stopped until the pedestrian has cleared both your lane and the next lane going in your direction.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: What must you do if your light turns green and Don't Walk appears while someone is still crossing?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Stop for every pedestrian still in a crosswalk even if the signal has changed to Don't Walk.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: What two actions around crosswalks—involving stopped cars and parking—are strictly prohibited?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Never overtake a vehicle that has stopped at a crosswalk for a pedestrian, and never block or park in a crosswalk.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Which five penalties—money, jail, service, license, and points—can hit drivers who fail to stop for pedestrians?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Not stopping for a pedestrian can cost a fine of up to five hundred dollars, a jail term of up to twenty-five days, community service, a suspension of driving privileges of up to six months, and two motor vehicle points.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: Along with walkers on foot, whom else must you yield to at crosswalks and inside intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: Yield to people using motorized or mobility-assistance devices in a crosswalk or trying to cross, and to other vehicles already inside the intersection.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: Where do most crashes happen, and what does a single solid white bar across the road mean there?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Most crashes happen at intersections, and a single solid white line across the road there means stopping behind it for a traffic signal or sign.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.front: How does New Jersey classify cutting across private property to bypass a red light or stop sign?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.expected_back: Cutting through private property to get around a traffic signal or sign is a motor vehicle violation.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: At an all-way stop, how are earlier arrivals and simultaneous ties decided?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: At a multi-way stop, a driver who arrives at the same moment as another yields to the one on the right, and also yields to any vehicle already stopped there.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: What speed and right-of-way duties apply at a posted yield sign?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: At a yield sign, slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic on the crossing road, stopping if needed.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: How does right-of-way at a multi-way stop contrast with right-of-way at a yield sign?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: A multi-way stop gives the right-of-way to the driver on the right when two arrive together, while a yield sign requires slowing and giving way to the crossing road's traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: Within how many feet of the crosswalk or stop line must you halt at a New Jersey stop sign?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: At a stop sign, come to a complete stop within five feet of the nearest crosswalk or stop line, then enter only after yielding to pedestrians and to any traffic close enough to be an immediate hazard.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: How must every approach treat a traffic signal gone dark from a power outage or malfunction?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: A traffic signal that is dark because of a power failure or other malfunction is treated as a four-way stop.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: How do you approach an unsigned crossroad versus pulling out of a private driveway?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: Approaching an uncontrolled crossroad, slow down and be ready to stop for traffic from either side, and when coming out of a private road or driveway yield to all traffic on the main road.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.front: When tall corn, trees, bushes, buildings, or parked cars hide cross traffic, how must you adjust?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.expected_back: On rural roads trees or crops, and elsewhere buildings, parked cars or bushes, can block the view of cross traffic, so slow down or stop fully before going ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: At an uncontrolled intersection, which driver yields under New Jersey's baseline rule?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: As a general rule at an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: Since New Jersey sets no single statewide traffic-circle rule, what three clues govern right-of-way at circles?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: New Jersey has no set rules for traffic circles: the circle's established flow pattern usually decides the right-of-way, a major highway running through it usually dominates, and stop or yield signs at the entrances also govern.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Which baseline intersection rule takes over whenever right-of-way inside a traffic circle is unclear?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: When it is unclear who has the right-of-way in a traffic circle, fall back on the basic uncontrolled-intersection rule: the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle approaching from the right.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: How are highways, parkways, and turnpikes built—and who yields at an acceleration-lane merge?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.expected_back: Highways, parkways and turnpikes are divided roads with speeds up to sixty-five miles per hour and no direct intersections, entered by an acceleration lane, and drivers must yield to traffic already on the main road.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.front: What speed goal and stopping caution apply as you merge off a highway acceleration lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.expected_back: When entering a highway, speed up to the flow of traffic as you leave the acceleration lane and avoid stopping completely in that lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.front: What must you do—and never do—if you sail past your intended highway exit?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.expected_back: If you miss an exit, continue to the next one, and never back up on an exit ramp or deceleration lane.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: How do your speed actions contrast between an acceleration lane and a deceleration lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: An acceleration lane is for speeding up and should not be stopped in, while a deceleration lane is where you start slowing down and obey its advisory speed.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.front: Which side carries most highway exits, and how do you handle an occasional left-side exit?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.expected_back: Most exit ramps and deceleration lanes are on the right; when an exit is on the left, follow the signs that direct traffic to the proper exit lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.front: Inside a shared weave lane serving both entering and exiting expressway cars, which driver yields?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.expected_back: In a weave lane, which serves as both an entrance and an exit, the driver coming from the entrance ramp must yield to the driver leaving the expressway.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.front: How should you navigate the tight curving ramps of a cloverleaf interchange?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.expected_back: At a cloverleaf interchange, watch for the entrance and exit signs and drive slowly through the loop at the posted speed.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.front: Which lanes does New Jersey recommend on multi-lane city highways during heavy rush hour?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.expected_back: On highways through cities, drive in the left or center lane during rush hour to avoid merge conflicts, and look for your exit early.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.front: What three habits keep you safe entering, picking a lane at, and leaving a highway toll plaza?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.expected_back: At toll plazas, slow down early because traffic may back up, look for green lights marking open booths, and check both sides for merging traffic when leaving.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.front: How should you respond when you spot a broken-down vehicle on the highway shoulder ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.expected_back: When you see a disabled vehicle ahead, slow down and leave more space, possibly by changing lanes, and watch for pedestrians, tow trucks and police.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.front: List the shoulder, signal, cabin, and personal-safety rules if your own car breaks down on a highway?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.expected_back: If your vehicle breaks down, pull as far onto the shoulder or median as you can, turn on the flashers, raise the hood, stay inside with the seat belt on and doors locked, and never get into a stranger's vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: Whom must you yield to and whom must you stop for whenever turning left?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and stop for pedestrians in the crosswalk.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.front: Before making any turn—including right on red—what full visual sweep protects cyclists and walkers?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.expected_back: Watch carefully for pedestrians when turning, including right turns on red, and before any turn scan left, right and behind and check mirrors and blind spots for cyclists and pedestrians.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.front: Under what sign check, stopping rule, and yield duty is turning right on red legal in New Jersey?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.expected_back: Unless a No Turn on Red sign is posted, a right turn on red is allowed after a full stop, and the driver must yield to all oncoming traffic and pedestrians first.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.front: Which slim road users might hold a green light across your path while you turn right on red?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.expected_back: Bicycles, mopeds and other hard-to-see vehicles may have a green light while you turn right on red, so look for them before turning.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.front: How close to the right edge should you position for a right turn, and what steering mistake is banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.expected_back: For a right turn, approach as far to the right as possible, close to the curb or parked cars, and do not swing wide or into another lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.front: When you and an oncoming driver face each other and both turn left, where relative to center do you pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.expected_back: When two vehicles facing each other both turn left, each should turn to the left of the center of the intersection when it is safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.front: Which departure lane and arrival lane belong to a left turn from one one-way street onto another?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.expected_back: For a left turn from a one-way road onto another one-way road, approach in the left lane and turn into the left lane of the new road.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.front: Turning left from a two-way street onto a four-lane highway, which lane do you enter first—and what comes next?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.expected_back: For a left turn from a two-way road onto a four-lane highway, turn into the lane nearest the center line, which is the passing lane, and move right out of it when traffic allows.

sec06-card-sec06-R23.front: How do you line up and finish a left turn from one two-way street onto another two-way street?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.expected_back: For a left turn from a two-way road onto another two-way road, approach close to the line nearest the center of the road and keep to the right of the center line of the road you enter.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: During which window at a traffic light do most signal crashes occur, and how should you start on a fresh green?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Most crashes at traffic signals happen in the first few seconds after the light changes, so take care when moving off on a fresh green.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: What should you do when a green light turns yellow ahead — and what if it flips while you are already inside the intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: When a yellow light follows a green, stop before the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely, and if the light changes while you are already in the intersection, continue through with caution.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: What is a stale green traffic light, and what phase change should you anticipate?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: A stale green is a light that has already been green for some time, so be ready for it to turn yellow and then red.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: Which octagon sign and which two red signal displays always require a complete stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: A driver must stop at a stop sign and at a red light, whether the red is steady or flashing.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: Which cane-carrying or guide-dog pedestrians — including trainers — require drivers to come to a stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: A driver must stop for a blind pedestrian using a white or metallic cane or a trained guide dog, and for a guide dog instructor who is training a dog.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: Along with pedestrians on foot, which mobility users at a crosswalk or intersection require drivers to stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: A driver must stop for a pedestrian in a crosswalk or at an intersection, and for a motorized wheelchair or mobility-assistance device there.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: When must you come to a full stop for a traffic officer or at a YIELD sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: A driver must also stop when a traffic officer orders it, and at a yield sign when traffic does not allow a safe merge.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: What stopping duty applies when emerging from an alley, private driveway, or building — and at an opening drawbridge?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: A driver must also stop when coming out of an alley, private driveway or building, and at a bridge span that is about to open for boats.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: Which six static, lit, gated, audible, or human warnings can mark a New Jersey railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: Railroad crossing warnings can include advance-warning signs, pavement markings, flashing red lights, gates with or without flashing lights, ringing bells and flag signals.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: At least how many feet back must you stop at a railroad crossing when lights flash, bells ring, gates lower, or flags wave?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: Stop at least fifteen feet from a railroad crossing when there are flashing red lights, ringing bells, lowering or lowered gates, or flag signals.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: After halting at an active railroad crossing, which three signals must all clear before you drive across?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Do not cross the tracks until the gates are up, the bells have stopped ringing and the red lights have stopped flashing.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: How much distance do most trains traveling sixty miles per hour or faster need to stop, and what rule follows?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: Most trains moving at sixty miles per hour or more need over a mile to stop, so never race a train.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Which three vehicle types must stop at every railroad crossing, and how should you drive behind them?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: School buses, buses and vehicles carrying hazardous materials must always stop at railroad crossings, so be ready to stop behind them even when no train is signaled.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: What space check prevents getting trapped on railroad tracks — and what must you do if warning bells start while you are already on them?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: Never stop on railroad tracks; make sure there is room to get fully across, and if the warning devices start while you are on the tracks, keep going to the other side.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: What two situations around a school bus require every approaching driver to stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: A driver must stop when a school bus is picking up or dropping off children or has its red lights flashing.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: What light sequence do school buses use when stopping, and why shouldn't drivers behind a bus rely solely on those lights?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: School buses turn on yellow or amber lights before stopping and red lights once stopped, but drivers behind a bus should not rely on those lights because they could be broken.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: How many feet away must you stop for a red-flashing school bus, and on which three road types does that full stop apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: For a school bus with flashing red lights, stop at least twenty-five feet away on a two-lane road, on a multi-lane highway whose lanes are separated only by lines, or on a privately maintained road.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: On a dual-lane highway, what must you do when a stopped school bus is across a safety island or raised median from you?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: On a dual-lane highway where you are on the other side of a safety island or raised median from a stopped school bus, slow to ten miles per hour

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: When a school bus stops directly in front of a school to load or unload, how may drivers pass from either direction?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: When a school bus has stopped directly in front of a school to load or unload, you may pass it from either direction at no more than ten miles per hour

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: Which two specific New Jersey school-bus scenarios replace the twenty-five-foot full stop with a ten-miles-per-hour speed cap?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: Two separate ten miles per hour rules apply to school buses: slow to ten miles per hour when you are across a safety island or raised median on a dual-lane highway, and pass at no more than ten miles per hour when the bus is stopped directly in front of a school.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: When may you resume driving after stopping for a school bus, and whom must you still watch carefully for?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: After stopping for a school bus, move on only once its signals are off, and even then watch for children and people with developmental disabilities.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: What three-step sequence applies when approaching an ice cream or frozen dessert truck displaying flashing red lights and a stop arm?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: For an ice cream or frozen dessert truck showing flashing red lights and a stop signal arm, yield to anyone crossing to or from it, stop, and then pass at no more than fifteen miles per hour

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: On a dual highway, must a driver on the far side of a safety island or raised median stop for a frozen dessert truck?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: A driver on the far side of a safety island or raised median on a dual highway does not have to stop for a frozen dessert truck.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: How do you clear the way for a signaling emergency vehicle, and how far back must you stay afterward?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: When an emergency vehicle uses its siren or flashing red or blue lights, steer to the far right, stop and let it pass, then stay at least three hundred feet behind any signaling emergency vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How does New Jersey split red warning lights from blue warning lights among emergency responders?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Police cars, fire trucks, ambulances and other emergency vehicles use sirens and red lights, while private vehicles of volunteer fire and rescue squad members answering a call, with emergency vehicle identification, use blue lights.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: How close may you park to a fire department vehicle in service, and when may you drive across a fire hose?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Never park within two hundred feet of a fire department vehicle in service, and never drive over a fire hose unless a fire, rescue or police official tells you to.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: Keep New Jersey's two emergency-vehicle distances straight — following a signaling rig versus parking near a fire rig in service?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: Two emergency-vehicle distances are easy to swap: stay at least three hundred feet behind a signaling emergency vehicle, and never park within two hundred feet of a fire department vehicle in service.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: Which stopped vehicles — including disabled civilian cars — trigger New Jersey's Move Over lane-change rule when safe?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: The Move Over law requires moving into a lane not next to a stopped emergency, tow, highway maintenance or other service vehicle showing flashing lights, or a stopped vehicle using hazard lights, flares or reflective triangles, when safety and traffic allow.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: Under New Jersey's Move Over law, what must you do when changing lanes is impossible, illegal, or unsafe?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: If moving over is impossible, illegal or unsafe, slow to a reasonable speed below the posted limit and be ready to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: What dollar fine range hits a Move Over violation, and when do motor vehicle points get added?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: A Move Over violation carries a fine of one hundred dollars to five hundred dollars, and three or more convictions can also bring motor vehicle points.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: When patrol lights flash behind your car, what three immediate steps bring you to a safe stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: When emergency lights appear behind you, signal, slow down and move promptly to the right shoulder or another safe place.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: Once pulled over by police, what five gear, cabin, window, lighting, and hand positions should you take?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: During a police stop, put the vehicle in park, stay inside unless told otherwise, roll down the window, switch on the interior light at night and keep your hands visible, ideally on the steering wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.front: Why shouldn't you dive into the glove box or console during a police stop before the officer asks — and what else keeps things calm?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.expected_back: During a police stop, turn the music down, avoid sudden movements, and do not reach for documents, the glove box, the console or under a seat unless told to, saying first what you are about to do.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.front: When is switching on your vehicle's interior overhead light appropriate?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.expected_back: Interior overhead lights should be used only briefly while driving, or when a police officer asks you to light up the inside of a stopped vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: Which three credentials or papers must every New Jersey driver produce at a traffic stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: At a traffic stop, New Jersey drivers must show a valid driver license, the vehicle registration and proof of insurance.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.front: How should you respond to an officer's requests — including stepping out — or to an instruction you did not catch clearly?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.expected_back: Follow the officer's instructions, including stepping out of the vehicle if asked, and politely ask for an instruction to be repeated if it is unclear.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.front: If you think a traffic stop or ticket is unfair, where should you challenge it instead of arguing at the roadside?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.expected_back: If you disagree with a stop, do not argue at the roadside; you can contest the ticket later in court or file a complaint with the law enforcement agency.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: Between which exact sunset and sunrise offsets must New Jersey drivers run their headlights?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: Headlights are required from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise.
