sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: Regardless of the clock, which visibility distance, wiper setting, and weather conditions require headlights?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: Headlights are also required whenever visibility is five hundred feet or less, whenever the windshield wipers are in use, and in fog, mist, smoke or anything else that cuts visibility.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: Can parking lights or auxiliary lights legally substitute for headlights when headlights are required?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: Parking lights or auxiliary lights may not legally take the place of headlights when headlights are required.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.front: How are fog lights classified, and which headlight beam setting pairs legally with them in fog?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.expected_back: Fog lights are auxiliary lights that may be used together with low beams to light the road ahead in foggy weather.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: Where are high beams appropriate, and which two traffic encounters require switching them off?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: Use high beams only in open country with no traffic in sight, and switch them off when another vehicle approaches or when you are following one.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: Contrast the driving environments calling for high beams against the four everyday situations calling for low beams?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: High beams are for open country with no traffic in sight, while low beams are for city driving, heavier traffic, following another vehicle and meeting oncoming vehicles.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.front: What happens inside a driver's eyes at night that lets sudden bright headlights blind them momentarily?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.expected_back: At night the pupils are dilated, and bright beams can blind other drivers for a moment by making their pupils constrict.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: How many seconds can glare recovery take after oncoming high beams, and how far do you travel at fifty miles per hour meanwhile?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: Recovering from the glare of oncoming high beams can take three to five seconds, and at fifty miles per hour a driver covers the length of a football field in that blind time.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: Where should you aim your eyes if an oncoming driver leaves high beams on — and why shouldn't you flash yours back?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: If an oncoming driver has high beams on, look toward the right side of the road until it passes, and never flash your own high beams back.

sec07-card-sec07-R16.front: When do taillights illuminate at night versus in daylight, and how do they show braking?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.expected_back: Taillights come on with the headlights and parking lights and grow brighter when the brakes are applied; in daylight they also light up when braking.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.front: What balance should you strike when adjusting dashboard instrument lights at night?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.expected_back: Keep dashboard lights dim enough to avoid glare but bright enough to read the dials.

sec07-card-sec07-R19.front: For what sole purpose are spotlights and hazard flashers meant — and what use of spotlights is strictly banned?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.expected_back: Spotlights and hazard flashers are for emergencies only, and spotlights may never be used for driving.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: Where must a parked vehicle keep its parking lights switched on?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: Parking lights are required on vehicles parked anywhere other than business or residential zones.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: What is the maximum legal distance between a parked vehicle and the curb in New Jersey?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: Parking a vehicle more than six inches from the curb is illegal.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: Within how many feet of a fire hydrant is parking prohibited in New Jersey?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: Do not park within ten feet of a fire hydrant.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: How far must you park from an intersection crosswalk, and what single junction type is exempt?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: Do not park within twenty-five feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, except at alleys.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: Which two traffic controls share New Jersey's fifty-foot no-parking distance?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: Do not park within fifty feet of a railroad crossing or within fifty feet of a stop sign.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: What no-parking distances apply on the same side of a fire station driveway versus across the street?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: Do not park within twenty feet of a fire station driveway, or within seventy-five feet of the entrance on the opposite side of the street.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Which two different New Jersey locations both enforce a twenty-foot no-parking buffer?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: Two different twenty-foot no-parking rules exist: within twenty feet of the end of a pedestrian safety zone, and within twenty feet of a fire station driveway entrance.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.front: From sidewalks, bus zones, and driveways to tunnels, double parking, and disability spots, where is stopping or parking always banned?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.expected_back: Never stop or park in a crosswalk, on a sidewalk, in a bus stop zone, in front of a driveway, inside an intersection, on an interstate, on a bridge, elevated roadway or in a tunnel, next to a car already parked at the curb, or in a disability space without authorization.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.front: Why must you scan for traffic, bikes, and mopeds before opening your street-side door — and which side should passengers exit?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.expected_back: Before opening the driver-side door, check for traffic and for hard-to-see bicycles and mopeds, because a driver who opens a door into traffic may be liable for the crash; passengers should get out on the curb side.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.front: Where should you pull over and what lights should you activate during mechanical trouble or an emergency?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.expected_back: If your vehicle has mechanical trouble or another emergency, stop on the right shoulder and turn on the emergency flashers.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.front: How does New Jersey classify handheld phone or texting use on public roads versus hands-free phone use?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.expected_back: Using a handheld phone or texting device while driving on any public road is a primary offense, while a hands-free phone is legal but strongly discouraged.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.front: Which five emergencies permit using a handheld phone while driving, and what steering rule still applies?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.expected_back: A handheld phone may be used only in an emergency such as a fire, a traffic crash, a serious road hazard, a medical emergency or a hazardous material emergency, and one hand must stay on the wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.front: What evidence might a driver have to show in court to prove a handheld call met the emergency exception?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.expected_back: To prove a handheld phone was used legally in an emergency, a driver may have to provide testimony or written statements from the authorities, or phone records.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.front: What fine tiers — plus third-offense points and possible suspension — hit repeat handheld phone convictions within ten years?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.expected_back: Handheld phone fines are two hundred dollars to four hundred dollars for a first offense, four hundred dollars to six hundred dollars for a second within ten years, and six hundred dollars to eight hundred dollars for a third or later offense, which also brings three points and possibly a ninety-day suspension.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.front: Which phones and electronic devices are banned for every New Jersey GDL holder behind the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.expected_back: A GDL holder may not use a handheld or hands-free phone, or any other handheld electronic device, while driving.

sec07-card-sec07-R26.front: When are the only two times a school bus driver may use a handheld or hands-free phone?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.expected_back: A school bus driver may not use a handheld or hands-free phone while driving the bus, except in an emergency or when parked in a safe place off the highway.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.front: How does Kulesh's, Kuberts' and Bolis' Law treat illegal cell phone use in serious or fatal crashes?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.expected_back: Kulesh's, Kuberts' and Bolis' Law, enacted in two thousand twelve, treats illegal cell phone use while driving as recklessness under the vehicular homicide and assault by auto statutes.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.front: What fine cap and license consequence can hit drivers who toss trash or dangerous objects onto a New Jersey roadway?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.expected_back: Throwing trash from a moving or parked vehicle is illegal, throwing dangerous objects onto a roadway can bring fines of up to one thousand dollars, and littering from a moving vehicle can cost the driver the license.

sec07-card-sec07-R27.front: How must any trash, debris, or rubbish hauled in a vehicle be prepared before driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R27.expected_back: Any trash, debris or rubbish carried in a vehicle must be covered so it cannot litter the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: Roughly what percentage of a driver's decisions depend on vision, and what happens to that sight after dark?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Roughly ninety percent of the decisions a driver makes depend on what they can see, and that vision shrinks after dark.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: How should you match your nighttime speed to the forward reach of your headlights?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: At night, slow down and stay within the reach of your headlights so the vehicle can always stop inside the distance you can actually see.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: What beam setting and reaction time does the manual's night stopping table assume — and how many feet per second do you cover at sixty miles per hour?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: The manual's night stopping table assumes low beams and a nighttime reaction time of one point five seconds, and notes that a vehicle covers eighty-eight feet each second at sixty miles per hour

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: On low beams at twenty miles per hour, what reaction, braking, and total stopping distances does the night table list?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: On low beams at twenty miles per hour, the table lists forty-four feet of reaction distance plus thirty-one feet of braking distance, for seventy-five feet of total stopping distance.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: On low beams at forty miles per hour, what reaction, braking, and total stopping distances does the night table list?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: On low beams at forty miles per hour, the table lists eighty-eight feet of reaction distance plus one hundred twenty-three feet of braking distance, for two hundred eleven feet in total.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: On low beams at sixty miles per hour, what reaction, braking, and total stopping distances does the night table list?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: On low beams at sixty miles per hour, the table lists one hundred thirty-two feet of reaction distance plus two hundred seventy-seven feet of braking distance, for four hundred nine feet in total.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: On low beams at seventy miles per hour at night, what reaction, braking, and total stopping distances does the table list?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: At seventy miles per hour on low beams at night, the table lists one hundred fifty-four feet of reaction distance plus three hundred seventy-six feet of braking distance, for five hundred thirty feet in total.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: Beyond staying inside headlight reach, what speed, scanning, and space habits keep night driving safe?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Other night rules are to drive more slowly than in daylight, watch for road signs, slow or unlit vehicles, bicycles, pedestrians and animals, and keep wider safety margins.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: At which four low-light times of day — plus what weather visibility threshold — do headlights belong on?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Headlights belong on at dusk, at night, at dawn, on dark days, and any time weather cuts visibility to under five hundred feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: What lighting rule does New Jersey law enforce whenever your windshield wipers are running?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: New Jersey law requires headlights to be on whenever the windshield wipers are running.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: Who holds the right of way in a crosswalk, and does lacking painted lines excuse drivers from stopping?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: In a crosswalk, pedestrians and people using wheelchairs or mobility-assistance vehicles always have the right of way, and drivers must stop for pedestrians whether or not the crosswalk is marked.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: How many seconds ahead of your vehicle should you scan while driving, and what does that time horizon mean?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Scan at least twelve seconds ahead, meaning you should spot objects far enough away that reaching them would take at least twelve seconds.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: At twenty-five miles per hour on a clear city street, how much physical distance does a twelve-second scan cover?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: On a clear city street at twenty-five miles per hour, looking that far ahead works out to seeing about one block in front of you.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: How do you give yourself the extra reaction time needed in heavy city traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: In heavy city traffic you need extra time to react, which means slowing down, since a lower speed buys time.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: What speed, left-right scan, and foot position apply as you near an intersection — and where should your speed be lowest?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: Approaching an intersection, slow down, glance left and then right, and keep your foot on the brake; at the crosswalk itself the vehicle should be at its slowest.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: What does an intersection with zero lights or signs mean — even on a wide, smooth, busy road?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: An intersection with no lights or signs has no traffic control at all, even if the road is wide, smooth or busy, so avoiding a collision there is entirely up to the driver.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: How big a role does speeding play in crashes — and does dry, clear highway weather prevent speed-related wrecks?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Going over the posted limit or too fast for conditions is among the most common factors in crashes, which happen on highways even in good weather on dry pavement.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: Why can wide-open highways lull drivers into trouble, and what three habits counter that danger?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: Wide-open highways can tempt drivers to relax, but some have no signals at crossroads, so drivers must stay alert, drive defensively and keep within the speed limit.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: Which road features do warning signs announce, and why must you slow down before reaching them rather than braking hard on top of them?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Warning signs mark hazards such as hills, dips, narrow bridges, bumps and railroad tracks; slow down there, because speeding and then braking hard can cause a skid or a spin.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: How should you respond when deer or livestock stand in a rural or open road, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: In farm country or open land where livestock or deer may cross, slow down for an animal in the road until it has passed, since animals move unpredictably.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: What happens to fines for motor vehicle violations committed inside a New Jersey roadway construction zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: In New Jersey, fines for motor vehicle violations double when they are committed in a roadway construction zone.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: How far ahead can a work zone be announced, and what two warnings alert approaching drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: A work zone is announced as far as one-half mile ahead of the work area, either by an advance warning sign or by a vehicle with flashing lights.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: How does routing traffic by a detour differ from routing traffic by a work-zone diversion?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Drivers may be routed around a work zone by a detour that uses a different road, or by a diversion such as a lane shift or a crossover through the median.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: Which five attention, obedience, lighting, following, and speed rules form New Jersey's work-zone basics?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Work zone basics are to stay fully attentive, obey signs and flaggers, turn on headlights so workers can see you, avoid tailgating and keep to the posted speed limit.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: Which cabin distractions — even legal ones — should you skip in a work zone, and what attitude keeps crews safe?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: Through a work zone, avoid distractions such as changing radio stations or hands-free calls, watch for workers and equipment, and be patient with the crews.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: Which two roadside markers signal that a work zone is over and normal driving may resume?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: An End Road Work sign, or the last temporary traffic control device, marks where normal driving can resume after a work zone.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: Roughly how many fatal crashes and serious-injury crashes strike U.S. work zones each year?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: Across the nation each year, work zones see nearly eight hundred fatal crashes and over thirty-seven thousand serious injury crashes.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: Which transmission gear position is the only one that lets an ignition release the key?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: An ignition system lets you remove the key only when the transmission is in Park.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: What happens if you twist a steering-column ignition to the lock position while the vehicle is still moving?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Never turn a steering-wheel ignition to the lock position while the vehicle is moving, because the steering locks as the vehicle turns and you lose control.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: What abrupt inputs usually trigger skids, and does recovery differ between front-wheel-drive and rear-wheel-drive cars?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Skids usually come from sudden turns, lane changes or hard braking, often on wet or icy roads, and are handled the same way in front-wheel and rear-wheel drive vehicles.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: When the rear of your car slides sideways, what do you do with the gas pedal, steering wheel, and your eyes?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: If the rear of the vehicle slides, lift your foot off the gas and steer in the direction the rear is skidding without oversteering, while looking where you want to go.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: What happens if you yank the wheel sharply away from a skid — and what must you avoid doing with the brakes in a side skid?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: Turning the wheel sharply away from the direction of a skid can make the vehicle spin, and during a side skid you should not use the brakes.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.front: Once you feel your skidding tires bite and bring the vehicle back under control, what steering step finishes recovery?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.expected_back: Once you feel the vehicle is back under control after a skid, straighten the wheels.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: For a highway emergency stop, how does your speed when leaving the travel lane differ between a paved shoulder and an unpaved shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: For an emergency stop on a highway with a paved shoulder, signal and move onto the shoulder at or near traffic speed before slowing; on an unpaved shoulder, slow to a safe speed before leaving the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: After an emergency stop on the shoulder, where do you place your two flares or warning devices — including pace count?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: After stopping on the shoulder, set a flare or warning sign just behind the vehicle and another warning device at least three hundred feet back, about one hundred twenty paces.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.front: Once stopped on a shoulder, what lighting, standing-position, hood, and white-cloth distress steps apply?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.expected_back: Once pulled onto the shoulder, turn on parking or emergency lights, never stand where you block the taillights at night, raise the hood, and tie a white cloth to the antenna or left door handle if you need help.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: If your right wheels accidentally drop onto the highway shoulder, what speed and steering-turn fraction bring you safely back onto pavement?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: If the wheels drift onto the shoulder, do not jerk back onto the pavement; stay on the shoulder, ease off the gas, and once at twenty-five miles per hour or less turn the wheel one-quarter turn toward the road.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.front: What is the three-step summary for recovering safely after running off the pavement edge?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.expected_back: The short version for running off the pavement is to slow down, regain control and then turn slowly back onto the road.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: Contrast your highway speed when intentionally pulling onto a paved shoulder versus accidentally drifting off the pavement?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: Leaving the road onto a paved shoulder is done at or near traffic speed before slowing, but drifting off the pavement by accident calls for slowing to twenty-five miles per hour or less before steering back.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: What sparks most vehicle fires, and what three rules govern your response if your car catches fire?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: Most car fires start with an electrical short circuit; get everyone out and away at once, call for help, and never try to fight the fire yourself.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: Roughly how long does a car with closed windows and doors float on water, and what is your best escape route?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: A vehicle with its windows and doors shut floats for about three to ten minutes, and the best escape is through an open window while it is still on the surface.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: Compare the manual's three-to-ten-minute float window with the time window it says is plenty to escape?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: A car floating with its windows and doors closed stays up for about three to ten minutes, while the manual separately says three to five minutes is plenty of time to get out in an emergency.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.front: Why does wearing a seat belt improve survival if your vehicle plunges into water?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.expected_back: Wearing a seat belt improves your odds of surviving the impact with water and is the best protection against being knocked unconscious.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.front: Why must you hit power-window switches immediately upon entering water — and what does breaking side or rear glass take?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.expected_back: Try power windows immediately because they may short out, and side or rear glass can only be broken with a heavy, hard object.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.front: Which end of a front-engine car sinks first, when will a submerged door finally open, and how do you find the surface?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.expected_back: A front-engine vehicle sinks nose first, a door opens more easily once pressure inside and outside equalizes, and once outside you should follow the air bubbles to the surface.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: If your car stalls on railroad tracks with zero train in sight, must passengers still evacuate — and whom do you call?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: If the vehicle stalls on railroad tracks, everyone must get out and move far from the vehicle and tracks even when no train is coming, then call the number on the Emergency Notification sign or nine one one.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: When a train bears down on your stalled vehicle, at what angle and in which direction should you run?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: If a train is approaching, run away from the vehicle and tracks at a forty-five-degree angle toward the direction the train is coming from, to avoid flying debris.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: If conventional disc and drum brakes fail on the road, what two immediate steps try to slow the car and rebuild pressure?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: If conventional disc and drum brakes fail, downshift and then pump the pedal hard and quickly several times to try to build pressure.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: If pumping failed brakes builds zero pressure, how must you apply the parking brake — and why hold its release?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: If pumping fails, use the parking brake while holding its release so you can let up if the rear wheels lock and the vehicle starts to skid.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: When a tire suddenly goes flat or blows out at speed, what steering, gas, and brake discipline brings you to a safe stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: With a flat or blowout, grip the wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, take your foot off the gas without braking, and coast to a stop in a safe spot.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: Contrast what your right foot does during conventional brake failure versus a tire blowout?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: When conventional brakes fail you pump the pedal, but during a tire blowout you take your foot off the gas and do not brake at all.

sec09-card-sec09-R22.front: What happens to power steering if your engine dies while moving, and how do you get off the road?
sec09-card-sec09-R22.expected_back: When the engine dies, power steering fails, so grip the wheel firmly and use extra force to steer the vehicle to a safe stop off the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: If your accelerator sticks down, what four-step sequence brings the car safely to a stop before shutting off the engine?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: If the gas pedal sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift quickly to neutral, steer to a safe spot off the road, and turn off the engine.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: If your hood latches fail and the hood flies up against the windshield, where can you look to guide off the road?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: If the hood flies up, slow down at once, look under the hood or out the side window, and use the center line or lane markings to guide the vehicle off the road.

sec09-card-sec09-R23.front: What steps should you follow if your headlights abruptly go dark at night?
sec09-card-sec09-R23.expected_back: If headlights suddenly go dark, stop safely off the road, try the headlight or dimmer switch, and if that fails switch on parking lights, flashers or turn signals and call for help.

sec09-card-sec09-R24.front: What three actions apply if your windshield wipers quit working during rain or snow?
sec09-card-sec09-R24.expected_back: If the wipers quit during rain or snow, slow down, pull to a safe spot off the road and turn on the emergency flashers.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: When a sudden collision threatens ahead or beside you, what are your three evasive choices?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: When a collision threatens, the three choices are to stop, to turn or to speed up.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: During an emergency stop to dodge a crash, how do you brake with ABS versus conventional non-ABS brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: With antilock brakes, press as hard as needed and keep steering without pumping; with conventional brakes, pump them to keep steering control, since holding them down hard locks the wheels.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: Why do you hold firm pedal pressure with ABS yet pump conventional brakes when steering around a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: To avoid a crash with ABS you hold firm pressure without pumping, whereas with conventional brakes you pump to keep steering.

sec09-card-sec09-R25.front: While swerving to dodge a collision — or steering onto a soft shoulder — what brake mistake must you avoid?
sec09-card-sec09-R25.expected_back: When turning away from a crash, avoid braking while you turn to lessen the chance of a skid, and do not brake hard when turning onto a soft shoulder.

sec09-card-sec09-R26.front: In which two impact-angle scenarios with open road ahead is flooring the gas the right crash-avoidance move?
sec09-card-sec09-R26.expected_back: Speeding up is the right choice when you are about to be struck from the side or behind and there is open room ahead, so press the gas fully, then slow once clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.front: If an impact cannot be avoided completely, which direction should you steer and what kind of roadside object should you pick?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.expected_back: If a crash looks likely, steer away from oncoming traffic even if that means leaving the road, and choose to hit something that gives way, such as shrubs, rather than something hard.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.front: Rank the three impact targets from least severe to worst when a collision is unavoidable — and what impact angle helps?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.expected_back: When something must be hit, prefer an object moving your way over a stationary one, and a stationary one over one coming head-on, aiming for a glancing blow.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.front: Seconds before a head-on crash while wearing a shoulder belt in an airbag-equipped car, how should you protect yourself?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.expected_back: If you are about to be hit head-on while wearing a shoulder strap in a car with airbags, protect your face with your arms and hands.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: Contrast your last-second head-on crash defense with a shoulder strap and airbags versus having neither?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: In a head-on threat with a shoulder strap and airbags you shield your face, but without a strap or airbags you throw yourself across the seat to avoid the wheel and windshield.

sec09-card-sec09-R27.front: When you spot an unavoidable rear-end hit coming in your mirror, what three brake, body, and headrest actions protect you?
sec09-card-sec09-R27.expected_back: If a rear-end crash is coming, be ready to brake so you are not shoved into the car ahead, brace between the wheel and seat back and press your head against the headrest.

sec09-card-sec09-R28.front: What steering grip and recovery readiness help if another vehicle is about to strike you from the side?
sec09-card-sec09-R28.expected_back: If you are about to be hit from the side, keep a tight grip on the wheel and be ready to turn quickly to regain control if the vehicle spins.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.front: Which crashes must New Jersey drivers report to police — and what strict rule governs fatalities at the scene?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.expected_back: New Jersey requires drivers to notify police of any crash involving injury, death, or vehicle or property damage, and a body must not be moved until police or an ambulance arrive.

sec09-card-sec09-R29.front: What two duties apply if you scrape or hit an unattended parked vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-R29.expected_back: After hitting a parked vehicle, you must notify the police and should also try to find the owner.

sec09-card-sec09-R30.front: Whether involved in or witnessing a crash, what five roadside steps help secure the scene?
sec09-card-sec09-R30.expected_back: At any crash you witness or are part of, stop, stay calm, get help from police and an ambulance, wait at the scene without blocking traffic and warn oncoming drivers.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.front: What dollar-damage threshold or injury triggers a ten-day written MVC crash report, what excuses filing it, and whom do you call immediately?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.expected_back: When property damage exceeds five hundred dollars or someone is injured, send a written report to the MVC within ten days unless the police file one, and notify your insurer at once.

sec09-card-sec09-R31.front: Why doesn't a driver need to mail a separate written MVC report after police investigate — and what medical advice applies if shaken up?
sec09-card-sec09-R31.expected_back: No written MVC crash report is needed when the police file one, and you can get a copy of their report; if shaken up, see a doctor promptly.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: How does New Jersey classify driving, and what can follow serious violations alongside fines and jail?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Driving is a privilege rather than a right, and state law allows or requires suspension for certain violations, on top of possible fines and imprisonment.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: Which unpaid tickets, coverage gaps, health issues, crash faults, or ignored notices can cost your driving privilege?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Grounds for losing the privilege include unanswered or unpaid parking tickets, driving while suspended, no proof of insurance, physical or mental disqualification, drug or alcohol use, traffic violations, fault in a fatal crash and ignoring an MVC notice.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: Are all New Jersey license suspensions automatic, or who decides discretionary ones?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Some suspensions are not mandatory and are decided case by case by the MVC Chief Administrator or the courts.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: What check may the MVC Chief Administrator order before deciding whether to suspend a problem driver?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: The MVC Chief Administrator may order a re-examination of a problem driver to help decide whether to suspend driving privileges.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: How many license suspensions over what timeframe label a New Jersey driver a habitual offender?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: A habitual offender is a driver whose license has been suspended three times within three years.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.front: Falling how far behind on child support or court-ordered health coverage can suspend which licenses?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.expected_back: Owing six months or more of child support or court-ordered health coverage can lead to a court-ordered suspension of both driver and professional licenses.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: What is New Jersey's minimum age to buy, possess, or drink alcohol, and what about adult suppliers?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: In New Jersey a person must be at least twenty-one to buy, possess or drink alcohol, and adults who supply alcohol to underage people also face serious consequences.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: What fine and license hit can strike someone under twenty-one caught buying or drinking at a licensed venue?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: A person under twenty-one who buys or drinks alcohol where alcohol is licensed for sale may be fined five hundred dollars and lose their license for a time.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: When does an underage alcohol suspension start if the teen isn't licensed yet, and what class may apply?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: If the underage person has no license yet, the suspension begins on the date they first become eligible for one, and an alcohol education or treatment program may be required.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: How long is the suspension for a first underage offense with BAC from point zero one to under point zero eight?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: For an underage first offense with a BAC from zero point zero one up to under zero point zero eight percent, the license is suspended thirty to ninety days, starting on the later of eligibility or conviction.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: Alongside suspension, what community service and coursework hit a first underage BAC offense?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: An underage first offense also brings fifteen to thirty days of community service and either an IDRC or an alcohol education and highway safety program.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: What fine, IDRC hours, and jail ceiling apply to a first adult DUI from point zero eight to under point one zero?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: For a first DUI with a BAC of zero point zero eight percent but under zero point one zero percent, the fine is two hundred fifty dollars to four hundred dollars, with twelve to forty-eight hours at an IDRC and up to thirty days in jail.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: What court-fine bracket applies to a first DUI when BAC reaches point one zero percent or higher?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: For a first DUI with a BAC of zero point one zero percent or higher, the fine rises to three hundred dollars to five hundred dollars.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: How do court fines shift when a first-offense BAC climbs from under point one zero to point one zero or above?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: A first DUI between zero point zero eight and under zero point one zero percent is fined two hundred fifty dollars to four hundred dollars, while a first DUI at zero point one zero percent or more is fined three hundred dollars to five hundred dollars.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: What annual violation surcharge—and for how many years—hits a first DUI conviction?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: A first DUI offense also carries an annual surcharge of one thousand dollars for three years.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: What fees does the IDRC charge for its twelve-hour program versus its forty-eight-hour program?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: The IDRC charges two hundred sixty-four dollars when the program lasts twelve hours and three hundred twenty-one dollars when it lasts forty-eight hours.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: Who must report to an Intoxicated Driver Resource Center, and what two steps happen there?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: Anyone charged with an alcohol-related traffic offense must be detained at an IDRC, where offenders take an alcohol and highway safety education program and are evaluated for treatment needs.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: How are first-, second-, and third-time alcohol offenders split between county and regional IDRCs?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: Each of New Jersey's twenty-one counties has an IDRC for first- and third-time offenders, while second-time offenders go to one of three regional IDRCs.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: Which repeat-offender group goes to a regional IDRC rather than their home county's IDRC?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: First- and third-time alcohol offenders are detained at their county IDRC, whereas second-time offenders go to one of the three regional centers.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: How long is the minimum referral treatment program after IDRC screening, and how does it tie to relicensing?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: Offenders found to need treatment are referred for a program of at least sixteen weeks, and satisfactory participation is a condition for getting licensed again.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: What action on New Jersey roads triggers implied consent to a post-arrest breath test?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Under New Jersey's implied consent law, simply driving on New Jersey roads means agreeing to a breath test by police or hospital staff after an arrest for intoxicated driving.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: Where are you taken if you refuse a breath test, and what may medical staff do there?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: A driver who refuses the breath test is detained and taken to a hospital, where staff may draw blood.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: How much is the yearly violation surcharge—and for how many years—after refusing a breath test?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Refusing a breath test carries a violation surcharge of one thousand dollars a year for three years.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: On a refusal conviction tied to a first offense, what must happen before driving privileges return?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: A refusal conviction tied to a first offense means losing driving privileges until an ignition interlock device is installed.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Above what BAC reading does an ignition interlock breathalyzer block the engine from starting?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: An ignition interlock device has a built-in breathalyzer that stops the vehicle from starting when the driver's BAC is above zero point zero five percent.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How does an ignition interlock's engine-lockout BAC compare with New Jersey's adult DUI limit?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: The adult DUI limit is a BAC of zero point zero eight percent, but an installed interlock blocks the engine once BAC tops just zero point zero five percent.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: How long must an ignition interlock remain installed after a first DUI from point zero eight to under point one zero?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: After a first DUI with a BAC of zero point zero eight to under zero point one zero percent, the interlock stays installed for three months from restoration of driving privileges.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: How long is an interlock required after restoration on a first DUI from point one zero to under point one five?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: After a first DUI with a BAC of zero point one zero to under zero point one five percent, the interlock is required for seven months to one year after restoration.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: When and for how long is an interlock mandatory on a first DUI at point one five BAC or higher?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: After a first DUI at zero point one five percent or higher, the interlock is required during the suspension and for twelve to fifteen months after restoration.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: How does post-restoration interlock time for a breath-test refusal compare with a point-one-five-plus first DUI?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: For a breath-test refusal, the interlock runs for nine to fifteen months after restoration, compared with twelve to fifteen months after a first DUI at zero point one five percent or higher.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: How long must an interlock stay installed after a second or later DUI or refusal conviction?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: After a second or later DUI or refusal offense, the interlock is required during the suspension and for two to four years after restoration.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: Under the February 2024 update for qualifying alcohol arrests, why install an interlock voluntarily before conviction?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: For offenses on or after February nineteen, two thousand twenty-four, a person arrested for certain alcohol offenses may install an interlock voluntarily before conviction, which may reduce fines and the suspension period.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.front: What added penalty applies if you drive after skipping a court-ordered ignition interlock installation?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.expected_back: Driving after failing to install a court-ordered interlock adds a one-year suspension on top of any existing suspension.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.front: How do fines and jail escalate across first, second, and third offenses for driving while suspended?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.expected_back: Driving while suspended costs five hundred dollars plus up to six more months of suspension the first time, seven hundred fifty dollars and up to five days in jail the second time, and one thousand dollars with a ten-day jail term the third time.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.front: What fine, added suspension, and jail range hit driving while suspended for DUI, refusal, or habitual offending?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.expected_back: Driving while suspended for a DUI, a refusal or as a habitual offender brings a five hundred dollars fine and one to two more years of suspension, with possible jail of ten to ninety days.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.front: How does jail time jump on a first offense if that DUI- or habitual-suspended driver enters within a thousand feet of a school?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.expected_back: If that same suspended driver drives on school property, through a school crossing zone, or anywhere within one thousand feet of a school, the penalty is one to two years of suspension, a five hundred dollars fine and sixty to ninety days in jail for a first offense.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.front: When does driving while suspended cross into an indictable fourth-degree crime?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.expected_back: Driving while suspended for a second or later DUI or refusal conviction is a fourth-degree crime.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.front: What happens to a vehicle owner who knowingly hands keys to someone suspended for DUI or refusal?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.expected_back: An owner who knowingly lets someone drive whose license is suspended for DUI or refusal faces up to six months of license and registration suspension and a one thousand dollars fine, up to fifteen days in jail, or both.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: How do base fines climb across first, second, and third unsafe-driving convictions—plus what court surcharge hits each?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: An unsafe driving conviction is fined fifty dollars to one hundred fifty dollars the first time, one hundred dollars to two hundred fifty dollars the second, and two hundred dollars to five hundred dollars for a third or later offense, plus a two hundred fifty dollars court surcharge each time.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: When does New Jersey's 'no-point' unsafe-driving offense suddenly post four penalty points?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: A third or later unsafe driving offense within five years of the previous one also adds four motor vehicle penalty points.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: What jail maximum, fine range, and record hit can a first reckless-driving conviction bring?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: A first reckless driving offense can bring up to sixty days in jail, a fine of fifty dollars to two hundred dollars, or both, and points are also assessed.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: By how much over a sixty-five-mile-per-hour limit does speeding trigger doubled fines?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: In a sixty-five miles per hour zone, speeding ten miles per hour or more over the limit, or certain other moving violations, means doubled fines.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Which two New Jersey highway settings double moving-violation fines?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Fines double for moving violations in highway construction zones, and they also double in a sixty-five miles per hour zone for speeding ten miles per hour or more over the limit or certain other violations.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: How do fines and points differ when carelessly passing a vulnerable road user causes injury versus no injury?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: Failing to pass a vulnerable road user with due caution is fined five hundred dollars with two penalty points if someone is injured, but one hundred dollars with no points if no one is hurt.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: What fine hits a driver who refuses an officer's request to illuminate the driver's compartment at a stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: A driver who ignores a police officer's request to light up the driver's compartment during a stop faces a fifty dollars fine.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: What penalties apply for keeping an open alcohol container or unsealed cannabis item in the passenger cabin?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: Carrying an open or unsealed alcohol container, or an unsealed cannabis item, in the passenger area is fined two hundred dollars the first time and two hundred fifty dollars or ten days of community service after that.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: What fine applies just for driving without clearing snow or ice off your car—even if nothing falls?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: Failing to clear snow or ice from a vehicle before driving carries a twenty-five dollars to seventy-five dollars fine even if none of it comes loose.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: How high do fines climb for private drivers versus commercial rigs when dislodged ice causes harm or damage?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: If ice flies off a private vehicle and causes death, injury or property damage, the driver faces a fine of two hundred dollars to one thousand dollars each time, and commercial owners and operators face five hundred dollars to one thousand five hundred dollars.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: Leaving a car unauthorized along a limited-access highway for four-plus hours risks what first-time fine and suspension?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Leaving a vehicle on or along a limited-access highway for four hours or more without permission brings a fine of one hundred dollars to five hundred dollars and possible loss of driving privileges for up to two years.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: How high do fines and suspension climb on a repeat highway vehicle-abandonment offense?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Repeat vehicle abandonment raises the fine to five hundred dollars to one thousand dollars with a suspension of up to five years.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: What fine, jail time, and first-versus-repeat license loss hit an injury or fatal hit-and-run?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: A hit-and-run involving injury or death can bring a fine of two thousand five hundred dollars to five thousand dollars, one hundred eighty days in jail, or both, plus a one-year license loss for a first offense and permanent loss for a later one.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: Up to what fine, prison term, and mandatory license loss punish auto-insurance fraud?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: Insurance application or claim fraud can be punished by fines up to five thousand dollars, up to three years in prison, or both, and an auto insurance crime conviction also costs the license for one year.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: What fine, jail maximum, and privilege loss punish lying on a license or registration form?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: Lying on a license or registration application brings a two hundred dollars to five hundred dollars fine, up to six months in jail, or both, and loss of license or registration privileges for six months to two years.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.front: What fine and jail sentence apply to taking someone else's license exam—or hiring a stand-in?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.expected_back: Having someone else take your license test, or taking it for someone else, brings a two hundred dollars to five hundred dollars fine, thirty to ninety days in jail, or both.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.front: Which privileges and first-time fine hit someone convicted of boating DUI on New Jersey waters?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.expected_back: A boater convicted of DUI on New Jersey waters loses boating and all driving privileges, and a first offense is fined two hundred fifty dollars to five hundred dollars.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: When did New Jersey launch GDL, how does it build safer drivers, and what age unlocks an unrestricted license?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: New Jersey began its Graduated Driver License (GDL) Program in two thousand one; it phases in privileges for first-time drivers, extends practice time and sets eighteen as the minimum age for an unrestricted basic license.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: What permit, minimum age, signature, and course enrollment kick off GDL Option A, the early bird road?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: GDL Option A, the early bird road, begins with a special learner permit at age sixteen or older, signed parent or guardian consent, and enrollment in an approved behind-the-wheel training course.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: What form and three proof categories must a teen supply before the instructor can buy a special learner permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: The instructor can purchase the special learner permit once the applicant has filled out the form and supplied six points of ID, proof of home address and proof of Social Security number.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: Who purchases the special learner permit, and how long does that permit remain valid?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: The instructor buys the special learner permit, and it stays valid for two years.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: Once an instructor purchases a special learner permit, how long does the permit itself stay good?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: The special learner permit itself is valid for two years once the instructor buys it.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: On Option A, which two MVC screenings must you pass, and when does the MVC validate the permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: On Option A an approved instructor buys the permit, the applicant must pass the knowledge and vision tests, and the MVC validates the permit only once the training course is complete.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: What makes up an approved special-permit driving course, and what MVC trip time cannot count toward it?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: The approved course behind a special learner permit is six full hours of behind-the-wheel teaching in a car with dual controls, and time spent at the MVC buying the permit or testing does not count.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: After completing six-hour training, which specific MVC facility must validate a special learner permit before practice starts?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: After finishing the training course and before practicing, the special learner permit holder must get the permit validated at a Licensing Center that has a Driver Testing Center.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: When is a permit holder legally allowed to start practice driving on New Jersey roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: A permit may not be used for practice driving until an MVC Driver Testing Center has validated it.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: On Option A, who must buy the Special Learner Permit and what milestone unlocks MVC validation?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: On Option A, the early bird road, an approved instructor must purchase the Special Learner Permit and the MVC validates it only after behind-the-wheel training completion.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: What minimum months, total hours, night hours, and plate markers apply to Option A supervised practice?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Option A supervised practice lasts at least six months and must total at least fifty driving hours, ten of them in darkness, with red GDL decals on the vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Who completes the Certification of Supervised Driving form, and when do you turn it in?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: A parent, guardian or supervising driver fills out a Certification of Supervised Driving form, and the applicant hands it in at the time of licensing.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: Which three requirements unlock an Option A probationary license?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: The Option A probationary license requires six months of supervised driving without suspensions or postponements, a passed MVC road test, and an age of at least seventeen.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: After earning an Option A probationary license, what solo milestone and minimum age unlock the basic license?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Option A then requires at least one year of unsupervised driving under probationary restrictions, and the basic license comes at age eighteen or older.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: What happens if you finish twelve probationary months without visiting a Licensing Center to upgrade?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: After the standard twelve-month probationary period, the driver must visit a Licensing Center to upgrade to a basic license, or the probationary restrictions keep applying and can be enforced by police.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: How does GDL Option B—the young adult road—begin, and who still needs parent or guardian consent?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: GDL Option B, the young adult road, begins with an examination permit at age seventeen or older after passing the knowledge and vision tests, with parent or guardian consent if under eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: Who qualifies for an examination permit, and which two school or instructor ties are NOT required?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: A New Jersey resident aged seventeen or older who is not suspended can get an examination permit, which needs neither student status nor an instructor.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: How does a special learner permit differ from an examination permit regarding school and instructors?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: A special learner permit is tied to a student in a training course with an instructor, while an examination permit needs neither student status nor an instructor.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: How much supervised driving must an Option B applicant complete before taking the road evaluation?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: Option B also requires at least six months of supervised practice with at least fifty hours, ten of them after dark, followed by a passed road test.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: What final stage and minimum age complete Option B for a basic license?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: Option B ends with the basic license at age eighteen or older after one year of unsupervised driving under probationary restrictions.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: At what age does GDL Option C—the adult road—begin, and what comes first?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: GDL Option C, the adult road, begins with an examination permit at age twenty-one or older after passing the knowledge and vision tests.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: How long are the supervised and unsupervised phases on Option C before earning a basic license?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: Option C requires at least three months of supervised practice with no suspensions or postponements before the road test, then one year of unsupervised driving before the basic license.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: What supervised duration appears on the Option C adult chart, and what teen requirement is left off?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: Option C, the adult road for ages twenty-one and up, lists only three months of supervised practice on its chart, with no practice-hour minimum.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: How long do passed knowledge and vision screening results remain valid?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: Knowledge test and vision screening results are good for two years.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: Along with the special learner permit, what two MVC screening results also stay valid for two years?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: Knowledge test and vision screening results also remain valid for two years.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: Between which exact late-night and early-morning hours are GDL permit and probationary drivers barred from driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: Special learner permit, examination permit and probationary license holders may not drive between eleven oh one pm and five am.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: When and how may a GDL driver under twenty-one legally drive during overnight curfew hours?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: A permit or probationary driver under twenty-one may drive during the prohibited hours for work or religious reasons only while carrying a signed certification on the employer's or religious institution's official letterhead.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Which GDL rule alone does the work-or-religion waiver lift, and what must stay in the car?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: The work or religion exemption covers only the prohibited driving hours, and the driver must carry the signed letterhead certification while driving then.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: Which cell phones and electronic devices are banned across all three GDL stages while driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: All three GDL stages forbid hand-held and hands-free cell phones and every other electronic device while driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: What seat, minimum age, license state, and years of experience must a permit holder's supervising driver have?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: A permit holder must have a front-seat supervising driver who is at least twenty-one, holds a valid New Jersey license and has at least three years of driving experience.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: Who takes legal responsibility if a student driver commits a traffic violation during supervised practice?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: If a student driver commits a traffic offense, both the student and the instructor or adult supervising driver are held responsible.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: What fine or license consequence can hit a motorist who violates GDL restrictions?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Ignoring GDL restrictions can lead to a one hundred dollars fine or a suspension of the motorist's driving privilege.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: Who is allowed to ride as a passenger with a special learner permit driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: A special learner permit holder may carry any parent, guardian or dependent plus one additional passenger.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: How many passengers may an examination permit or probationary driver carry, and what lifts that cap?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: Examination permit and probationary license holders may carry their dependents plus one other person, unless a parent or guardian is riding along.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: How does the passenger wording for a special learner permit differ from an examination permit?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: Passenger limits differ by permit: a special learner permit allows any parent, guardian or dependent plus one more passenger, while an examination permit allows dependents plus one more unless a parent or guardian rides along.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: Who must buckle up inside a GDL driver's vehicle, and what must show outside?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: The GDL driver and every passenger must wear seat belts, and the decals must be displayed on the license plates.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: On which exact corner of which plates do GDL drivers under twenty-one stick their red decals?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: GDL drivers under twenty-one put one red reflective decal on the top left corner of the rear license plate and one on the top left corner of the front plate.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: How do GDL drivers get their removable decals, and how much does a pair or extra pair cost?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: Two removable decals come with the permit for a four dollars fee, and extra pairs cost four dollars at any MVC Licensing Center.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: Which three GDL restrictions drop away for examination permit or probationary drivers aged twenty-one or older?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: When an examination permit or probationary license holder is twenty-one or older, the hour, passenger and decal restrictions no longer apply.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: Which three limits does the age-twenty-one footnote lift, and which two GDL rules does it NOT lift?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: For examination permit and probationary license holders aged twenty-one or older, the footnote lifts only the hour, passenger and decal restrictions; it does not mention the phone ban or the seat belt rule.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: Does a newcomer holding a valid out-of-state driver license still need a New Jersey examination permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: A driver examination permit is required even if the motorist already holds a valid license from another state.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: How soon after becoming a permanent New Jersey resident must an out-of-state driver buy an examination permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: Drivers arriving from another state must purchase a New Jersey examination permit within sixty days after becoming permanent residents, or when the old license expires if that happens first.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: What happens when an out-of-state licensed driver younger than eighteen moves to New Jersey?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: Out-of-state drivers under eighteen who move to New Jersey fall under the GDL Program.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: Which screening must out-of-state transfers always pass, and what waives their knowledge and road checks?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: Out-of-state applicants must pass a vision screening, but the knowledge and road tests are waived with a valid non-probationary license or certified driver abstract from any state, the District of Columbia or a US territory.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.front: What extra document should foreign-licensed visitors carry, and where must non-citizens obtain an IDP?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.expected_back: Visitors with a foreign license should carry an International Driving Permit (IDP) or an acceptable English translation, and non-citizens must get the IDP in their own country before traveling.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.front: What helpful role does an International Driving Permit serve, and what can it never replace?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.expected_back: An IDP is an official document but can never replace a driver license; it only adds identification and helps across language barriers.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Why must a visiting foreign driver carry their valid home license alongside an International Driving Permit?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: An International Driving Permit adds identification and translation, but a valid driver license must still be carried because the permit cannot replace it.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.front: Who can apply for a New Jersey non-driver ID card, and when must that card be surrendered?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.expected_back: Anyone aged fourteen or older without a valid driver license may apply for a non-driver ID card, which must be given up when the person receives a New Jersey driver license.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.front: How do you have the words organ donor printed onto your New Jersey license?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.expected_back: Answering yes to organ donation at an MVC Licensing Center puts the words organ donor on your license.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: At which two milestone ages and transactions does the MVC ask about the Donate Life Registry?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: At age fourteen a non-driver ID applicant is asked about the Donate Life Registry, and the question comes again at eighteen when applying for an unrestricted license or renewing.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: What is the minimum donor registration age, what does donation cost the family, and how are funerals affected?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: Anyone fourteen or older can register as an organ and tissue donor; the family pays nothing, funeral arrangements are not affected, and organs are shared through a national list.

sec02-card-sec02-F41.front: Who can use New Jersey's Next-of-Kin Registry under Sara's Law, and when may police access those contacts?
sec02-card-sec02-F41.expected_back: The Next-of-Kin Registry (Sara's Law) lets people aged fourteen or older store emergency contacts with the MVC, used only by police to reach them after a crash leaves the person unable to communicate.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.front: Which MVC cardholders qualify for the Next-of-Kin Registry, and what two ways can contacts be submitted?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.expected_back: The Next-of-Kin Registry is open to holders of any MVC-issued license, permit or non-driver ID, including a boat license, and contacts can be registered online or by a mailed form.

sec02-card-sec02-F42.front: Under the National Voter Registration Act, during which three MVC transactions must staff offer voter registration?
sec02-card-sec02-F42.expected_back: Under the National Voter Registration Act, motor vehicle offices must offer voter registration to anyone applying for or renewing a license or ID, or changing an address.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.front: What decibel threshold, card mark, and medical sign-off apply to a hearing-impaired driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.expected_back: A hearing-impaired driver license, for a loss of forty-one decibels or more, is marked with a numerical code and needs verification by a physician or audiologist.

sec02-card-sec02-R14.front: What are the three commercial license classes, and what license must you already hold to apply?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.expected_back: There are three commercial license classes, A, B and C, and none can be applied for without a valid basic Class D New Jersey license or a valid out-of-state CDL.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.front: Which combined and towed weight ratings demand a Class A CDL, and which lower classes can it cover?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.expected_back: A Class A license is needed for a tractor trailer or other combination rated at twenty-six thousand one pounds or more when the towed vehicle is rated above ten thousand pounds, and it also covers Classes B, C and D with the proper endorsements.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.front: Which vehicle weights, trailer limits, and passenger counts fall under a Class B CDL?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.expected_back: A Class B license covers any vehicle rated at twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, including one towing a trailer rated at ten thousand pounds or less, and buses that size built for sixteen or more passengers counting the driver.

sec02-card-sec02-R17.front: Which three hazmat or passenger categories under 26,001 pounds require a Class C CDL?
sec02-card-sec02-R17.expected_back: A Class C license covers lighter vehicles placarded for hazardous material, buses under twenty-six thousand one pounds built for sixteen or more passengers, and vehicles carrying eight to fifteen passengers for hire.

sec02-card-sec02-R18.front: Which five groups—including taxis, emergency rigs, farms within 150 miles, funerals, and RVs—do NOT need a CDL?
sec02-card-sec02-R18.expected_back: Taxi drivers, funeral procession drivers, rescue and firefighting apparatus operators, farmers hauling within one hundred fifty miles of their farms, and personal-use RV drivers do not need a CDL.

sec02-card-sec02-R19.front: What three requirements earn the P passenger endorsement, and which two letters must school-bus drivers hold?
sec02-card-sec02-R19.expected_back: The passenger endorsement P requires a road test, age twenty-one and three years of driving experience, and a school bus driver needs both the S and the P endorsements.

sec02-card-sec02-R20.front: How do the requirements for the H hazmat endorsement compare with the N tanker endorsement?
sec02-card-sec02-R20.expected_back: The hazardous materials endorsement H requires a knowledge test, age twenty-one, and training with retesting every two years, while the tanker endorsement N requires a knowledge test.

sec02-card-sec02-R21.front: What does Restriction L bar on a commercial license, and which manual prepares all CDL screenings?
sec02-card-sec02-R21.expected_back: Restriction L on a commercial license means the driver may not operate a vehicle equipped with air brakes, and all CDL tests come from the separate Commercial Driver Manual.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: Under New Jersey law, which occupants of a car, van, pickup, or SUV must buckle a seat belt?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: New Jersey law requires the driver and every passenger of a passenger vehicle, such as a car, van, pickup truck or SUV, to wear a seat belt.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: Which three unbelted occupants give New Jersey police primary authority to pull a vehicle over for that violation alone?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: An unbelted driver, front-seat passenger or child under eighteen is a primary offense, so a police officer may stop the vehicle for that violation alone.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: Under what condition can an unbuckled back-seat passenger aged eighteen or older receive a summons?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Unbuckled back-seat riders aged eighteen or older can receive a summons under a secondary law, but only when the vehicle has been stopped for some other reason.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: What separates New Jersey's primary seat-belt enforcement from its secondary rule for adult rear-seat riders?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: An unbelted driver, front-seat passenger or child under eighteen can be the only reason for a traffic stop, whereas an unbelted back-seat rider aged eighteen or older can be ticketed only after a stop for something else.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: For standard license holders, who answers legally for unbuckled minors under eighteen versus unbuckled front-seat adults?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: The driver is answerable for every passenger under age eighteen, while front-seat passengers aged eighteen or older are answerable for themselves.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: What expanded seat-belt responsibility rests on a driver holding a GDL permit or probationary license?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: A driver holding a GDL permit or probationary license must wear a seat belt and must also make every passenger, in any seat, buckle up.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: How does passenger belt accountability shift when you move from a GDL license to an unrestricted basic license?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: An ordinary driver answers for belting passengers under eighteen, but a GDL permit or probationary license holder must make passengers of every age buckle up.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: Which vintage vehicles, federal categories, or medical cases are exempt from New Jersey's seat-belt mandate?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: The seat belt law exempts passenger vehicles built before July one, nineteen sixty-six, vehicles that federal law does not require to have belts, and people with a physical or medical reason confirmed in writing by a licensed physician.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: What duty applies to a driver transporting a passenger seated in a wheelchair?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: A driver who carries a passenger using a wheelchair must secure that person with a correctly adjusted, fastened wheelchair and occupant securement device.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: By what percentage does wearing a seat belt raise a motorist's odds of surviving a crash?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Wearing a seat belt improves a motorist's chance of surviving a crash by sixty percent.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: How many times better are crash survival odds when wearing both a lap belt and a shoulder strap?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Survival odds in a crash are three to four times better when a motorist wears both a seat belt and a shoulder strap.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: Slamming unrestrained into the dashboard or windshield at thirty miles per hour equals falling from what height?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Hitting the dashboard or windshield at thirty miles per hour is compared with falling from the top of a three-story building.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: Roughly how many seconds does clicking on a seat belt actually take?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: Buckling up takes only about three seconds.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: Which two physical actions allow seat belts to reduce crash injury severity?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Belts slow the body down together with the vehicle and keep occupants from being thrown out in a crash, so injuries are likely to be less severe.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: Where across your torso and pelvis should the lap belt and shoulder strap rest?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: The lap belt should sit under the abdomen and low on the hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the collarbone and breastbone while staying away from the neck.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: May two passengers ever buckle a single seat belt around both bodies together?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: Never fasten one belt around two people.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Why must everyone—including back-seat passengers—wear lap and shoulder belts even inside air-bag-equipped cars?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Because air bags are only supplemental protection, both the lap and shoulder belts should be worn on every trip and in every seat, back seat included.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: Since January one, nineteen eighty-one, what testing and label details must every child restraint carry?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Every child restraint system made since January one, nineteen eighty-one, must be designed to pass demanding safety tests and carries a label giving its manufacture date and its conformity with federal safety standards.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: Which direction must an infant carrier never face, and where do you check its size and weight limits?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: An infant seat must never be turned to face forward, and the seat label shows the child size and weight it is designed to protect.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Beyond buying an approved car seat, what habit gives a child the strongest protection?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Using the car seat on every ride and using it correctly each time, following the seat's own instructions, is the best protection a driver can give a child.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: How must children under age two and weighing under thirty pounds ride under New Jersey's manual?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: The manual says children under age two and those weighing under thirty pounds must ride in a rear-facing child restraint equipped with a five-point harness.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: Where and in what restraint must children under age four weighing under forty pounds ride?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Children under age four who weigh under forty pounds must ride in a rear seat in a five-point-harness restraint, either rear-facing until they outgrow the maker's limits and then forward-facing, or forward-facing.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: What restraint and seating rules apply to children under age eight who stand shorter than fifty-seven inches?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: Children under age eight and shorter than fifty-seven inches (four feet, nine inches) must ride in a rear seat, either in a forward-facing restraint with a five-point harness until they outgrow it and then a booster seat, or in a booster seat.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: Can you line up New Jersey's three progressive child-restraint cutoffs—two, four, and eight?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.memory_hook: Two rear-facing, four harness, eight booster
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: Three child-seat thresholds are easy to mix up: under age two or under thirty pounds means rear-facing, under four and under forty pounds means a harness in a rear seat, and under eight and under fifty-seven inches means a harness or booster in a rear seat.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: When is a child under age eight legally permitted to ride in a front passenger seat?
