sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: All children under age eight must sit in a rear seat, and only a vehicle with no rear seat allows them to ride in an approved restraint or booster seat up front.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: Which children are barred from riding aboard a three-wheeled autocycle in New Jersey?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: An autocycle operator may not carry any child who would have to ride in a child passenger restraint under the child passenger safety law.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: What fine range—before fees and court costs—applies for breaking New Jersey's child passenger safety law?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: Violating the child passenger safety law can bring a fine of fifty dollars to seventy-five dollars, plus fees and court costs.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: What crash role are air bags designed for, and which new vehicles must carry them under federal rules?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: Air bags are meant to add to seat belt protection in frontal crashes, and federal standards require them in all new passenger cars and light trucks.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: Up to how fast do air bags burst open, and when should a belted adult contact the cushion?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: Air bags can inflate at speeds up to two hundred miles per hour, and a correctly belted adult of average size usually reaches the bag only after it is fully inflated.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: Why do air bags pose opposite outcomes for belted adults compared with children sitting up front?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: Air bags have saved many belted adults but could seriously injure or kill children sitting in the front seat.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: Where must a rear-facing infant or toddler restraint never be installed?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: A rear-facing child restraint may never be placed in a front seat that has a passenger-side air bag that has not been disabled or turned off.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: Up through what age does the manual recommend keeping all children in the back seat?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: Children twelve years old and younger should always ride in the back seat.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.front: In a vehicle equipped with front air bags, where and facing which way should an infant always ride?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.expected_back: An infant should always ride in a rear-facing infant safety seat in the back seat of a vehicle that has air bags.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Which words or three-letter abbreviations stamped on the wheel and dash identify air bags?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: A vehicle has an air bag when the steering wheel and dashboard panel show the words air bag or the letters SRS or SIR.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.front: Besides the wheel hub and dashboard, what three places commonly display air-bag warning labels?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.expected_back: Besides the steering wheel and dashboard markings, makers may place air bag warning labels on the sun visors, on the sides of the open-door frame, or in the owner's manual.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: How did federal NHTSA air-bag cutoff switch rules expand between nineteen ninety-five and January nineteen ninety-eight?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: In nineteen ninety-five NHTSA allowed air bag cutoff switches in pickup trucks, sports cars and cars with no back seat, and from January nineteen ninety-eight it let repair shops and dealers install switches after an approved application.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: Which narrow group qualifies for cutoff switches on both the driver and passenger air bags?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: A switch for both driver and passenger air bags is for people whose medical condition makes a deploying air bag riskier than hitting the wheel, dashboard or windshield.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.front: What ten-inch rule qualifies for a driver cutoff switch, and what child situations qualify for a passenger switch?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.expected_back: A driver-side air bag switch is for people unable to keep ten inches between steering wheel center and breastbone center, while a passenger-side switch is for placing an infant or child age one to twelve in front due to no rear seat, insufficient rear-seat space or capacity, or medical monitoring.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: When should white backup lights illuminate, and what does New Jersey forbid while driving forward?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: Backup lights should come on when reversing, and New Jersey law forbids having any backup light on while the vehicle is moving forward.

sec04-card-sec04-R17.front: How can you verify brake bulbs work, and why must cracked plastic taillight covers be replaced?
sec04-card-sec04-R17.expected_back: Get a helper to check the brake lights, and replace broken light covers because their glare can affect the driver behind.

sec04-card-sec04-R18.front: If oncoming drivers repeatedly flash at you while your switch is already on low beam, what is likely wrong?
sec04-card-sec04-R18.expected_back: High and low beams must both work and be aimed correctly; other drivers flashing their lights at your low beams may mean your headlights are out of line.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: Which three steering, pedal, or sound clues tell you your brakes need immediate inspection?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: Brakes need checking if the vehicle pulls to one side when stopping, the pedal feels taut, or there is unusual squealing or grinding.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: After driving through deep puddles with conventional drum or disc brakes, how do you dry them safely?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: After driving through water, gently pump conventional disc and drum brakes to test and dry them, since braking hard could lock them up.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: What pedal pressure tests anti-lock brakes properly, and what two mistakes must you avoid while braking?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: Anti-lock brakes are tested with steady pressure on the pedal, and a driver should never pump ABS brakes or jerk the steering wheel while braking.

sec04-card-sec04-R15.front: How does drying conventional brakes after puddles contrast with braking in an ABS vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.expected_back: Conventional disc and drum brakes are pumped gently after driving through water, while anti-lock brakes are pressed steadily and never pumped.

sec04-card-sec04-R16.front: On which loose road surfaces can anti-lock brakes actually lengthen your stopping distance?
sec04-card-sec04-R16.expected_back: On very soft surfaces such as loose gravel or unpacked snow, anti-lock brakes may make the stopping distance longer.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: Within how many feet should a healthy car stop from twenty miles per hour during a chalk-mark lot test?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: A vehicle should be able to stop within twenty-five feet from twenty miles per hour, which a driver can test in an empty parking lot using chalk marks.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: In which three situations does New Jersey advise tapping your horn without overusing it?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Sound the horn to signal that you are passing, to announce yourself as you leave a blind alley, curve or driveway, or to warn another driver of danger, but do not overuse it.

sec04-card-sec04-R19.front: How should a mechanically sound vehicle track and feel on a straight, level road?
sec04-card-sec04-R19.expected_back: On a straight, level road the vehicle should keep a straight course with no front-end shimmy and without excess play in the steering wheel.

sec04-card-sec04-R20.front: What two steps apply right away if your electric turn signals burn out or fail?
sec04-card-sec04-R20.expected_back: When the turn signals fail, repair them quickly and give hand signals until they work again.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: When should you gauge tire pressure, and where do you look up the exact target number?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: Check tire pressure often, especially while the tires are cold, using the pressure listed in the owner's manual or on the driver's door jamb.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: What minimum tread depth—tested with a penny—and tire-mixing ban apply in New Jersey?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: Do not drive on tires with less than one sixteenth inch of tread, roughly the edge of a penny, and do not mix radials with other tire types.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: On which vehicle glass does New Jersey forbid aftermarket add-on window tinting?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: New Jersey prohibits add-on tinting on the windshield and the front side windows.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: Which exterior vehicle surfaces must a New Jersey driver clear of built-up snow and ice before pulling out?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: Before driving, a motorist must make every reasonable effort to clear built-up snow and ice from the exposed surfaces of the vehicle, including the hood, trunk, roof and windshield.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: Compare New Jersey's baseline fine for uncleared snow or ice with the penalty when flying ice causes damage or injury?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: Not clearing snow or ice brings a fine of twenty-five dollars to seventy-five dollars even if none falls off, and fines up to one thousand five hundred dollars when falling snow or ice causes injury or property damage.

sec04-card-sec04-R21.front: Does snow or ice actually have to blow off your roof before police can ticket you?
sec04-card-sec04-R21.expected_back: The snow and ice fine applies whether or not any snow or ice actually comes loose from the vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.front: Why is carbon monoxide in vehicle exhaust impossible to detect with your senses?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.expected_back: Carbon monoxide is an odorless, colorless gas in vehicle exhaust that can build up to deadly levels in or around a vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-R22.front: Which engine issues or rear cargo-door habits pull carbon monoxide into a moving cabin?
sec04-card-sec04-R22.expected_back: Driving with an exhaust leak or a poorly tuned engine, or with the trunk or rear tailgate open, can let carbon monoxide build up.

sec04-card-sec04-R23.front: How can snowbanks, rusted body panels, or an open garage door still cause carbon monoxide poisoning?
sec04-card-sec04-R23.expected_back: Carbon monoxide can also build up from holes in the vehicle body, from a tailpipe blocked by snow, leaves or water, and from idling in a garage or other enclosed space even with the outside door open.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.front: Why can't drivers rely on headache, dizziness, nausea, or chest pain to warn them of carbon monoxide in time?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.expected_back: Carbon monoxide can kill before a person notices any symptom such as headache, dizziness, nausea, chest pain, confusion or loss of consciousness.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.front: What immediate steps must you take if you suspect carbon monoxide poisoning inside a vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.expected_back: If carbon monoxide poisoning is suspected, move the person away from the source and call nine one one; in a vehicle, switch off the engine and get out as soon as it is safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.front: Where should you check before opening the driver's door, and what hidden hazards are you looking for?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.expected_back: Before getting into the vehicle, look both in front of it and behind it, because children or objects may be hidden in spots the driver cannot see from the seat.

sec04-card-sec04-F40.front: How far from the wheel should most drivers sit, and what five cockpit items get set before moving?
sec04-card-sec04-F40.expected_back: Before moving off, the seat should let you reach every pedal and control (about an arm's length from the wheel for most drivers), the mirrors should be adjusted, belts fastened, the gear in park or neutral with the parking brake set, and the doors locked.

sec04-card-sec04-F41.front: More than what share of all driving information reaches a motorist through the eyes?
sec04-card-sec04-F41.expected_back: More than ninety-five percent of the information a driver needs comes through vision.

sec04-card-sec04-F42.front: How often does the New Jersey manual recommend getting your vision examined?
sec04-card-sec04-F42.expected_back: A motorist should have an eye examination every two years.

sec04-card-sec04-R24.front: To cut nighttime headlight glare, which eyeglass lenses should you avoid and which coating should you pick?
sec04-card-sec04-R24.expected_back: To cut night glare, skip colored lenses because they distort color, and choose anti-reflective lens coatings.

sec04-card-sec04-R25.front: How does light intake at age sixty compare with age twenty in the manual's vision example?
sec04-card-sec04-R25.expected_back: With age, visual clarity and side vision fade; in the manual's example, a person of sixty takes in only about one third of the light that a person of twenty does.

sec04-card-sec04-F43.front: Which exact piece of your car should sit in the lower-right corner of a properly aimed driver-side mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-F43.expected_back: Set the outside mirror so the tip of the driver-side front door handle appears in the lower right of the mirror.

sec04-card-sec04-R26.front: How does a car overtaking you on the left confirm your inside and outside mirrors overlap properly?
sec04-card-sec04-R26.expected_back: To check the mirrors on the road, let a car pass on the left: as it leaves the inside mirror, its front bumper should already show in the outside mirror.

sec04-card-sec04-F44.front: Right after starting the engine, how should you verify a clear path instead of trusting mirrors alone?
sec04-card-sec04-F44.expected_back: After starting the engine, turn and look back to confirm the path is clear rather than relying on the rearview mirrors, and watch for pedestrians, bicycles and mopeds.

sec04-card-sec04-F45.front: What maximum idling time does New Jersey enforce for motor vehicles?
sec04-card-sec04-F45.expected_back: New Jersey requires every motorist to keep vehicle idling to three minutes or less.

sec04-card-sec04-R27.front: Does New Jersey's three-minute idling cap apply when stuck in highway traffic or a drive-thru line?
sec04-card-sec04-R27.expected_back: Some situations allow longer idling, such as sitting in traffic or waiting at a drive-thru, so the three-minute limit has listed exemptions.

sec04-card-sec04-F46.front: What dollar fine range can hit both vehicle owners and property owners for each unlawful idling violation?
sec04-card-sec04-F46.expected_back: Vehicle and property owners face fines of two hundred fifty dollars to one thousand dollars for each idling violation.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: How many points collected within what timeframe cause the MVC to mail you a Notice of Scheduled Suspension?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.memory_hook: Twelve to fourteen in two years
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: A driver who accumulates twelve to fourteen points within a twenty-four-month period receives a Notice of Scheduled Suspension from the MVC by mail.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Once a Notice of Scheduled Suspension arrives, what three options do you have?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: After that notice, the driver may attend a New Jersey Driver Improvement Program, ask for a hearing, or surrender the license for the suspension period.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: If you are granted a suspension hearing, which two officials have authority to decide whether your privileges get suspended?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: When a driver is granted a hearing, the MVC Chief Administrator or an Administrative Law Judge decides whether to suspend driving privileges.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: How many points are removed from your driving record when you finish a Driver Improvement Program?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Successfully completing a Driver Improvement Program takes three points off the driver's record.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: Which two types of organizations teach New Jersey Driver Improvement and Probationary Driver classes?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: Driver Improvement and Probationary Driver classes are taught by a licensed Statewide Safety Organization or a New Jersey-licensed driving school approved for that program.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: When taking a private-provider Driver Improvement or Probationary class, how much is the MVC admin fee and when is each fee due?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.memory_hook: Seventy-five before scheduling, provider before class
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: For a Driver Improvement or Probationary Driver class with a private provider, a seventy-five dollar MVC administration fee is due before scheduling and a separate provider program fee is due before attending.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: How long is your probationary period after finishing Driver Improvement or getting privileges restored, and what happens if you get a moving violation?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: After finishing a Driver Improvement Program or having driving privileges restored, a driver serves a one-year probationary period in which any moving violation leads to a scheduled suspension.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: When does New Jersey's two-year probationary driver period officially start?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: A two-year probationary driver period begins once a driver receives a special learner or examination permit.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: During the new-driver probationary period, what ticket and point combination requires you to enroll in the Probationary Driver Program?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: During that probationary period, two or more moving violations adding up to four or more points require enrollment in the Probationary Driver Program.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: How many points can finishing the Probationary Driver Program cut, and what triggers suspension if you fail to comply or reoffend?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.memory_hook: Up to three off, otherwise suspended
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: Completing the Probationary Driver Program can cut up to three points, but skipping it or picking up another moving point violation during the test period brings a suspension.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How does the point deduction for finishing a Driver Improvement Program compare with finishing a Probationary Driver Program?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.memory_hook: Improvement cuts three, Probationary up to
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: A finished Driver Improvement Program removes three points, while a finished Probationary Driver Program removes up to three points.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: How does the probation length after Driver Improvement or restoration compare with the new-driver probationary period starting at permit?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.memory_hook: One year after, two from permit
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: The probation after a Driver Improvement Program or restoration lasts one year, while the new-driver probationary period that starts with a permit lasts two years.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: What two benefits can you earn by completing a voluntary defensive driving course?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Finishing a voluntary defensive driving course removes two points from the license and may qualify the driver for a lower insurance rate.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: How often will the MVC count a voluntary defensive driving course toward reducing points on your record?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.memory_hook: Point credit once every five years
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: The MVC credits a defensive driving course toward point reduction only once every five years.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: In addition to in-person classroom sessions, what other defensive driving option does the MVC list?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: Besides classroom courses, the MVC lists approved online defensive driving providers.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: At what age do mature drivers qualify to take defensive driving courses through various driving schools or specific organizations?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: Mature drivers aged fifty-five and older can take defensive driving courses at various driving schools or through specific organizations.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: How long is the open-enrollment driver safety class available in person or online, and what rewards can it earn?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.memory_hook: Six-hour class, discount and two points
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: Various providers offer a six-hour driver safety class, open to everyone and also available online, that can earn a multi-year insurance discount and a two-point reduction where applicable.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: How many points come off your total for each violation-free, suspension-free year in good standing, and how low can your total go?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.memory_hook: Up to three off, floor zero
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Up to three points are subtracted from a driver's point total for each year without a violation or suspension while driving privileges remain in good standing, and the total never drops below zero.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: At what three-year point total do surcharges kick in, and what is the base dollar charge plus per-point add-on?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: A driver with six or more points within three years owes a surcharge of one hundred fifty dollars for six points plus twenty-five dollars for each point above six.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: Which date determines when points count toward MVC surcharges rather than the day the violation occurred?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.memory_hook: Posted date counts, not violation date
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Points count toward surcharges from the date the violation is posted to the record, not the date it happened.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: Once you hit six or more points within three years, for how long do point surcharges continue to apply?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.memory_hook: Billed while six three-year points remain
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Surcharges apply once a driver has six or more points within three years, and they keep applying for as long as six or more points posted in the preceding three years remain on the record.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: Do standard point reductions lower your surcharge total, and how often and how long is a surcharge paid?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.memory_hook: No reductions, paid yearly three years
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: Standard point reductions do not apply to the surcharge system, and a surcharge is paid every year for three years on top of any court fines.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: Beyond court fines and state surcharges, what ongoing private cost can motor vehicle convictions increase?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: Motor vehicle convictions may also raise the premiums an insurance company charges.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: What is the yearly surcharge for driving unlicensed compared with driving while suspended or without liability insurance?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: The yearly surcharge is one hundred dollars for driving unlicensed and two hundred fifty dollars for driving while suspended or for having no liability insurance on a motor vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: What is the yearly surcharge for a DUI or breath-test refusal, and what does it jump to on a third offense within three years?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.memory_hook: One thousand yearly, fifteen hundred third
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: A DUI or refusal carries a one thousand dollars yearly surcharge, which rises to one thousand five hundred dollars for a third offense within three years.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: What three consequences hit a parent or guardian convicted of DUI while carrying a passenger under eighteen?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.memory_hook: Disorderly offense, six months, five days
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: A parent or guardian convicted of DUI with a passenger under eighteen in the vehicle commits a disorderly persons offense, faces up to six months of suspension and must do up to five days of community service.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: If you fail to pay MVC surcharges, what three legal collection actions can follow?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.memory_hook: Court judgment, property lien, garnished wages
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Unpaid surcharges can lead to collection action, including a Superior Court judgment, a lien on real property or wage garnishment.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: How long do point violations recorded after March first, nineteen seventy-four remain on a New Jersey driver's record?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Point violations recorded after March one, nineteen seventy-four, stay on a driver's record permanently.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: Besides public highways and roadways, on what three types of government-owned and maintained spaces do traffic laws apply?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.memory_hook: Government parking lots, driveways, and grounds
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: Traffic laws apply not only on highways and roadways but also on parking areas, driveways and grounds owned and maintained by government entities.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: How many points are assessed across New Jersey's three speeding brackets over the posted limit?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.memory_hook: Speeding costs two, four, or five
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Speeding one to fourteen miles per hour over the limit costs two points, fifteen to twenty-nine miles per hour over costs four points, and thirty miles per hour or more over costs five points.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: How does the point penalty change when speeding climbs from fifteen-to-twenty-nine over the limit to thirty or more over?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.memory_hook: Four points jumps up to five
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: Speeding fifteen to twenty-nine miles per hour over the limit carries four points, but thirty miles per hour or more over jumps to five.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: What point penalties apply to racing on a highway versus not yielding to someone in a crosswalk?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.memory_hook: Highway racing five, crosswalk yield two
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Racing on a highway carries five points, and failing to yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk carries two points.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.front: What point penalty applies if a construction vehicle exceeds forty-five miles per hour?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.memory_hook: Construction vehicle over forty-five costs three
sec12-card-sec12-R13.expected_back: Driving a construction vehicle faster than forty-five miles per hour carries three points.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: How many points do tailgating and reckless driving each carry compared with careless driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.memory_hook: Tailgating and reckless five, careless two
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Tailgating and reckless driving each carry five points, while careless driving carries two.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.front: How many points does driving in an unsafe manner carry, and which offense triggers those points?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.memory_hook: Four points on third within five
sec12-card-sec12-R16.expected_back: Driving in an unsafe manner carries four points, but only for a third or later violation within five years of the previous one.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: How many points do failing to keep right of oncoming traffic and improper passing on the right or off the roadway carry?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.memory_hook: Oncoming right five, bad pass four
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: Failing to keep to the right of a vehicle coming from the opposite direction carries five points, while passing improperly on the right or off the roadway carries four.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: How many points are added to your record for improper passing in a no-passing zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: Improper passing in a no passing zone carries four points.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: On New Jersey's three major toll highways, what point penalties hit moving against traffic versus improper passing?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.memory_hook: Against traffic two, improper passing four
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: On the New Jersey Turnpike, Garden State Parkway and Atlantic City Expressway, moving against traffic carries two points and improper passing carries four.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: How many points do you get for improperly passing a school bus compared with improperly passing a frozen dessert truck?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.memory_hook: School bus five, dessert truck four
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Improperly passing a school bus carries five points, and improperly passing a frozen dessert truck carries four.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: What point penalty hits an improper signal-light turn, an improper left or right turn, or an illegal U-turn?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.memory_hook: Every improper turn carries three points
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: An improper turn at a traffic light, an improper right or left turn and an improper U-turn each carry three points.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: How many points does handheld phone use while driving carry, and on which convictions do those points apply?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.memory_hook: Three points starting third within ten
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: Using a handheld phone while driving carries three points, assessed on a third conviction within ten years of the second and on every fourth or later offense.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.front: What point penalty applies for ignoring a traffic officer's command or disregarding traffic signals?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.memory_hook: Officer direction and signals cost two
sec12-card-sec12-R14.expected_back: Failing to obey an officer's direction and failing to observe traffic signals each carry two points.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.front: What point penalty hits running a traffic light, blowing past a flashing red, or failing to signal turns?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.memory_hook: Red light, flashing red, signal two
sec12-card-sec12-R17.expected_back: Failing to stop for a traffic light, failing to stop at a flashing red signal and failing to signal properly each carry two points.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.front: What point penalty applies for not yielding right-of-way to an emergency rig or at an intersection?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.memory_hook: Emergency and intersection yield cost two
sec12-card-sec12-R15.expected_back: Failing to yield to an emergency vehicle and failing to yield at an intersection each carry two points.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: How many points do violating the Move Over Law, disobeying Stop or Yield signs, and an out-of-state moving violation each carry?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.memory_hook: Move Over, signs, out-of-state cost two
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: Violating the Move Over Law, failing to obey Stop or Yield signs and committing a moving violation out of state each carry two points.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: How many points does leaving the scene of a crash add when nobody is injured versus when personal injury occurs?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.memory_hook: No injury two, personal injury eight
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: Leaving the scene of a crash costs two points when no one is hurt and eight points when there is personal injury.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: How many points are added to your New Jersey driving record when you commit a traffic violation in another state?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: A traffic violation committed in another state adds two points to a New Jersey record.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: Under the Nonresident Violator Compact, what happens if you fail to satisfy a traffic ticket received in a member state?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.memory_hook: Satisfy ticket or risk home suspension
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: Under the Nonresident Violator Compact, a driver ticketed in a member state must satisfy the citation or risk suspension in their home state.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: Under the Driver License Compact, what happens to traffic violations you commit in other member states?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.memory_hook: Member-state violations join your home record
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: Under the Driver License Compact, violations from other member states become part of a driver's New Jersey record.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: How does the role of the Nonresident Violator Compact differ from the role of the Driver License Compact?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.memory_hook: Violator enforces compliance, License shares records
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: The Nonresident Violator Compact makes visiting drivers answer for tickets as residents would, while the Driver License Compact shares violation records so out-of-state tickets land on the home record.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.front: How many jurisdictions belong to the Nonresident Violator Compact, and which three violation types are excluded?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.memory_hook: Forty-four states plus DC, three exclusions
sec12-card-sec12-R18.expected_back: The Nonresident Violator Compact covers forty-four states plus the District of Columbia and excludes parking or standing, weight limit and hazmat violations.

sec12-card-sec12-R19.front: What two legal protections do visiting drivers keep under the Nonresident Violator Compact?
sec12-card-sec12-R19.memory_hook: Due process kept, no out-of-state detention
sec12-card-sec12-R19.expected_back: Nonresident drivers keep due process protection and cannot be detained out of state under that compact.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: Which three legal steps must a New Jersey resident complete before driving a newly bought new or used car on public roads?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Before a New Jersey resident drives a newly bought vehicle, new or used, on public roads, it must be titled, registered and insured.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: Where must a vehicle's Lemon Law classification permanently appear?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: A vehicle classified under the Lemon Law must carry that classification on its title.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: Who is permitted to process a title and registration transaction at an MVC Vehicle Center?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: Only the titled owner, or someone authorized to act for the owner, may process a title and registration transaction at an MVC Vehicle Center.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: What document does a leased car require at the MVC, and who supplies the original title for an out-of-state leased or financed car?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: A leased vehicle needs a power of attorney issued by the leasing company, and for a leased or financed out-of-state vehicle, get the original title from the lien holder or leasing company.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: How soon after moving to New Jersey must a new resident title and register their vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: A driver who moves to New Jersey must title and register the vehicle within sixty days, or sooner if the out-of-state registration runs out first.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: Which MVC form handles an initial registration, and what two insurance facts must be written on it?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: An initial registration uses the BA-forty-nine application at an MVC Vehicle Center, and it must list the current insurance company and policy number.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: Which documents prove ownership when registering a brand-new vehicle versus a used vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: Proof of ownership is the manufacturer's certificate of origin plus the dealer's certificate of sale for a new vehicle, or a title signed over by the previous owner for a used one.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: What sales-tax requirement applies when registering a vehicle at an MVC Vehicle Center?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: You must also show that sales tax has been paid, or pay it at an MVC Vehicle Center.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: How long does the initial registration on a brand-new vehicle last compared with standard registrations?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: The first registration of a brand-new vehicle lasts four years, while other registrations usually last one year.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: How many license plates does New Jersey issue to a passenger car versus a trailer, moped, or motorcycle?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: A registered car gets two matching plates, one for the front and one for the rear, while a trailer, moped or motorcycle gets just one.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: Within what ground-clearance range must passenger vehicle plates be mounted, and in what condition?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: Passenger vehicle plates must be mounted at least twelve inches but less than forty-eight inches above the ground and kept clean and visible.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: From how far away must your rear license plate be readable at night, and does a reflectorized plate waive lighting?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: The rear plate must be lit so it can be read from fifty feet at night, even when the plate is reflectorized.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: What happens if a license-plate frame or tinted cover obscures any lettering on your plate?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: A plate cover or holder that hides any lettering on the plate is a violation with a fine of up to one hundred dollars.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: What single rule governs which license plates may be mounted on a vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: Only valid plates may be placed on a vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: Which two agencies must hear about lost or stolen plates, and how quickly must lost or damaged plates be replaced?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: For lost or stolen plates, notify local police, save a copy of the complaint and notify the MVC; lost or damaged plates must be replaced within twenty-four hours at an MVC Vehicle Center.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: Which three maximum penalties can hit a driver caught using forged or counterfeit license plates?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: Using forged or counterfeit plates can bring a fine of up to five hundred dollars, up to sixty days in jail or a license suspension of up to six months.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: Under which insurance or vehicle-disposal situations must you surrender your license plates to the MVC?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: If you end the vehicle's insurance, or the vehicle is sold, junked or destroyed and you do not plan to buy another, the plates must be turned in to the MVC.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: What two options do you have for your old plates after selling a car, and what proof should you keep?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: Most plates can be transferred to your next vehicle, and plates not transferred after a sale must be surrendered to the MVC in person or by mail, keeping the receipt.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: Which gasoline-powered passenger cars must pass a New Jersey state inspection every two years?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: Gasoline-fueled passenger vehicles from model year nineteen ninety-six on that are more than five model years old must pass a state inspection every two years.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: What inspection credential does a passenger car under five model years old receive, and when does it run out?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: New passenger vehicles under five model years old receive a new car dealer sticker that expires five years after initial registration.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: How long does a new dealer sticker last on a passenger vehicle compared with a new commercial-registered dealer vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: A new passenger vehicle's dealer sticker runs five years, while a commercial-registered vehicle under one year old bought from a dealer gets a sticker that runs one year.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Which gasoline and diesel commercial vehicles must pass inspection every single year?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Gasoline-fueled commercial vehicles, and diesel commercial vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating of eight thousand five hundred pounds or less, must be inspected every year.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: How does the routine inspection cycle for passenger cars differ from covered commercial-registered vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: Passenger vehicles are inspected every two years, but commercial-registered vehicles covered by the rule are inspected every year.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: Which model-year, age, and weight rules put a diesel passenger vehicle onto a two-year emissions schedule?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Diesel passenger vehicles from model year nineteen ninety-seven on, more than five model years old and with a gross vehicle weight rating of eight thousand five hundred pounds or less, must pass an emissions inspection every two years.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: After registering a passenger vehicle five model years old or older in New Jersey, how many days does a new resident have to inspect it?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: A new resident must have a passenger vehicle that is five model years old or older inspected within fourteen days of registering it in New Jersey.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: How does New Jersey handle inspection for a new resident's passenger car that is under five model years old?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: A new resident's passenger vehicle under five model years old is exempt from inspection and gets a new car dealer sticker expiring five years from the model year.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: Which three documents must you bring along to every New Jersey vehicle inspection?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: Bring a valid driver license, valid New Jersey registration and the vehicle's insurance documents to any inspection.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: Which two types of facilities conduct standard New Jersey motor vehicle inspections?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Inspections take place at a State inspection station or at a State-licensed private inspection facility (PIF).

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: Where in New Jersey must high-rise lifted trucks and reconstructed vehicles go for inspection?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: High-rise and reconstructed vehicles must go to one of the MVC Specialty Inspection sites in Eatontown, Secaucus or Winslow.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: Which type of motor vehicle insurance is mandatory for every vehicle registered in New Jersey?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Liability insurance is mandatory for every vehicle registered in New Jersey.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: Where must your New Jersey insurance ID card stay, when must you present it, and is a phone copy valid?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: Each insured vehicle gets a New Jersey insurance ID card that stays in the vehicle and must be shown at inspection, after a crash and at a traffic stop or roadside check, and an electronic version is accepted.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: Which four penalties can follow driving a vehicle without mandatory liability insurance?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: Driving without liability insurance can bring fines, community service, license and registration suspension and violation surcharges.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: Which New Jersey state department's website outlines available auto-insurance coverage options?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: The type and cost of insurance coverage vary, and the Department of Banking and Insurance website lists coverage choices.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.front: What criminal, civil-fine, and licensing penalties can hit someone who files a false insurance claim or application?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.expected_back: Insurance fraud through a false claim or application can lead to criminal charges and jail, civil fines of up to fifteen thousand dollars per violation, and possible loss of the driver license.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.front: How does insurance fraud hurt honest New Jersey drivers, and how does the Insurance Fraud Prosecutor treat tips?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.expected_back: Fraud raises insurance costs for everyone in New Jersey, and tips to the Office of the Insurance Fraud Prosecutor are kept anonymous and confidential.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Where on the steering wheel—and with what thumb placement—should your hands sit for normal driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Resting thumbs lightly along the wheel face instead of hooking spokes prevents broken thumbs in potholes or crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: Why does holding nine and three matter specifically if the steering-wheel air bag deploys?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: High hands draped across twelve o'clock get blasted straight back into your face when the hub cover splits.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: Which inward-facing steering grip must a driver never use while turning?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Reaching inside the wheel spokes traps your wrist if a front tire hits a curb or rut.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: For which two brief driving actions may one hand legally leave the steering wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Outside stick-shift gear changes and window arm cues, two-handed steering gives instant emergency leverage.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: How firmly should you hold the wheel, and how does steering input change as speed rises?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: White-knuckle tension tires arms quickly, while tiny highway inputs move lanes sharply at higher speeds.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: Where within your lane should you track, especially on a two-lane road with oncoming traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Holding the center of the right-hand lane maximizes buffer space away from opposing mirrors.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: Up to how many degrees around the rim may your hands travel during hand-over-hand turning?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Smooth arcs up to a hundred sixty-five degrees turn corners crisply without tangling your wrists.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: What turn range does hand-over-hand cover compared with what your hands do on a gentle curve?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Sweeping highway bends need only slight finger or wrist pressure without ever lifting a palm off nine and three.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: How do your pushing hand and crossing hand coordinate to start a hand-over-hand turn?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Sliding one hand up from nine or three toward twelve lets the opposite hand cross cleanly over the top.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: Which two steering techniques straighten the front tires smoothly coming out of a turn?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Never take hands completely off a spinning wheel—either unwind hand-over-hand or let the rim glide under light finger control.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: In which four driving situations does hand-over-hand steering shine brightest?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Rapid multi-angle wheel input saves tight parking stalls, sharp intersections, and sudden rear-end skids.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: Which seven human, environmental, and mechanical variables govern total stopping distance?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Wait—let's keep every piece sharp because worn rubber, heavy cargo, or rain stretches stops even with alert reflexes.
sec05-card-sec05-F08.must_match_memory_hook: Driver, weather, weight, brakes, road, speed

visual_sync.text_span: Driver, weather, weight, brakes, road, speed

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: Across every road and vehicle type, what single speed-and-stopping rule never changes?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Braking energy climbs with the square of speed, stretching stopping room dramatically with every extra ten miles per hour.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: Is there a simple formula that predicts exact stopping footage for every car at a set speed?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Because pavement grip, tire compound, and driver alertness shift constantly, published charts only show baseline averages.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: Under everyday traffic conditions, how long does a typical driver's reaction time take?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Before your shoe even touches the brake pedal, three-quarters of a second rolls past at full cruising speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: How many feet of pavement does your car cover every single second at sixty miles per hour?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Looking down at a dashboard screen for two seconds at sixty carries you blind across half a football field.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.question_text: In New Jersey's stopping table, what reaction, braking, and total distances apply at ten miles per hour?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.teaching_text: Notice that at parking-lot speeds, reaction distance of eleven feet actually exceeds the eight-foot braking roll.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: What reaction distance, braking distance, and total stop does the manual list at twenty miles per hour?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Doubling speed from ten to twenty nearly quadruples braking distance from eight feet up to thirty-one.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: What reaction, braking, and total stopping footage does the chart show at thirty miles per hour?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: Even in a quiet thirty-mile-per-hour town zone, stopping consumes over a hundred feet from hazard sight to halt.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: At fifty miles per hour, how many reaction feet, braking feet, and total feet does stopping take?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: On fifty-mile-per-hour rural roads, total stopping room stretches nearly two hundred fifty feet.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.question_text: At sixty miles per hour, what reaction, braking, and total stopping distances appear in New Jersey's chart?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.teaching_text: Crossing three hundred forty-three feet tops an entire football field between goalpost and goalpost.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.question_text: What reaction, braking, and total stopping distances does the manual give at seventy miles per hour?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.teaching_text: High-speed braking alone eats three hundred seventy-six feet after seventy-seven feet of reaction roll.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.question_text: Roughly how many feet per second does the manual state for typical braking deceleration?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.teaching_text: That fourteen-feet-per-second benchmark underpins all of the manual's dry-pavement braking distance calculations on clear roads.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: What braking habit do beginners often get wrong, and what foot pressure produces controlled stops?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Routine late panic stabs pitch passengers forward, chew up pads and tires, and invite rear-end hits.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: Which foot operates both the accelerator and brake, and what is the left foot's lone job in a stick-shift?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Using one dedicated right foot prevents pressing gas and brake together in a sudden panic.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.question_text: Does front-wheel versus rear-wheel drive change your braking technique—or what system actually matters?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.teaching_text: Drivetrain layout affects acceleration traction, whereas braking technique hinges solely on ABS versus conventional drums and discs.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: Even on dry asphalt at thirty-five miles per hour, what steering mistake can make an ABS car lose control?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Anti-lock electronics cannot overcome physics when violent wheel yanks overload front-tire side grip.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.question_text: Where should new drivers get comfortable with how anti-lock pedal pulsing and steering feel?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.teaching_text: Feeling normal ABS pedal chatter in an open parking lot stops beginners from lifting off during real emergencies.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: Before which four everyday speed or path changes must you give a proper signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Consistent blinkers and brake-light cues let surrounding drivers anticipate your next move smoothly.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: How far before a turn must your blinker click on in New Jersey, and what comes right after completing the turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Leaving a forgotten turn signal blinking down the block tricks cross-street cars into pulling out ahead of you.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: How do you hold your left arm and palm to hand-signal stopping or slowing down?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Pointing straight down with your open palm facing trailing traffic mimics a clear stop barrier.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: Which direction does a driver extend the left arm to hand-signal a right turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Bending the left elbow ninety degrees skyward makes your intention visible past the roof pillar.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: How does a driver hold the left arm out the window for a left turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Pointing horizontally out the driver's window aims straight toward the left turn path.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: Can you line up downward, upward, and straight out with their three driver hand-signal meanings?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Locking that three-way rhythm in memory keeps test stress from flipping right-turn upward with stop downward.
sec05-card-sec05-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Down stops, up right, out left

visual_sync.text_span: Down stops, up right, out left

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: What alternate right-turn hand signal may bicyclists, skateboarders, and inline skaters legally use?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Without a passenger door blocking their right side, open-air riders can point directly right with their right arm.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: Where is sounding your horn to alert a vehicle you are overtaking specifically appropriate?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Open rural passing benefits from a brief horn tap, whereas quiet neighborhoods and town blocks restrict unnecessary honking.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Under normal conditions, from at least how many feet away must a vehicle horn be heard?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Two hundred feet gives highway traffic roughly two seconds of advance audible warning.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: Which vehicles hold exclusive authority to mount sirens, whistles, or bells?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Keeping emergency acoustic warnings exclusive ensures drivers yield immediately whenever a siren sounds.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: Why must you combine mirror checks with physically turning around before backing up?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Rear pillars and trunk lids hide low obstacles unless you twist around to scan directly.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: In reverse gear, which way does the rear of your car move when you turn the wheel right, left, or straight?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Turn the top of the wheel toward whichever direction you want the back bumper to travel.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: While turning the wheel in reverse, which way does the front nose of your vehicle swing?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Forgetting nose swing scrapes your left front fender against adjacent parked cars while backing right.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: Where do your head, torso, right arm, and left hand go during straight-line backing?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Draping your right arm over the passenger seatback opens your torso to look straight through the rear glass.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: How fast—in miles per hour—should you normally roll while backing up?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Rear-wheel steering geometry feels touchy at speed, so creeping at two to four miles per hour keeps control effortless.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: What must your wheels do before you shift out of Reverse into a forward gear?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Slamming into Drive while still rolling backward shocks transmission gears and lurches the car unpredictably.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: Which one-handed reversing shortcut is dangerous and can fail you on the MVC road test?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Spinning the rim with one flat palm slips easily during turning reverses, so examiners require two-handed control.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: Roughly how far must an applicant back smoothly in a straight line during the New Jersey road test?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Examiners watch whether you hold a steady curb gap for roughly a hundred feet without weaving.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: Which two separate New Jersey rules—one on the road test and one on the street—use one hundred feet?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: You back one hundred feet straight for your examiner and signal plus lane-position one hundred feet before every turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: Since August thirty-one, two thousand sixteen, how does the MVC treat factory backup cameras and sensors during road tests?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Staring exclusively at a dash screen without shoulder checks and mirror scans still fails fundamental reversing technique.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: What is the only safe move if you overshoot a street corner or driveway turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Backing up inside active traffic lanes surprises following drivers who never expect reverse lights mid-street.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: Why must turns be planned well upstream, and how does faster traffic affect your timing?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: High-speed traffic eats up lane-change gaps fast, turning late dives across lanes into sideswipe hazards.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: Before starting any turn, where do you check your mirrors, and which smaller road users must you hunt for?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Narrow two-wheel silhouettes hide effortlessly behind mirror housings and door pillars until you scan deliberately.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: When positioning for an upcoming turn, which comes first—moving into the turn lane or signaling?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Flipping the blinker after drifting sideways defeats the whole warning purpose for drivers beside you.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.question_text: When do you shed speed for an intersection turn, and how should you drive through the arc itself?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.teaching_text: Finishing braking on straight pavement leaves full tire grip for steering cleanly along painted turn guides.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: What lane discipline applies mid-turn, and what dashboard check follows straightening out?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Drifting wide mid-intersection clips adjacent turners, and checking your dash catches non-canceling stalks.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: Where on the roadway—and with what sightlines—should you begin a turnaround?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Starting near a hillcrest or blind curve invites oncoming cars to appear mid-maneuver while you straddle lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: Walk through the three steering legs—and curb clearances—of a New Jersey K-turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Stopping several inches shy of each curb prevents bumping tires against concrete—an instant road-test deduction.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.question_text: Which classic turnaround maneuver is mandatory for every new driver on the MVC road test?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.teaching_text: Examiners grade every K-turn on smooth low speed, full mirror-and-shoulder scans, and zero curb strikes.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.question_text: What two steps secure an automatic versus a manual vehicle every time you park?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.teaching_text: Setting the parking brake first keeps vehicle weight off transmission pawls or manual gears.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.question_text: When parking downhill beside a curb, which way do your front wheels point and what gear holds a stick-shift?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.teaching_text: Angling tires into the concrete chocks the right front tire immediately if gravity nudges the car forward.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.question_text: When parking uphill beside a curb, how do you angle the front wheels and set a manual gearbox?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.teaching_text: Turning left away from the curb lets the back of the right front tire hook cleanly against the curb face.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: How do wheel angle and manual gear choice flip between downhill curb parking and uphill curb parking?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Both wheel angles use raised concrete as a physical wedge while pairing opposite manual gear ratios against roll.
sec05-card-sec05-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Down toward reverse, up away low

visual_sync.text_span: Down toward reverse, up away low

sec05-card-sec05-R21.question_text: What checks, signals, and steering steps guide you cleanly into a right-hand angle parking space?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.teaching_text: Confirming rear-quarter clearance before cutting sharply in avoids clipping the bumper of the car beside your stall.

sec05-card-sec05-R22.question_text: What physical check comes before climbing in to back out of an angle space, and how do you start reversing?
sec05-card-sec05-R22.teaching_text: Shopping carts, low bollards, and children vanish behind trunks unless you walk around first.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.question_text: How do you alert walkers and clear tall neighboring SUVs while backing out of an angle stall?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.teaching_text: Halting as soon as your sightline clears adjacent roofs lets you spot aisle traffic before swinging out.

sec05-card-sec05-R23.question_text: At what exact clearance point do you straighten your wheels while backing out of an angle space?
sec05-card-sec05-R23.teaching_text: Turning too early or straightening before your left front tire clears the adjacent bumper scrapes fenders.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.question_text: How important is parallel parking on the MVC road test, and how much rehearsal does it demand?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.teaching_text: Tight spatial judgment in reverse trips up unprepared applicants faster than any other test station.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.question_text: How far apart should you space practice flags for parallel parking, and what does bumping one tell you?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.teaching_text: Mastering twenty-five-foot cones in an empty lot saves real-world bumpers from expensive scrapes.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.question_text: How many feet beside the forward parked car should you pull up to begin parallel parking?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.teaching_text: Starting closer than two feet risks clipping their bumper, while starting past four misses the curb angle.

sec05-card-sec05-R24.question_text: Which two signals and visual check come right before backing into a parallel space?
sec05-card-sec05-R24.teaching_text: Alerting trailing cars before you halt prevents them from nosing right behind the space you want.

sec05-card-sec05-R25.question_text: Looking out the back window, how far do you roll straight back before cranking the wheel full right?
sec05-card-sec05-R25.teaching_text: Rolling two feet straight back clears the adjacent side panels before your tail angles curbward.

sec05-card-sec05-R26.question_text: What three things do you do once your front nose clears the rear bumper of the car ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-R26.teaching_text: Catching a steep angle early prevents slamming your right rear tire into the concrete curb.

sec05-card-sec05-R27.question_text: How do you steer, stop, and center to finish backing into a parallel space?
sec05-card-sec05-R27.teaching_text: Swinging full left tucks the front end inline before a short forward pull centers both bumper gaps.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.question_text: At maximum, how many inches from the curb may a properly parallel-parked vehicle's tires sit?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.teaching_text: Parking farther than six inches leaves your driver-side doors sticking out into passing traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R28.question_text: What pace and pedal control make backing into tight parking stalls much easier?
sec05-card-sec05-R28.teaching_text: Creeping smoothly gives your eyes plenty of time to spot mirror landmarks and adjust steering early.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: What single factor causes the majority of motor vehicle crashes?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Blaming bad luck or road surfaces misses the truth that human choices cause most collisions.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: What three steps make up the standard crash-prevention formula — and which three mindset habits back it up?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Expecting surprises, never assuming other drivers drive flawlessly, and staying calm turns awareness into timely action.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: What should an angry or excited driver do before getting behind the wheel, and why?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Heated anger or excitement warps judgment and reaction timing long before you even leave the driveway.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: Why isn't creeping noticeably slower than surrounding vehicles automatically the safest way to drive?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Crawling well below legal traffic pace creates speed gaps that trigger abrupt braking and risky passing.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: How does the New Jersey manual define aggressive driving, and which five unlawful acts illustrate it?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Stacking erratic lane cuts, sudden speed bursts, tailgating, running controls, and failing to yield escalates crash risk.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: What two duties still apply on a right turn on red, and how does the manual view rolling past without a complete stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Rolling a right-on-red counts directly as ignoring a traffic control device and endangers crosswalk users.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: What triggers road rage, and what dangerous driving moves or hostile signals display it?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Losing your cool over a traffic slight turns into running lights, weaving, illegal right passes, screaming, gestures, or beam flashing.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: What specialized law-enforcement resource does New Jersey deploy in its campaign against road rage?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Dedicated patrol officers trained to spot aggressive progressions pull hostile drivers over before tempers cause wrecks.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: Even when an emergency legally permits a handheld phone call, what is still the safest way to place it?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Stopping off the travel lane first lets you give dispatchers clear details without steering one-handed through traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Name and define the four categories of driving distraction?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Texting is lethal because it stacks eyes-off visual, hands-off manual, and mind-off cognitive distraction simultaneously.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Where do distractions rank among teen crash causes, and how far does a car travel during a few distracted seconds at highway speed?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Looking down for just a few seconds at highway speed sends your car blind down a whole football field.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: Beyond texting and scrolling, which everyday cabin habits — from GPS, music, and food to passengers and smartwatches — count as distractions?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Even hands-free calls, reaching for dropped items, programming navigation while moving, or checking a smartwatch steals vital focus.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: What three effects does fatigue have on a driver, and how dangerous can drowsy driving become?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Delayed reflexes, hair-trigger irritability, and nodding off make an exhausted driver rival an intoxicated one.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: Enacted in June two thousand three, what does Maggie's Law make illegal and how does it classify sleepless fatal crashes?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Knowingly driving while sleep-impaired violates state law and establishes criminal recklessness under vehicular homicide.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: What is highway hypnosis, and what eye-movement habit prevents it?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Staring at one spot for more than a few seconds lulls your brain into a glazed highway trance.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: How frequently should you stop to rest on a long trip — or what partner option keeps fatigue away?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Taking a break every two hours or rotating with another licensed passenger keeps alertness crisp.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: Which drivers — by sleep debt, trip style, medication, age, or work schedule — face the highest drowsy-driving risk?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Young drivers, shift workers, commercial haulers, solo rural travelers, and anyone mixing sedating meds or lost sleep top the danger list.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Which four visual, audible, or headlight cues help you communicate your intentions or presence to other drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Turn or arm signals, eye contact, a quick horn tap, or a brief low-high-low beam flick at night prevent surprises.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: How should your lane choice telegraph an upcoming turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Positioning early in the lane dedicated to your intended turn stops last-second swoops across adjacent cars.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: What steering habits fit town or city traffic, and what lights belong on whenever you pull off the road?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Skipping abrupt turns or lane darts calms city streets, while four-way flashers protect roadside stops.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: What lane-straddling mistake must you avoid, and what three-step check-and-signal sequence makes a lane change safe?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Riding across lane lines confuses neighbors, whereas checking mirror, blind spot, and blinker keeps shifts clean.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.question_text: Which three necessity, speed, and marking conditions must all hold true before you pass or change lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.teaching_text: Breaking the speed limit to squeeze past someone violates passing law even where dashed lines allow overtaking.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: After overtaking a car, what mirror cue confirms you are far enough ahead to signal right, return, and cancel your blinker?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Spotting the passed vehicle inside your center rearview mirror proves you will not clip their front fender.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: What lane and speed response helps an overtaking driver pass you safely, and when do you resume normal speed?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Backing off slightly shortens the passer's exposure in the left lane before you resume pace once they clear.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: What is tailgating, and what multi-car crash pattern does it commonly trigger?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Leaving zero braking gap behind the lead car turns one sudden tap of the brakes into a multi-car accordion crash.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.question_text: How should you position inside your lane and manage space around all sides of your vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.teaching_text: Centering your car with open buffers around you preserves stopping and passing options when traffic shifts.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: How many car lengths — and roughly how many feet — does the traditional rule of thumb add per ten miles per hour, and when do you add more?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: High speeds or slick weather outrun the basic twenty-feet-per-ten rule, calling for even wider buffers.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: While one twenty-foot car length per ten miles per hour is common, does the New Jersey manual consider any following rule perfect?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Judging twenty-foot car lengths by eye at freeway speeds is tricky, so no single formula guarantees safety alone.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: Walk through how you use a fixed roadside object to apply New Jersey's three-seconds-plus following rule?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Reaching that shadow or signpost before finishing three full seconds warns you immediately to drop back.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: To how many seconds should you stretch your following interval in bad weather?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Rain or slick spray stretches tire stopping distance, demanding at least four full seconds behind the car ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Compare your minimum time cushion under the three-seconds-plus rule on normal dry pavement versus bad weather?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Adding extra seconds automatically scales your physical gap upward whenever speed rises or traction drops.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.question_text: What road conditions do standard time and distance following guidelines assume, and what payoff comes from practicing them?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.teaching_text: Baseline numbers assume dry pavement, good tires, and alert eyes, letting you brake smoothly instead of panic-stopping.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: Which three distances add together to make total stopping distance?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Your car rolls forward while your eyes spot danger and your foot moves before the brake pads ever bite.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: What foot habit trims reaction distance, and how does vehicle weight affect total stopping distance?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Hovering your foot near the brake pedal shaves reaction roll, while heavy trucks carry extra momentum.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.question_text: What maintenance awareness should you keep on your brakes, and how should following distance shift on wet, snowy, or icy roads?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.teaching_text: Knowing how your brakes respond and opening extra space on rain, snow, or ice prevents rear-end slides.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: On ideal pavement, how many minimum car lengths does the manual's table list at twenty, thirty, forty, and fifty miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Ideal dry pavement matches the tens digit cleanly from two lengths at twenty up to five at fifty.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: How do the minimum car lengths in the manual's table change on wet pavement across twenty, thirty, forty, and fifty miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Wet asphalt cuts tire grip enough to double every ideal number straight to four, six, eight, and ten lengths.
sec08-card-sec08-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Doubles to four, six, eight, ten

visual_sync.text_span: Doubles to four, six, eight, ten

sec08-card-sec08-R16.question_text: In New Jersey's minimum following distance table, how do the car lengths for gravel compare with wet pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.teaching_text: Loose stones roll underfoot like water film, giving gravel the exact same four, six, eight, and ten counts.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: How must your speed, braking, and steering inputs change on wet roads, and why?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Jerky steering or abrupt throttle and brake changes snap wet tire grip and launch a skid.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: At roughly what speed can tires start hydroplaning on a film of water, and what happens as speed climbs?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Even neighborhood highway speeds around thirty-five miles per hour can wedge water under worn tire treads.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: What happens to tire contact, braking, and steering on wet roads above fifty-five miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Once water wedges tires completely off the asphalt past fifty-five, neither brakes nor steering wheels respond.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: Separate New Jersey's two hydroplaning speed benchmarks — where it can begin versus where tires can lose road contact entirely?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Written exams test thirty-five against fifty-five directly, so pair thirty-five with onset and fifty-five with total float.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: What tire rule, speed habit, and lane-position trick help prevent hydroplaning during heavy rain?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Deep tread channels water away while slowing down and riding the road's crowned center lane dodges deep puddles.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.question_text: Once a vehicle is hydroplaning on water, which three minor forces are enough to spin it into a skid?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.teaching_text: With zero rubber touching pavement, even a breeze, slight pavement crown shift, or tiny steering nudge spins the car.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: How should you warm up your engine and clear your vehicle's exterior before driving in cold winter weather?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Clearing every roof, hood, and trunk surface prevents snow sheets from sliding across your windshield or flying backward.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: Who is legally responsible in New Jersey if ice flies off a moving vehicle and causes death, injury, or property damage?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Skipping roof-ice removal carries serious legal liability when frozen slabs smash into windshields behind you.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.question_text: What visibility and weather hazards multiply in winter, and what reservoir fluid must be winter-ready?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.teaching_text: Plain water freezes solid in cold lines, making proper winter windshield washer fluid vital against road salt spray.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.question_text: After how many consecutive minutes is vehicle idling prohibited in New Jersey, and which situations are exempt?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.teaching_text: Shut off parked engines past three minutes unless stuck in traffic, undergoing repair or inspection, responding to emergencies, or loading buses.

sec08-card-sec08-R24.question_text: Before pulling out in frost or ice, how must you prepare your vehicle's glass and climate system?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.teaching_text: Peeking through a tiny scraped porthole hides pedestrians and cross traffic in all four corners.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: Which three driver mistakes break tire traction and start a skid?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Punching the throttle, yanking the steering wheel, or slamming brakes asks more grip than slick pavement has.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.question_text: How can you safely test just how slick a snowy or icy road is — and what else does that test reveal?
