sec08-card-sec08-R20.teaching_text: Feeling when tires slip during a slow, gentle brake tap shows your safe stopping pace early.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: On snow and ice, how does proper pedal technique differ between ABS brakes and conventional disc or drum brakes?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Pumping defeats antilock computer pulsing, while non-ABS disc or drum brakes respond best to firm steady pressure.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: If conventional non-ABS brakes lock up on slick pavement, how should you work the brake pedal until control returns?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Letting locked tires roll freely restores steering, and stepping back down slightly softer finds grip without re-locking.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: Contrast what your foot does on snow and ice with ABS versus locked conventional brakes?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Mixing these up makes drivers pump ABS needlessly or hold conventional brakes locked into a straight slide.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: Where do winter snow tires fall short, and what equipment delivers the best grip on ice and deep or hard-packed snow?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Rubber winter tread helps in loose snow yet slides on glare ice where metal chains bite.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: What three maneuvers do snow tires assist in snow — and why do tire chains still win in severe winter conditions?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Snow tires aid starting, steering, and stopping in snow, while chains conquer glare ice and deep pack.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: Between which exact calendar dates are studded snow tires legal on New Jersey roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Metal studs chew up bare warm asphalt, restricting legal New Jersey use from mid-November to April first.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.question_text: What throttle, gear, and rocking techniques help get a vehicle moving on snow or ice?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.teaching_text: Gentle revs and a lower gear tame wheelspin, while rocking forward and reverse frees stuck tires.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.question_text: How many seconds of following distance does the manual recommend on snow-covered roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.teaching_text: Notice the weather ladder — three seconds dry, four in rain, and at least six seconds on snow.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.question_text: What speed and two lighting choices belong whenever you drive through fog?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.teaching_text: High beams reflect blinding white glare off water droplets, so drop speed and run low beams plus fog lamps.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.question_text: When fog, snow, or heavy rain cuts visibility severely, where should you go and what lights do you switch on?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.teaching_text: Stopping inside a live lane causes blind pileups, so clear the roadway completely before hitting emergency flashers.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.question_text: If your windshield defroster quits during freezing rain or snow, what three steps help warm the glass?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.teaching_text: Pulling over with windows shut lets rising cabin heat thaw icing glass before your view freezes blind.

sec08-card-sec08-R23.question_text: Which four visor, steering, speed, and visual habits counter blinding sun glare?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.teaching_text: Angling visors without blocking sightlines while gripping firmly, slowing down, and tracking lane paint keeps you centered.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: Whose command must you obey when a police officer directing traffic gives an instruction that conflicts with the traffic light?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Live officers managing wrecks, detours, or gridlock hold legal authority above every automated bulb at the intersection.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: What legal consequence awaits anyone caught stealing or vandalizing traffic, airport, or railroad-crossing signs or equipment?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Missing stop signs or damaged crossing gates create fatal intersection ambushes, so courts punish sign tampering harshly.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: From top to bottom on a vertical traffic light—and on the left of a horizontal light—how are signal colors arranged?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Standardized bulb placement lets color-blind drivers read red on top or far left even in heavy glare.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt at a steady red light, and when may you proceed?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Rolling past the crosswalk edge on red puts your bumper into pedestrian and cross-traffic lanes.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: What does a steady yellow traffic light require unless you are already too close to brake safely?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Treating yellow like a speed-up cue triggers T-bone crashes when cross traffic launches on green.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: What signal transition does a yellow arrow warn you is about to happen?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: That yellow arrow gives turning drivers a brief safety buffer to brake smoothly before red locks the phase.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: Whom must you still yield to on a green light—including before making a left turn?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Green grants permission only after leftover walkers or cars clear—and left turns never outrank straight oncoming traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: How may you move when facing a green arrow—even alongside a red bulb—and whom must you still yield to?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Going straight from a green-arrow lane while the main light sits red runs a live red signal.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: How does pressing a pedestrian push button affect signal timing at an intersection?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Pressing the pole button cycles traffic timing to give crossing walkers a longer green window across the main road.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: How should you respond when approaching a flashing yellow signal?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Flashing yellow flags busy firehouses, hidden curves, or tricky junctions where full speed leaves too little reaction margin.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: What three steps does a flashing red traffic light require?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Treat a flashing red bulb identically to a stop sign—halt completely before yielding to cross traffic and walkers.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: What is the core operational difference between a flashing yellow signal and a flashing red signal?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Confusing the two causes rear-end stops under flashing yellow or dangerous roll-throughs under flashing red.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: How must every driver treat an unlit traffic signal when power is out and no officer is directing traffic?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Assuming the wider boulevard keeps right of way during a power outage causes high-speed broadside wrecks.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: What does a steady orange raised-palm pedestrian signal mean for people at the curb versus people mid-crosswalk?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Clearance timing builds in enough seconds for walkers already in the street to reach the far curb safely.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: What does a white walking symbol or countdown allow pedestrians to do, and what does New Jersey law require of turning drivers?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Turning green lights share the same phase as walk signals, so New Jersey mandates yielding to crossing walkers.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: Into which three broad categories do road signs fall, and what job does each category perform?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Sorting signs into hazard alerts, route directions, and enforceable traffic laws lets you read meaning by color and shape instantly.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: Which single traffic message owns the eight-sided red octagon?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Even caked in blizzard snow or viewed from behind, eight sides signify a mandatory stop and nothing else.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: Which traffic control sign uses the three-sided red triangle?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Pointing downward, that unmistakable three-sided outline tells drivers to slow and concede right of way from afar.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: What roadway restriction does a three-sided yellow pennant sign warn you about?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Mounted on the left side of two-lane highways, the pennant stays visible even when a tall truck blocks right-shoulder signs.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: What type of zone or crossing does a five-sided yellow pentagon announce?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Shaped like a classic one-room schoolhouse roof, five sides cue you to scan for children immediately.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: What roadside activity does an orange diamond sign warn drivers to expect?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Orange always flags temporary construction or maintenance crews working close to live travel lanes.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: What distinct information do blue, brown, and green rectangular highway signs each provide?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: Color-coding lets highway travelers spot gas or lodging in blue, parks in brown, and exit directions in green.
sec15-card-sec15-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Blue services, brown parks, green routes

visual_sync.text_span: Blue services, brown parks, green routes

sec15-card-sec15-F24.question_text: What shape, background color, and legend color identify general roadway warning signs?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.teaching_text: High-contrast black symbols or words on yellow diamonds pop clearly in peripheral vision at highway speeds.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: Beyond general cautions, which two specific warning categories also use the yellow diamond?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Watch yellow diamonds for sharp surface hazards as well as supplemental railroad crossing alerts.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: When do highway engineers mount a smaller advisory speed plaque together with a curve or turn warning?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: Entering a tight ramp or bend at the main highway limit risks sliding wide when safe cornering speed drops lower.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: Which two background colors may pedestrian and bicycle warning signs use, and what action do they demand?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Bright fluorescent yellow-green cuts through dawn and dusk shadows where walkers and cyclists cross.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.question_text: Which five conditions do orange road-work diamonds warn about—and how do New Jersey traffic fines change there?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.teaching_text: Closed lanes, shifted stripes, rough milled asphalt, and exposed crew flaggers explain why every work-zone fine doubles.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.question_text: What enforceable sign type is commonly posted right alongside orange work-zone warnings?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.teaching_text: Lower temporary limits protect crews inches from your mirror and carry doubled fines if ignored.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: Which four spacing, reading, braking, and scanning habits keep everyone safe inside a road-work zone?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: Heavy dump trucks pulling into travel lanes and sudden flagger stops punish tailgaters inside cone tapers.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.question_text: How much legal authority does a construction-zone flagger hold—and what happens if you ignore one?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.teaching_text: Rolling past a flagger's paddle carries the exact same ticket risk as running a posted regulatory sign.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.question_text: What does a fluorescent, reflective orange triangle mounted on the back of farm or construction gear signify?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.teaching_text: Closing highway speed onto a tractor crawls up far faster than normal traffic—brake early on spotting that triangle.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.question_text: What shape and color scheme do most regulatory traffic signs use?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.teaching_text: Tall white rectangles framed in black state enforceable speed, turn, and lane laws rather than mere advice.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.question_text: How are the shape, background, lettering, and borders arranged on a standard YIELD sign?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.teaching_text: Red wording and an inner red border band set inside a downward-pointing white triangle make YIELD unmistakable.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.question_text: Describe the shape, colors, central bar, and text layout of a DO NOT ENTER sign?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.teaching_text: Spotting that horizontal white bar splitting a red circle stops drivers from turning up one-way exit ramps.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.question_text: How do green national truck route signs differ in meaning from red national truck signs?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.teaching_text: Color flips permission instantly—green marks approved truck corridors and ramps while red bars trucks or ends routes.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: How do the round yellow railroad sign and the white X-shaped sign divide advance warning versus track location?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Yellow circles give early braking notice down the road, whereas the white crossbuck stands right at the rails.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.question_text: Which regulatory sign does a white railroad crossbuck match in legal meaning—and why must cars always yield?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.teaching_text: Locomotives locked onto steel rails cannot steer around a car, making every crossbuck an unconditional yield.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: What do flashing red railroad lights announce, and when is it legal to drive across the tracks?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Pulling onto multi-track crossings while bells ring or lights still flash risks getting struck by a hidden second train.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: Which three railroad crossing markers count as passive warnings, and which three count as active warnings?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Passive paint and crossbucks never change when a train nears, so you must look and listen yourself.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.question_text: How does the legal authority of painted road markings compare with posted signs and overhead signals?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.teaching_text: Crossing solid paint or ignoring turn arrows brings a moving violation just like running a sign or light.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.question_text: How do yellow roadway lines and white roadway lines tell you which direction neighboring traffic moves?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.teaching_text: Seeing yellow on your left warns that crossing it puts you nose-to-nose with oncoming traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.question_text: What do a broken centerline stripe versus a solid centerline stripe on your side allow regarding passing?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.teaching_text: Broken paint opens passing only when sightlines are clear, whereas solid paint on your side forbids crossing.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: When a solid yellow stripe runs beside a dashed yellow stripe, who may pass and by what point must the pass finish?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: You must be back inside your lane before those broken dashes turn solid ahead of a blind hill or curve.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: What passing and lane-discipline rules apply along double solid yellow or double solid white lines?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Double solid paint locks out passing from both sides, and slower traffic should keep right to avoid holding queues.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.question_text: What do painted lane arrows paired with signs require, and what do white dashed highway lines separate?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.teaching_text: Once inside a signed arrow lane you must follow that turn or path, while white dashes divide multi-lane same-way traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.question_text: What boundary do white and yellow highway edge lines mark for drivers?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.teaching_text: Continuous edge stripes guide your eyes cleanly along the pavement boundary in rain, fog, or oncoming headlight glare.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.question_text: Where must you stop when a white stop line is painted versus when no stop line is painted?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.teaching_text: Always halt behind the thick white bar when present, or before the crosswalk edge whenever no stop line appears.

sec15-card-sec15-R14.question_text: What purpose do oversized white pavement words like STOP AHEAD, SCHOOL, and RXR serve?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.teaching_text: Reading bold white words right on the asphalt reinforces roadside signs when traffic blocks shoulder views.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.question_text: What do painted or signed white diamonds reserve a lane for, and where do you find the active rules?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.teaching_text: Solo drivers wandering into diamond lanes during posted rush-hour windows face steep HOV citations.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: How does a street speed bump differ physically from a speed hump?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: Speed bumps jolt tires over a narrow low ridge, whereas speed humps stretch longer and flatter across neighborhood streets.

sec15-card-sec15-R17.question_text: How do rumble strips alert drivers, do they harm your tires or suspension, and what usually accompanies them?
sec15-card-sec15-R17.teaching_text: Harmless tire buzz and wheel vibration snap drowsy or distracted drivers awake ahead of tollbooths, curves, or lane edges.

sec15-card-sec15-R18.question_text: How does traffic circulate inside a roundabout, and why do roundabouts slash severe intersection crashes?
sec15-card-sec15-R18.teaching_text: Entering and exiting strictly by right turns around a center island eliminates deadly high-speed left-turn and head-on angles.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: How does alcohol distort a driver's thinking—even in small amounts when someone feels below the limit?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Feeling fine below the legal threshold is a classic trap because even slight drinking clouds judgment and raises crash odds.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Which five physical or visual driving skills start slipping after two, three, or four drinks?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Just a few drinks slow foot-to-brake timing while blurring eyesight and wrecking how you judge car gaps.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: Which emotional state paired with alcohol drives much of the reckless aggression behind fatal highway crashes?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Getting behind the wheel angry after drinking strips away restraint and triggers deadly, aggressive highway maneuvers.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: How many vehicles are involved in most alcohol-related crashes, and who still ends up killed or hurt?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Even when no second car is struck, single-car drunk wrecks routinely kill or maim passengers and pedestrians.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What is the sole cure for intoxication, and in what percentages does your body clear alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Cold showers and coffee cannot speed up a liver burning ninety percent while breath, sweat, and urine clear ten.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: How much pure alcohol sits inside five ounces of wine, twelve ounces of beer, or a one-and-a-half-ounce whiskey shot?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Exam traps try making beer look milder, yet every standard pour delivers roughly half an ounce of pure alcohol.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: In studies cited by the New Jersey manual, what beverage had most arrested drunk drivers been drinking?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Drivers underestimate cans of beer, making beer the number-one drink found in drunk-driving arrests.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: What is the sole scientific measure of alcohol in your system, and what quick test checks it?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Gut feelings lie after drinking—Blood Alcohol Concentration measured on a simple breath test gives scientific proof.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Which four personal or drinking variables determine your Blood Alcohol Concentration?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Two friends drinking together hit different BAC numbers based on drink count, body weight, drinking speed, and food.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: How does eating affect alcohol absorption, and can food stop a high BAC or sober you up?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: A heavy meal only delays bloodstream absorption—steady heavy drinking still spikes BAC and food never sobers anyone.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Why won't eating a big dinner protect a heavy drinker from hitting a high BAC?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Food slows the initial climb without erasing a single drop, so heavy drinking always lands at a high BAC.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: Which drug categories and adult BAC threshold make driving illegal in New Jersey?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Driving impaired by liquor or narcotic, hallucinogenic, or habit-forming drugs—or at point zero eight BAC—breaks state law.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: At what tiny BAC does a driver younger than twenty-one break New Jersey law?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Even mouthwash-trace drinking at point zero one percent triggers harsh underage penalties stacked onto any DUI.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does New Jersey's adult per-se BAC limit contrast with the under-twenty-one threshold?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Adults cross the statutory per-se line at point zero eight, while anyone under twenty-one violates law at point zero one.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: Just past which BAC mark does your statistical risk of causing a crash double?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Before you ever reach the adult point-zero-eight arrest threshold, passing point zero five already doubles crash risk.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: By what multiples does crash risk jump at point one zero BAC and point one five BAC?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Crash odds explode nonlinearly—six times higher at point one zero and twenty-five times higher at point one five.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: How do crash-risk multipliers escalate across New Jersey's three cited BAC benchmarks?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Lock those three rungs in order—double past point zero five, sixfold at point one zero, twenty-fivefold at point one five.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What four core penalties hit a driver who refuses a breath test in New Jersey?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Saying no to the breathalyzer never dodges trouble—expect lost privileges, IDRC referral, fines, and an ignition interlock.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: What extra financial assessment follows a breath-test refusal, and what happens if you leave it unpaid?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Skipping your refusal violation surcharge locks your driving privileges under indefinite suspension until paid.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Which five driving behaviors are New Jersey officers trained to spot as telltale drinking clues?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Patrol officers watch for speeding, lane weaving, crawling slow, jerky speed swings, and sudden stops at lights.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Why do officers treat unusually slow driving—not just speeding—as an impairment red flag?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Intoxicated drivers trying hard not to get noticed often creep well below normal traffic pace.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: Must a car cross painted lane lines for police to spot impaired weaving?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Wandering back and forth between your own two paint stripes still reveals impaired steering control.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: What causes an impaired driver's jerky speed changes and abrupt stops at intersections?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Brief attention blackouts make open-road speed surge and dip, then force panic braking right at stop bars.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: What is the one guaranteed way to prevent a drinking-and-driving crash, and which three ride options fit?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Never getting behind the wheel after drinking—using a designated driver, bus, train, or cab—eliminates alcohol crash risk.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: Whom does a designated driver protect by getting drinking friends or family home sober?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Staying sober behind the wheel safeguards both the friends in your back seat and every stranger sharing the road.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: Which designated-driver campaign did New Jersey become the first state in the nation to launch officially?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Launching the statewide Hero Campaign first put sober designated-driver pledges front and center across New Jersey roadways.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: What three drink-and-food habits define a responsible party host?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Put out substantial food and non-alcoholic drinks, skip aggressive refills, and close the bar well before guests leave.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: How should a host handle an impaired guest, when are police called, and what legal risk hits the host?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Insist on a nap or overnight stay—calling police only as a last resort—because crash victims can sue the host.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: What two drug-related conditions make driving illegal on New Jersey roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Both driving under any drug's influence and transporting prescription-only drugs without a valid script violate New Jersey law.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: What must you show police when driving with prescription medication, and what if you lack proof?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Without valid prescription proof on request, prescription-only pills in your car get treated just like illegal street drugs.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: How should you respond to a drowsiness or dizziness label, and which common medicines impair driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Everyday cold tablets, tranquilizers, and prescription meds carrying drowsy or dizzy warnings dull core driving reflexes.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: Whom must you consult before combining medications, and what substance must never mix with any drug?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Drug combinations multiply drowsiness unpredictably, and adding alcohol to any pill can trigger severe impairment.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: Why should you ask a pharmacist or doctor before driving on an over-the-counter medication?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Buying allergy or cold medicine legally without a prescription never guarantees your reaction times stay sharp.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: Right behind alcohol, which substance turns up most frequently in crash-involved drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Crash toxicology reports find marijuana more often than any other drug right behind alcohol.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: Which four lane, gap, alertness, and attention skills can marijuana weaken behind the wheel?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Cannabis degrades staying centered in your lane, judging gaps, staying alert, and juggling multi-task traffic cues.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: Can everyday aches like a stiff neck, cough, or sore leg hurt safe driving—and what should you do?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: A stiff neck blocks blind-spot checks and a sore leg slows braking, so let someone healthy drive.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: How often does the manual recommend vision checks generally—and once you pass age forty?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Gradual vision shifts sneak up unnoticed, making annual eye checks essential after turning forty.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.question_text: What re-screening power does New Jersey state law grant the MVC over licensed drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.teaching_text: Earning a New Jersey license once does not bar the MVC from retesting drivers later under state law.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.question_text: How does healthy side—or peripheral—vision help while you look straight down the road?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.teaching_text: Strong peripheral sight catches cross-street cars and stepping pedestrians at the edges while your eyes track forward.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.question_text: Why does distance judgment matter constantly around traffic and parked obstacles?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.teaching_text: Knowing your exact bumper clearance from surrounding cars prevents misjudged merges, passes, and rear-end taps.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.question_text: Why does sharp hearing matter in traffic, and what two audio habits keep your ears open?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.teaching_text: Blasting music or wearing earbuds drowns out sirens, horns, and screeching tires before hazards enter view.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: While pedestrian safety is shared, who holds the primary duty to prevent crashes with people on foot—and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Walkers lack steel doors or airbags, placing the heaviest burden on drivers steering multi-ton vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: How does a struck pedestrian's fatality risk jump between twenty miles per hour and forty miles per hour?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Doubling neighborhood speed from twenty to forty multiplies kinetic impact energy enough to turn survivable hits deadly.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: Does an intersection corner without painted white lines still have a legal crosswalk, and what is it called?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Missing paint never erases pedestrian rights where sidewalks or street corners meet at an intersection.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: How does New Jersey distinguish a driver's legal duty at a marked crosswalk versus an unmarked crosswalk?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Know both exact verbs because painted lines require coming to and holding a full stop until walkers clear.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: What must you do if the pedestrian signal switches to don't walk mid-crossing, and what two crosswalk actions are barred?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Swinging around a car stopped at a crosswalk or creeping across painted bars puts mid-crossing walkers in danger.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: Which five consequences can follow failing to stop for a pedestrian—and what escalates the penalty further?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Ignoring a walker in a New Jersey crosswalk risks your license and freedom, especially if serious bodily injury occurs.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: Where should you stop before a crosswalk on a multi-lane road when a pedestrian is crossing—and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Pulling right up to the stripe screens the crossing walker from cars approaching fast in the next lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: What rules bind pedestrians at crossings, and does a walker's mistake ever excuse a careless driver?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Even when someone jaywalks against a signal, motorists remain legally bound to exercise due care to avoid hitting them.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: Around which five community zones—and which curbside hazard—should you slow down and watch for children?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Rows of parked SUVs hide small children at bumper height until they dart out near playgrounds or bus stops.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: What full visual check is required before any turn—especially before turning right on red?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Drivers staring left for oncoming traffic gaps routinely roll right on red into walkers stepping off the right curb.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: Why do so many pedestrian collisions happen during turns, and which three off-street access points demand extra vigilance?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Drivers hunting only for metal bumpers overlook people walking across driveways, parking-lot aprons, and alley mouths.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: How should drivers adjust speed and attention for pedestrians after dark or during poor weather?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Rain glare and dark jackets shrink the distance at which headlights reveal someone crossing ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: How should pedestrians walk and dress at night where sidewalks are absent—and how does that affect your duty?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Even if a walker forgets reflective gear or walks with traffic, the driver's duty to stay alert never disappears.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: Do standard traffic laws apply to motorcycles, and how should you check blind spots before turning or changing lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Slim motorcycles react faster to road surface changes and slip easily behind window pillars on a single quick glance.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: Why must you never tailgate a motorcycle in traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Lightweight bikes shed speed far faster than heavy passenger cars, leaving tailgaters zero braking margin.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: How should you manage your speed and lane position while a motorcycle is passing your vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Speeding up or drifting toward the centerline crowds an exposed rider mid-pass with nowhere safe to bail out.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: What single driver failure causes the majority of motorcycle collisions?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Drivers tuned only to wide car silhouettes look straight through an approaching rider in open traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: Which road-surface textures threaten motorcycle stability and can trigger a sudden lane swerve?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: Bridge grates, milled grooves, or sloped patches that four tires barely feel can wobble two wheels instantly.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: Where do motorcycles demand extra visual scanning, and what signaling and spacing habits protect riders?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Left turns across oncoming lanes remain deadly for riders whenever drivers cut corners or skip turn signals.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: Before turning, parallel parking, opening a car door, or pulling from a curb, how must you check blind spots?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Glass mirrors always leave side-quarter dead zones capable of hiding an approaching cyclist or motorcyclist.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: By how much can bad weather stretch the stopping distance of a truck, tractor-trailer, or bus?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Rain or slush adds a full quarter more braking runway to heavy commercial rigs that already stop slowly.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: What does New Jersey call the areas around a truck or bus where its driver cannot see you in the mirrors?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: If you cannot see the trucker's face in their side mirror, they have zero view of your car.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: How should you position yourself when a truck is backing up or preparing to back—and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: A long box trailer blocks sightlines for both the commercial driver and nearby motorists right behind the bumper.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: How far behind a large truck or bus should you travel, and what multi-truck position should you avoid?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Riding pinched between two tractor-trailers leaves zero escape route and hides you from the lead rig's mirrors.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: Why must you stop with extra buffer behind a large truck or bus at a traffic light, especially facing uphill?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Releasing heavy air brakes to engage gears on a grade lets a loaded rig drift backward several feet.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: How may a long truck set up a right turn, and how should nearby drivers respond?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Squeezing into the right-curb gap beside a swinging trailer traps your car beneath its rear axles.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: When may you merge back in front after passing a truck, and which passing side is strictly off-limits?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Cutting in before the whole cab grille fills your inside mirror steals braking space, and right-side passes court blind-spot crushes.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: What should you avoid alongside a truck's trailer, and how should you steer when a large vehicle approaches oncoming?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Edging slightly right as an oncoming rig passes cushions wind buffeting and widens sideswipe clearance.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: Who must yield when a bus re-enters traffic from a passenger stop, and what penalties hit violators?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Blocking a departing transit bus risks fifty to two hundred dollars in fines and up to fifteen days jailed.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: Once a bus has rejoined normal moving traffic, does New Jersey's special bus-yield law cover its lane changes?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Test writers love swapping curb pull-outs with mid-road lane changes—special bus yield ends once the bus rejoins flow.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: What legal rights, duties, and New Jersey classification apply to bicyclists, skateboarders, and inline skaters?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Sharing identical traffic duties with cars while lacking crash protection gives cyclists and skaters vulnerable-user safeguards.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: What three progressive options does New Jersey's Safe Passing Law require when overtaking a covered road user?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Move over a full lane when possible, leave four feet single-lane, or slow to twenty-five prepared to stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: Under the Safe Passing Law, does giving space and slowing down let you break speed limits or no-passing zones?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Safe Passing requires slowing down and moving over when available while still honoring every speed and no-passing rule.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: How do the fine and license points compare for breaking the Safe Passing Law without injury versus causing bodily injury?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Causing bodily injury quintuples the fine from one hundred to five hundred dollars and adds two license points.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: What three visibility items must a bicycle carry after dark—and what caution still applies to drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Small battery bike lamps and reflectors still disappear against wet city glare unless drivers scan actively.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: Whom must a motorist signaling a right turn let pass through the intersection first?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Chopping right across a straight-moving bike or skater triggers classic right-hook intersection crashes.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: How do your responsibilities toward cyclists and skaters work on right turns compared with left turns?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Never cut across riders on right turns, and on lefts yield both to oncoming riders and any rider ahead in the turn lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.question_text: How may a bicyclist or skater position themselves in traffic lanes to make a left turn?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.teaching_text: Expect cyclists or skaters inside left-turn lanes—riding near that lane's right edge keeps them predictable.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: What mechanical feature, top speed, and lane-position rule define a moped in New Jersey?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Capped at twenty-five miles per hour with pedals, mopeds stay right with traffic flow so faster cars can pass safely.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: What wheel count, speed window, and fuel restriction define a New Jersey low-speed vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Electric four-wheelers topping above twenty up to twenty-five miles per hour never burn gasoline or diesel fuel.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: May motorized scooters ride on New Jersey public streets or sidewalks—and what is the lone exception?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: Public roadways and sidewalks are completely off-limits unless a town or county designates specific property for scooters.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: What registration, insurance, and minimum-age rules govern motorized scooters in New Jersey?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Even off public streets, motorized scooters require hometown registration, insurance, and an operator at least twelve or the local floor.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.question_text: Which four mini rigs count as motorized scooters—and which four electric or mobility vehicles do not?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.teaching_text: Separating pocket bikes and motorized skateboards from e-bikes, low-speed vehicles, and disability aids prevents wrong-category test traps.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.question_text: On which posted streets—and up to what scooter speed—may someone with a mobility disability operate certain motorized scooters?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.teaching_text: Approved mobility riders stay capped at fifteen miles per hour on twenty-five-limit streets or locally approved thirty-five-limit roads.

sec13-card-sec13-R18.question_text: What road-use ban, crossing allowance, and paperwork rules apply to snowmobiles, ATVs, and dirt bikes?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.teaching_text: Trail machines cannot cruise public traffic lanes, and even legal road crossings require displayed registration and carried insurance.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.question_text: How far can a fifty-five-mile-per-hour freight train travel before stopping, and who holds right of way?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.teaching_text: Thousands of tons rolling on steel rails need over a mile to halt, giving trains absolute right of way.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.question_text: What schedule, track-direction, and visual-speed realities explain why you must never race a train?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.teaching_text: Large locomotives create an optical illusion that makes fast trains look deceptively slow and distant.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.question_text: When is it safe to pull onto railroad tracks, and how far do trains overhang beyond the steel rails?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.teaching_text: Stopping close to the steel rail is still fatal because wide railcars jut three feet or more past both sides.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.question_text: Within what distance of a railroad crossing is passing banned, and what manual-gear rule applies on the rails?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.teaching_text: Stalling a manual transmission mid-shift on live tracks leaves zero margin if a train rounds the curve.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.question_text: Which roadside sign shape-and-color and pavement markings warn that railroad tracks lie ahead?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.teaching_text: Spotting the round yellow disk and painted white rail letters early lets you check far-side traffic space before reaching the rails.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.question_text: Why is driving or walking across railroad tracks outside a designated crossing illegal as well as dangerous?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.teaching_text: Every rail corridor outside public crossings belongs privately to the railroad, making shortcut crossings unlawful trespassing.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.question_text: What maximum speed applies when approaching or passing a horseback rider or horse-drawn vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.teaching_text: Dropping your pace around riders and buggies prevents engine rush and wind blast from spooking a live horse into traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: Besides slowing to twenty-five or less near horses, what must you do if an oncoming rider raises a hand?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: An oncoming rider raising a hand warns that the horse is restless—halt completely and wait until calm returns.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.question_text: Under which three time, visibility, or weather conditions must a horse-drawn vehicle display a front light?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.teaching_text: Watch thirty minutes post-sunset to pre-sunrise, five-hundred-foot low visibility, and fog, mist, or smoke.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.question_text: Why should you avoid swerving sharply for an animal, and what visual habit protects you instead?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel to miss wildlife routinely sends cars into trees, oncoming lanes, or rear-end pileups.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: Which three types of valid documents must every motorist carry whenever driving in New Jersey?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Getting pulled over with any one of those three cards missing at home earns a roadside citation.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Who must always ride along whenever you drive using a validated New Jersey permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Driving solo on a learner or examination permit breaks supervision rules and risks suspension.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: If wording in the driver manual ever conflicts with an actual statute or state regulation, which controls?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Handbooks summarize rules in plain English, whereas enacted statutes and regulations carry binding legal force.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: How soon after moving—even out of state—must a motorist report the new address to the MVC?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Missing that seven-day reporting window can send renewal notices or legal MVC mail to an old home.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: Within what deadline must you report a legal name change from marriage, divorce, or court order to the MVC?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Court decrees and marriage certificates give twice the reporting window of a home move, capping at fourteen days.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How does New Jersey's address-change deadline compare with its legal name-change deadline?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Permit checks love flipping one week and two weeks—moving is tighter than changing your legal name.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: How long does a new resident holding a valid out-of-state car license have to apply in New Jersey?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: If your former state card expires on day twenty, your sixty-day grace period ends early on day twenty.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: How soon must a new resident transfer a commercial driver license, and what happens to the old card?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Federal commercial rules cut the transfer window in half compared with basic car drivers and forbid holding two licenses.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: For how long may a motorist legally drive in New Jersey using a valid license from another country?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: International visitors get up to twelve months on a valid home-country credential before needing state licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: How do the timelines compare for regular out-of-state transfers, CDL transfers, and valid foreign licenses?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Pairing thirty days for commercial rigs, sixty days for cars, and one year for foreign cards prevents mix-ups.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: Which step-by-step program must every applicant complete if they have never held a driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Phasing in solo driving privileges after supervised practice cuts early crash rates among brand-new motorists.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: What signed paperwork must any license applicant younger than eighteen bring in?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Showing up at the agency before age eighteen without a completed parent or guardian consent form halts processing.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: Which drivers under twenty-one must display two MVC reflective GDL decals, and where are they mounted?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Special learner permits, examination permits, and probationary holders under twenty-one all need decals on both plates.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: What New Jersey credential must a motorist already hold before applying for a commercial driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: You cannot jump straight from unlicensed pedestrian into heavy commercial trucks without earning a basic license first.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: What is the minimum CDL age, and what geographic and endorsement bans apply under age twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Drivers aged eighteen to twenty can run commercial rigs strictly inside New Jersey without carrying passengers or hazardous loads.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: Where are all New Jersey licenses and IDs manufactured since 2021, and what security check fights identity theft?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Moving card printing out of local counters into a secure central plant helps block fraudulent duplicate credentials.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: What do you leave the MVC counter holding, how long is it valid, and how does your plastic card arrive?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Keep your thirty-day interim printout handy while your permanent plastic card ships through the mail.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: Which card orientation goes to motorists under twenty-one, and how many years do licenses and IDs last?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Portrait-style cards flag under-twenty-one status at a glance, while standard validity runs four years.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: How does the lifespan of your counter-issued temporary license compare with the mailed plastic card?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Watch the units closely—thirty days on the interim paper versus four full years on the permanent card.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: When do license endorsements expire, and which single endorsement follows a shorter retest schedule?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Hazardous-materials security rules demand retesting every two years even while your base card still has time left.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: What sets a Hazmat endorsement apart from every other New Jersey license endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Every other endorsement rides along to your four-year card renewal without a mid-cycle two-year retest.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: How does the MVC calculate the fee when you add an endorsement partway through your current license cycle?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: You only pay for the months or years left until your existing base license reaches expiration.

sec01-card-sec01-R20.question_text: What typical prorated fee applies when returning after one year to upgrade to a Standard or REAL ID license?
sec01-card-sec01-R20.teaching_text: Upgrading after your probationary year prorates the remaining three years of your four-year cycle.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: What three punishments can strike someone who alters a license, gets one by fraud, or shows a doctored card?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Tampering with or using a fake card risks suspended driving privileges, up to a thousand-dollar fine, and prison.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: On New Jersey's license requirement chart, what four screenings do the letters K, V, R, and C stand for?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Reading those four shorthand letters tells you instantly which screenings apply to each credential class.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: Which vehicles does a basic Class D auto license cover, and what are its permit and license minimum ages?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Basic Class D covers registered passenger vehicles excluding motorcycles, starting permits at sixteen and unrestricted licensing at eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: What are the permit age, minimum license age, permit and decal fees, and license fee on the probationary auto row?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Watch the chart specifics—ten-dollar permit plus four-dollar decals at sixteen, and seventeen minimum age with a sixty-three-dollar chart entry.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How do the minimum ages for basic and probationary auto licenses compare, and what permit age do both share?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Both tracks let teens start supervised permits at sixteen before stepping to probationary at seventeen and basic at eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: What permit fee, Standard and REAL ID license fees, and three required screenings appear for a basic auto license?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Choosing REAL ID adds eleven dollars over the twenty-four-dollar Standard card, and all applicants clear knowledge, vision, and road checks.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Which vehicle types and letter classes fall under a CDL, what does the permit cost, and what extra screening applies?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Heavy trucks and buses across Classes A, B, and C carry a hundred-twenty-five-dollar permit fee plus specialized commercial testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: What vehicles does Class E cover, what are the two ways it is issued, and what is the minimum age?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Riders at least seventeen can hold standalone Class E or add an M endorsement onto an existing basic license.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: At what age can unlicensed riders get a moped license, and which existing license holders don't need one?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Anyone already holding Class A, B, C, D, or E never needs a separate moped credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: What work is an agricultural license restricted to, which ages qualify, and when does it end?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Farm teens aged sixteen to seventeen can operate agricultural equipment for four years or until earning a basic license at eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: How does the starting age for a moped license compare with an agricultural license?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Moped licensing opens a year earlier at fifteen, whereas farm-only agricultural licensing starts at sixteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: Who needs a New Jersey boat license, and what certificate must every power-vessel operator present?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Running motorboats on fresh, non-tidal waters from age sixteen requires both a boat license and a Boating Safety Certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: What three core categories of proof must a Standard New Jersey license applicant bring?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Standard applicants pair SSN or ITIN proof—or an ineligibility affidavit—with one residential proof and six ID points.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: Which document buckets must combine to reach a Standard applicant's six identification points?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Bringing six points of minor cards fails without at least one primary document, one secondary document, and home address proof.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.question_text: Which four major birth, passport, or state cards count as primary identity proofs for a Standard license?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.teaching_text: U.S. birth certificates, U.S. or home-country passports, and digitized New Jersey licenses or IDs anchor your primary slot.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.question_text: What extra item must accompany a foreign-issued photo driver license for it to count toward identity?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.teaching_text: Standing alone, a foreign driver license cannot satisfy identity verification without a second government-issued document alongside it.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.question_text: For a Standard license, how long past its expiration date can a primary or secondary ID document still count?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.teaching_text: Any primary or secondary card expired longer than three years is rejected at the Standard verification counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F42.question_text: What is the maximum number of one-point documents a Standard applicant can count toward six points?
sec01-card-sec01-F42.teaching_text: Stacking four or five low-value one-point items won't work because the MVC caps one-pointers at two.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.question_text: What extra legal-status proof does the Standard document chart note specifically for CDL applicants?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.teaching_text: Commercial licensing follows federal rules requiring proof of U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: What must accompany any identification document that is not written in English?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Arriving with untranslated foreign records stalls your appointment unless an MVC-approved English translation comes with them.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: What physical condition and official markings are required on identity documents?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Coating a birth certificate in plastic lamination ruins raised state or municipal seals and gets it turned away.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.question_text: How can the MVC respond when submitted documents conflict or look altered, false, or invalid?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.teaching_text: Examiners hold full authority to request more paperwork on mismatches and reject any questionable application outright.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.question_text: What details must appear on Standard residency proof, and how recent must utility bills versus pay stubs be?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.teaching_text: Every residency paper needs your name and home address—utility or credit bills within a year, pay stubs within six months.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: How many address proofs does a Standard license require, and how old may bank, utility, or government mail be?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Standard keeps residency simple—bring one qualifying bill, bank statement, or government letter dated within twelve months.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: Which two MVC-issued cards both show your address yet cannot be paired together as two address proofs?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: When two address proofs are needed, combining your driver license and vehicle registration is explicitly disallowed.

sec01-card-sec01-R18.question_text: Which two bank items cannot be submitted together, and how may you protect private account numbers?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.teaching_text: Pick either your debit card or a bank statement—never both together—and feel free to black out dollar figures.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: What exact combination of address, Social Security, identity points, and status proof does REAL ID require?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Upgrading to federal REAL ID doubles address proofs to two and mandates lawful U.S. presence plus full SSN proof.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.question_text: In what order do REAL ID Steps I, II, and III organize your paperwork?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.teaching_text: Walking through Step I two addresses, Step II full SSN, and Step III six points prevents counter surprises.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.question_text: How many documents may you pick from the REAL ID primary list?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.teaching_text: Even if you own both an unexpired U.S. passport and a certified birth certificate, only one counts as primary.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.question_text: When can paper proofs already shown in REAL ID Steps I and II count again in Step III?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.teaching_text: If a Step I or II paper also appears on the Step III secondary chart, it can pull double duty.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.question_text: In REAL ID Step III, how many one-point secondary documents can count toward your six-point total?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.teaching_text: Just like the Standard chart, REAL ID Step III caps one-point secondary items at two.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How recent must utility bills, bank statements, and first-class government mail be for REAL ID address proof?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: REAL ID tightens date cutoffs sharply compared with Standard's full-year address window—check every statement date before leaving home.

sec01-card-sec01-R19.question_text: On the REAL ID secondary list, which states qualify for an unexpired photo license versus a non-driver ID?
sec01-card-sec01-R19.teaching_text: Out-of-state non-driver IDs do not count here—only a New Jersey non-driver ID or any state's driver license qualifies.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: What must you bring if your current legal name no longer matches your birth certificate?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: Certified marriage, civil union, divorce, or court papers build the unbroken legal bridge from birth name to today.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: What two details must appear inside a divorce decree to restore a previous name at the MVC?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: A decree missing your prior name or lacking explicit permission to resume it won't clear name verification.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: What exact name change can a marriage or civil union certificate prove compared with a divorce decree?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Marriage certificates cover last-name changes only, whereas divorce decrees only authorize returning to a listed prior name.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: How does a Standard applicant without SSN eligibility or an ITIN satisfy that requirement?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Ineligible applicants without an ITIN submit a sworn affidavit either notarized ahead of time or witnessed by MVC staff.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: What must you bring if the Social Security Administration database cannot verify the number on your application?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Pay stubs masking digits won't fix a verification mismatch—bring your Social Security card or past-year W-2 showing every digit.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: What document verification standard must every New Jersey driver license applicant satisfy?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Showing up for permits or licensing without your complete six-point verification stack stops your visit at check-in.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: What eye screening applies to every motorist, and what two follow-ups may the MVC require for impaired sight?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Every driver clears vision screening, and impaired sight can trigger a physician referral plus periodic rechecks.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: What visual acuity standard must basic license applicants meet, with or without corrective lenses?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Wearing glasses or contacts to hit twenty-fifty satisfies the standard, adding a corrective-lens code to your card.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: What acuity standard and paperwork apply when an applicant has vision in only one eye?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Seeing out of one eye still qualifies once that eye meets twenty-fifty and a licensed physician signs documentation.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: What acuity in both eyes and color-recognition check must CDL applicants pass?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Commercial drivers face stricter eyesight rules—twenty-forty in each eye plus distinguishing red, green, and amber signals.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: How does the vision standard for a basic license compare with the vision standard for a CDL?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Compare both numbers carefully—twenty-fifty works for basic drivers, while commercial applicants need twenty-forty in both eyes plus colors.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: Which self-certification and medical paperwork must commercial drivers file under federal and state rules?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Keeping commercial driving active requires filing your CDL self-certification and, when applicable, a certified examiner's medical card.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: What must license applicants disclose to the examiner regarding health, and what can follow?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Sharing medical conditions up front lets the agency evaluate whether a formal medical review is needed for safe driving.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: How many scored items appear on the New Jersey knowledge check, and what extra survey item is included?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Expect fifty driving-rule items on screen followed by one unscored organ-donation registry prompt.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: What percentage and exact number of right answers out of fifty are needed to pass the written screening?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Missing eleven items drops you below eighty percent, so you can miss at most ten out of fifty.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: Along with English and American Sign Language, how wide is New Jersey's written-screening language menu?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Standard terminals offer English, ASL, plus twelve spoken languages ranging from Spanish, Arabic, and Chinese to Turkish.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: How does the MVC accommodate an applicant who cannot read in any language?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Audio headphones let applicants who cannot read text listen to every item and respond orally.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: What prerequisite must happen before you can use a state-approved interpreter for an unlisted native language?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: You cannot book a foreign-language interpreter on try one without first attempting one of the MVC's offered languages.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: How far in advance must you notify the MVC when you need an interpreter for your written screening?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Securing an approved interpreter takes scheduling lead time, requiring at least fourteen days' advance notice.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: Even though ASL is built in, what two steps precede getting an interpreter for an unlisted foreign language?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: First attempt an offered language, and if unsuccessful, give at least two weeks' notice to arrange an approved interpreter.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: Who supplies and pays for approved Deaf or Hard of Hearing interpreters, and what paperwork triggers payment?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Deaf or Hard of Hearing applicants get MVC-arranged interpreters paid by the state once a payment voucher is filed.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Which New Jersey court registry determines whether a foreign-language interpreter is state-approved?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Friends or relatives cannot translate—your interpreter must come off New Jersey's court-maintained Language Services registry.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: Which two qualification paths make a Deaf or Hard of Hearing interpreter state-approved?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Qualifying interpreters either hold national RID certification on file with NJ's Division or pass that Division's own evaluation.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: How is the appointment set once a foreign-language interpreter is secured, and how are Deaf interpreter fees paid?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: MVC staff reach out directly with your scheduled foreign-interpreter slot, and Deaf interpreter costs clear via payment voucher.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: Which transfer applicants aged eighteen or older can have both knowledge and road screenings waived?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Adults holding valid non-provisional credentials from any U.S. state, D.C., or U.S. territory skip written and road checks.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: Even when screenings are waived, what must an adult out-of-state transfer submit, receive, and surrender?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Waiving exams never waives ID rules—submit six points, trade in your old state plastic, and get a four-year license.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: What New Jersey credential and rules apply to an out-of-state transfer aged seventeen to eighteen holding a valid license?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Even with an unrestricted license back home, a seventeen-year-old newcomer steps onto a one-year GDL probationary license.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: How does the license issued to an eighteen-plus non-provisional transfer differ from a seventeen-to-eighteen transfer?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Age eighteen unlocks the four-year basic license on transfer, whereas seventeen-year-olds serve one probationary GDL year.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: Which screenings must every out-of-country applicant pass, what else may apply, and how long do results last?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Foreign-country transfers always pass knowledge and vision checks—and possibly a road check—with scores good for two years.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: How do screening waivers differ between U.S. state transfers and foreign-country applicants?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Qualifying U.S. state transfers can skip knowledge and road checks, whereas every foreign-country applicant takes knowledge and vision.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: When did Nikhil's Law take effect, and what warning did it add into New Jersey's licensing statute?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Signed August 2015 and active March 1, 2016, Nikhil's Law ensures applicants confront the deadly cost of breaking traffic laws.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: What four safe-driving commitments make up the Safety Pledge to Nikhil?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Leaving five minutes early, stopping completely, staying alert, and using hands-free audio target rushed intersection tragedies.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: When can eligible citizens start voter registration at the MVC, and how many days before an election is the cutoff?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Applying for or renewing a license or ID opens voter sign-up, with registration closing twenty-one days pre-election.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: How can someone register to vote or update a voting address without doing an MVC card transaction?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Anyone outside a license transaction can request a mailed voter application straight from the New Jersey Division of Elections.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: How are MVC address changes submitted, and what follow-up question appears during that process?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Filing your address change online automatically prompts whether you want your voter registration address updated too.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: Where does the MVC forward address updates, and whom should you call if no voter confirmation arrives?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: If the Division of Elections forwarding leaves you without a confirmation card, check with your county Commissioner of Registration.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: Which address must you legally keep on file with the MVC, and how can your plastic card show it?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Once your current New Jersey residence processes in the system, you can order a replacement license displaying it.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: Which steps must be completed before the MVC validates a permit for practice driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Clearing written and eye checks—plus any mandatory behind-the-wheel school—earns the validation stamp needed to practice.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: How many months, total hours, and dark hours of supervised practice must GDL holders under twenty-one finish before road evaluation?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Scheduling your road slot under twenty-one requires six full months and fifty logged hours, including ten after sunset.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: How long must GDL permit holders aged twenty-one or older practice under supervision before a road appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Adult GDL permit holders complete at least three months of supervised driving before taking the road evaluation.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: How do pre-road-appointment practice minimums compare between GDL permit holders under twenty-one and twenty-one-plus?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Under-twenty-one learners double the calendar wait to six months and add the fifty-hour, ten-night requirement.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: Which signed form from a parent, guardian, or supervising driver must be handed in at the road appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Arriving at the road line without your signed BA-CSD supervised-driving form turns your appointment away.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: Which two MVC areas are strictly off-limits for practice driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Rehearsing inside the MVC road course or its parallel-parking bay is prohibited at all times.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: Which five original items—covering your ID, permit, and car—must you bring to the road appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Photocopies or laminated permits get rejected—bring original six-point IDs, unlaminated permit, valid inspection proof, registration, and insurance.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: What exterior GDL markers must already be mounted on a GDL applicant's vehicle at the road appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: Pulling into the road-evaluation lane without both red decals properly mounted on the plates triggers an instant turn-away.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: What insurance rule applies if you bring a vehicle registered in another state to your New Jersey road appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Out-of-state plates are welcome at the road line provided the car satisfies its own state's insurance-card law.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.question_text: Under what contract condition may you use a rental car for your road evaluation?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.teaching_text: If only your parent's name appears on the rental paperwork without listing you as an authorized driver, examiners refuse it.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.question_text: Can a permit holder inch the car forward alone in the road-evaluation queue while the accompanying driver steps out?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.teaching_text: Even creeping ten feet forward in the waiting lane without your licensed driver seated inside violates permit law.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.question_text: When must your accompanying licensed driver—rather than you—drive the car to the road-evaluation site?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.teaching_text: Because a New Jersey permit supervisor needs a NJ license and three years' experience, anyone else must do the driving there.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.question_text: Does the MVC provide vehicles for road evaluations, and who is allowed inside during the drive?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.teaching_text: Parents, instructors, and pets wait outside once the evaluation begins—only MVC examiners ride along.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.question_text: Besides your driving skills, what else can end your road evaluation before you even roll out?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.teaching_text: Examiners inspect the vehicle first and refuse to ride in any car with safety defects or blocked brake access.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.question_text: What brake access must the right-seat examiner have inside your road-evaluation vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.teaching_text: Center consoles blocking the foot pedal and foot-operated left-side parking brakes fail unless the examiner can reach a brake.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.question_text: Which two vehicle types are barred from the road evaluation, and what three visibility or signal items must work?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.teaching_text: Three-wheeled autocycles and self-parking cars are disqualified, and broken turn signals, brake lamps, or wipers cancel your run.

sec03-card-sec03-F43.question_text: Which five sticker, brake, dashboard-light, or tire issues commonly get a vehicle turned away?
sec03-card-sec03-F43.teaching_text: Check your inspection sticker, center brake reach, pedal feel, dash brake lamp, and tire tread before appointment morning.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.question_text: What paper saves a car that failed inspection, and why does a fast engine idle get rejected?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.teaching_text: A valid station Vehicle Inspection Report covers a failed sticker window, while a racing idle masks low-speed pedal control.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.question_text: Starting from which manufacturing date must every vehicle have seat belts to pass pre-drive inspection?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.teaching_text: Any post-July 1, 1966 vehicle missing working seat belts is turned away immediately at the starting line.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.question_text: Which four front-tint, mirror, glass, or door defects will get your vehicle rejected?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.teaching_text: Tinted front side windows, missing interior or left mirrors, cracked glass, or stuck inside latches all halt the check.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.question_text: What brake-pedal, lighting, and interior cleanliness standards apply to your road-evaluation car?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.teaching_text: Spongy pedals sinking to the floorboard, dead lights, or a trash-filled passenger cabin give examiners grounds to refuse.

sec03-card-sec03-R17.question_text: For motorcycle and moped road evaluations only, which four rider-gear or horn problems cause rejection?
sec03-card-sec03-R17.teaching_text: Two-wheel applicants need state-required bike gear, a helmet, approved goggles or face shield, and a 100-foot horn or bell.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: In what two course settings may an MVC examiner ride along to grade your safe driving?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Depending on the testing site, your examiner evaluates rule mastery either on a closed range or live public streets.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.question_text: What extra skill will the examiner check if you bring a manual-transmission car?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.teaching_text: Driving a stick shift means showing smooth, controlled clutch work and gear selection throughout the course.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.question_text: Which core driving maneuvers—including reversing, parallel parking, turns, turnarounds, and yielding—appear on the basic road check?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.teaching_text: Examiners grade posture and belt use alongside reversing, parallel parking, K-turns, smooth stops, following distance, horn use, and yielding.

sec03-card-sec03-F41.question_text: What slip do you get upon passing the road evaluation, and what three items go to a Licensing Center?
sec03-card-sec03-F41.teaching_text: Passing at the course yields a licensing authorization—carry it with your permit and six ID points to get licensed.
