sec03-card-sec03-F42.question_text: Which license does a brand-new driver receive, and for how long does the MVC monitor their driving habits?
sec03-card-sec03-F42.teaching_text: First-time motorists earn a Class D probationary or basic credential while the MVC tracks their record closely for twelve months.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: Unless posted otherwise, which three New Jersey zones carry a twenty-five-mile-per-hour speed limit?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Heavy foot traffic, driveways, and school crossings cap unposted town and school blocks at twenty-five.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: Unless posted otherwise, what default speed limit governs suburban business and residential districts in New Jersey?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Wider setbacks on suburban corridors step the unposted cap ten miles above compact town centers.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How do New Jersey's two lowest unposted speed limits—twenty-five and thirty-five—split up districts?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Watch the word suburban on the exam—adding suburban bumps business and residential defaults from twenty-five to thirty-five.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What default speed limit applies on unposted rural roadways in New Jersey?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Country two-lane roads without speed signs cap out at fifty rather than fifty-five.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: Which two road categories carry New Jersey's fifty-five-mile-per-hour speed limit?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Fifty-five serves as New Jersey's standard expressway ceiling unless signs specifically grant sixty-five.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: Where is driving sixty-five miles per hour legal in New Jersey?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Never assume sixty-five on unposted stretches or regular state highways—only designated interstate corridors post it.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: What distinguishes where fifty-five applies from where sixty-five applies on New Jersey highways?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: State highways can post fifty-five, whereas sixty-five belongs exclusively to specifically signed interstate segments.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: What happens to ticket fines when you go ten or more over—or commit most moving violations—inside a sixty-five zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Higher interstate speeds paired with strict enforcement double standard fines once you push seventy-five or drive recklessly.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: How does speeding hurt crash odds, crash violence, and your window to react?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Excess speed shrinks your hazard-correction window right as kinetic impact forces climb steeply.
sec06-card-sec06-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Higher risk, harder hits, less time

visual_sync.text_span: Higher risk, harder hits, less time

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: How sensitive are pedestrian injury and survival odds to even small changes in vehicle speed?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Shaving just a few miles per hour in town dramatically boosts a struck walker's survival odds.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: Can driving at or below the posted speed limit still earn a moving violation in bad weather or heavy traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Driving too fast for rain, fog, or traffic violates state law regardless of the number printed on the sign.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Name the road features, crossings, weather, and sightline conditions that always demand slowing down?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Narrow lanes, rail tracks, intersections, blind bends, walkers, wet ice, and poor visibility all shrink stopping margins.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.question_text: When should you shed speed for a curve, and what lane risk must you watch for inside it?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.teaching_text: Braking mid-curve risks skidding wide right where fast opposing drivers often drift across the centerline.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: When pavement and traffic are clear and normal, what does New Jersey law say about crawling far below pace?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Unreasonably slow cruising on clear dry pavement triggers frustrated tailgating and risky passes behind you.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: What should you do if engine trouble keeps your car from maintaining safe traffic speed?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Limping along or backing up in active lanes causes rear-end collisions that shoulder hazard stops avoid.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: What passing rule applies when both yellow centerlines are solid?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Solid paint on both sides warns sightlines are too short for either lane to overtake safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: When one centerline stripe is dashed and the partner stripe is solid, which direction may overtake?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Only drivers with dashed yellow paint directly beside their left tires have clear sightlines ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: Who may pass when both parallel centerline stripes are broken?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Matching dashed stripes confirm straight, level sightlines open to drivers heading both ways.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: How do you read solid, mixed, and double-broken centerlines from the driver's seat?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Checking your own side's paint instantly separates forbidden passes from legal overtaking zones.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: Before what pavement-marking change must every two-lane pass be completely finished?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Cutting back across newly solid yellow paint puts you head-on inside a blind hill or curve zone.

sec06-card-sec06-R24.question_text: When may you legally cross solid no-passing lines between intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.teaching_text: Solid centerlines outlaw overtaking slower cars yet still let residents and shoppers turn carefully into driveways.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: Signed in July two thousand three, what penalty rule does New Jersey's Safe Corridors law enforce?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Speeding and aggressive-driving citations cost twice as much along posted Safe Corridor state highways.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: Which two crash statistics put a New Jersey state highway onto the Safe Corridors list?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Logging at least one thousand crashes over three years alongside a rate fifty percent above average triggers designation.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: Passing belongs normally on the left—which two narrow situations allow passing on the right?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Only two-plus steady same-way lanes or ample paved room beside a left-turning car makes right passing legal.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: May you ever drop tires onto the right road shoulder to squeeze past a left-turning vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Shoulders harbor broken glass, cyclists, and stopped cars—turning unpaved or edge pavement into a lane breaks state law.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: List the blind terrain, crossings, structures, markings, and pedestrian situations where passing is banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Anywhere sightlines vanish—hills, bends, rail grades, intersections, tunnels, narrow bridges, or stopped crosswalk cars—forbids overtaking.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: Which half of the road must New Jersey drivers hug, and what are the two exceptions?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Staying near the right edge keeps opposing lanes separated outside active passes or one-way streets.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: Which lane is your home lane on a multi-lane New Jersey road when not overtaking or turning left?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Cruising in the rightmost open lane leaves inner passing lanes clear and predictable.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: Which emergency responders and rail vehicles command your right-of-way every time?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Sirens, flashing emergency beacons, and approaching locomotives outrank every passenger car on the road.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: Which two public-service vehicles receive right-of-way when pulling back into traffic from the curb?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Easing off the gas to let signaling buses and mail trucks merge keeps transit and delivery routes moving.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: Does a legal crosswalk require white paint—and where do crosswalks exist by default?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Unless signs explicitly bar foot crossings, every intersection corner holds a legal crosswalk paint or no paint.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: What exact pedal action does New Jersey require when a pedestrian is inside a marked or unmarked intersection crosswalk?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Rolling slowly toward a crossing walker violates New Jersey's strict stop-for-pedestrians statute.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: Once stopped for a crosswalk pedestrian, how far across must they walk before you roll again?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Waiting until the walker clears both your lane and the adjacent same-way lane gives a full safety buffer.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: What must you do if your light turns green and Don't Walk appears while someone is still crossing?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Changing signal lights never strip protection from a pedestrian still on the asphalt.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: What two actions around crosswalks—involving stopped cars and parking—are strictly prohibited?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Whipping around a car stopped at a crosswalk strikes hidden pedestrians stepping past its front fender.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Which five penalties—money, jail, service, license, and points—can hit drivers who fail to stop for pedestrians?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Up to five hundred dollars, twenty-five days jail, community service, six-month suspension, and two points underscore strict enforcement.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: Along with walkers on foot, whom else must you yield to at crosswalks and inside intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Motorized wheelchairs, scooters, and vehicles already occupying the intersection hold clear priority.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: Where do most crashes happen, and what does a single solid white bar across the road mean there?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Conflicting paths make intersections crash hotspots, and the white stop bar keeps bumpers clear of cross flow.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: How does New Jersey classify cutting across private property to bypass a red light or stop sign?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Dodging corner controls through strip-mall lots endangers pedestrians and carries moving-violation penalties.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: At an all-way stop, how are earlier arrivals and simultaneous ties decided?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Drivers already waiting roll first, and yielding right breaks simultaneous ties cleanly.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: What speed and right-of-way duties apply at a posted yield sign?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Always approach slow enough to halt completely whenever cross-road traffic closes the gap.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: How does right-of-way at a multi-way stop contrast with right-of-way at a yield sign?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Multi-way stops rotate turns and break ties right, whereas a yield approach always defers to cross traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: Within how many feet of the crosswalk or stop line must you halt at a New Jersey stop sign?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Stopping twenty feet back behind a tree hides cross traffic and fails New Jersey's five-foot rule.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: How must every approach treat a traffic signal gone dark from a power outage or malfunction?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Blasting through a blacked-out intersection as if green causes severe T-bone crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: How do you approach an unsigned crossroad versus pulling out of a private driveway?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Unsigned crossroads need cautious two-way readiness, while private driveways always defer to main-road traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: When tall corn, trees, bushes, buildings, or parked cars hide cross traffic, how must you adjust?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Never guess across a blind corner—stop and edge out slowly until sightlines open both ways.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: At an uncontrolled intersection, which driver yields under New Jersey's baseline rule?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Checking your right first and deferring when you sit on the left prevents unsigned-corner collisions.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: Since New Jersey sets no single statewide traffic-circle rule, what three clues govern right-of-way at circles?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: Older Jersey circles vary in design, so read entrance stop or yield signs, major-route flow, and historical patterns.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Which baseline intersection rule takes over whenever right-of-way inside a traffic circle is unclear?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Falling back on yielding to vehicles on your right prevents hesitation crashes at ambiguous circles.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: How are highways, parkways, and turnpikes built—and who yields at an acceleration-lane merge?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Mainline traffic cruising up to sixty-five holds priority while ramp traffic blends in via acceleration lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: What speed goal and stopping caution apply as you merge off a highway acceleration lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: Stopping at the end of a ramp forces you to launch from zero into sixty-mile-per-hour traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.question_text: What must you do—and never do—if you sail past your intended highway exit?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.teaching_text: Backing down a deceleration lane or ramp puts you head-on against sixty-mile-per-hour exiting traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: How do your speed actions contrast between an acceleration lane and a deceleration lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Keep ramp physics clean—never stop on the entry runway, and wait until the exit lane to shed speed.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.question_text: Which side carries most highway exits, and how do you handle an occasional left-side exit?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.teaching_text: Spotting overhead left-exit banners early lets you move left smoothly instead of cutting across lanes late.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.question_text: Inside a shared weave lane serving both entering and exiting expressway cars, which driver yields?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.teaching_text: Clearing exiting cars off the expressway first prevents mainline backups inside tight cloverleaf weave zones.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.question_text: How should you navigate the tight curving ramps of a cloverleaf interchange?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.teaching_text: Tight two-hundred-seventy-degree loops demand obeying advisory ramp plaques closely so tires never break loose.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.question_text: Which lanes does New Jersey recommend on multi-lane city highways during heavy rush hour?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.teaching_text: Holding center or left through dense city interchanges leaves the right lane open for constant ramp merges.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.question_text: What three habits keep you safe entering, picking a lane at, and leaving a highway toll plaza?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.teaching_text: Queues stack up fast ahead of green-lit open booths, and wide plaza aprons funnel lanes back together afterward.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.question_text: How should you respond when you spot a broken-down vehicle on the highway shoulder ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.teaching_text: Changing lanes away and slowing protects stranded passengers, tow operators, and troopers stepping near live asphalt.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.question_text: List the shoulder, signal, cabin, and personal-safety rules if your own car breaks down on a highway?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.teaching_text: Raising the hood with flashers on while waiting belted behind locked doors—and refusing rides from strangers—maximizes safety.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: Whom must you yield to and whom must you stop for whenever turning left?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Fixating solely on gaps in oncoming cars blinds left-turners to pedestrians stepping into the side-street crosswalk.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: Before making any turn—including right on red—what full visual sweep protects cyclists and walkers?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Checking behind and over your shoulder catches curbside cyclists and walkers beside your rear fender.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.question_text: Under what sign check, stopping rule, and yield duty is turning right on red legal in New Jersey?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.teaching_text: Confirm no prohibitive plaque hangs overhead, halt completely, and yield to every oncoming car and pedestrian.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.question_text: Which slim road users might hold a green light across your path while you turn right on red?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.teaching_text: Cross-street cyclists and mopeds blend into headlight clutter yet hold full green-light priority.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.question_text: How close to the right edge should you position for a right turn, and what steering mistake is banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.teaching_text: Swinging left like a tractor-trailer lures trailing drivers right or drifts into opposing cross-street lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.question_text: When you and an oncoming driver face each other and both turn left, where relative to center do you pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.teaching_text: Passing in front of each other—left of the center point—keeps sightlines open past each other's hoods.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.question_text: Which departure lane and arrival lane belong to a left turn from one one-way street onto another?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.teaching_text: Keeping tight curb-to-curb on the left avoids crossing paths with dual turn lanes or straight flow.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.question_text: Turning left from a two-way street onto a four-lane highway, which lane do you enter first—and what comes next?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.teaching_text: Completing the turn into the inner passing lane first avoids cutting across two lanes mid-intersection before signaling right.

sec06-card-sec06-R23.question_text: How do you line up and finish a left turn from one two-way street onto another two-way street?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.teaching_text: Cutting the corner early clips the opposing left-turn box, so stay right of the new road's centerline.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: During which window at a traffic light do most signal crashes occur, and how should you start on a fresh green?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Red-light runners blow through right after signals flip, making blind jackrabbit starts on green dangerous.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: What should you do when a green light turns yellow ahead — and what if it flips while you are already inside the intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Slamming brakes inside the box invites rear-end hits, so stop before entry when safe or continue through cautiously.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: What is a stale green traffic light, and what phase change should you anticipate?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Spotting a light that was already green down the block keeps you ready to brake smoothly.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: Which octagon sign and which two red signal displays always require a complete stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Whether a red bulb shines steadily or pulses on and off, rolling past without halting breaks the law.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Which cane-carrying or guide-dog pedestrians — including trainers — require drivers to come to a stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: New Jersey protects both blind pedestrians using white or metallic canes or guide dogs and instructors actively training dogs.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: Along with pedestrians on foot, which mobility users at a crosswalk or intersection require drivers to stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Motorized wheelchairs and mobility-assistance devices carry the exact same crosswalk stop protection as pedestrians on foot.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: When must you come to a full stop for a traffic officer or at a YIELD sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: A yield sign turns into a mandatory full stop whenever cross traffic leaves no safe gap.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: What stopping duty applies when emerging from an alley, private driveway, or building — and at an opening drawbridge?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Sidewalk pedestrians cross unseen outside buildings and driveways, and rising bridge spans leave zero margin.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: Which six static, lit, gated, audible, or human warnings can mark a New Jersey railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Expect any combination from advance signs and pavement paint up to bells, red flashers, gates, or human flaggers.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: At least how many feet back must you stop at a railroad crossing when lights flash, bells ring, gates lower, or flags wave?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Pulling closer than fifteen feet puts your hood inside lowering gate arms and locomotive side overhang.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: After halting at an active railroad crossing, which three signals must all clear before you drive across?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Rolling forward the instant the last car passes while lights still flash risks hitting a second oncoming train.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: How much distance do most trains traveling sixty miles per hour or faster need to stop, and what rule follows?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: An engineer slamming emergency brakes at highway speed still slides past a full mile before halting.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Which three vehicle types must stop at every railroad crossing, and how should you drive behind them?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Tailgating a bus or hazmat truck toward quiet tracks causes rear-end collisions when they make their mandatory halt.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: What space check prevents getting trapped on railroad tracks — and what must you do if warning bells start while you are already on them?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Freezing or backing up once flashers start mid-track traps your car right inside the impact zone.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: What two situations around a school bus require every approaching driver to stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Even before spotting flashing lenses, kids stepping on or off a yellow bus demand an immediate stop.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: What light sequence do school buses use when stopping, and why shouldn't drivers behind a bus rely solely on those lights?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Malfunctioning warning bulbs never excuse passing a stopped school bus where children are boarding.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: How many feet away must you stop for a red-flashing school bus, and on which three road types does that full stop apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Two-lane streets, painted-line multi-lane highways, and private roads all lack physical barriers, requiring a twenty-five-foot stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: On a dual-lane highway, what must you do when a stopped school bus is across a safety island or raised median from you?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: New Jersey does not let opposing divided-highway traffic blast past at full speed, capping your pass at ten miles per hour.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: When a school bus stops directly in front of a school to load or unload, how may drivers pass from either direction?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Curbside school loading zones supervise students onto school grounds, allowing cautious passing up to ten miles per hour.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: Which two specific New Jersey school-bus scenarios replace the twenty-five-foot full stop with a ten-miles-per-hour speed cap?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Exam writers test these exact two New Jersey exceptions constantly because most states either stop fully or allow normal speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: When may you resume driving after stopping for a school bus, and whom must you still watch carefully for?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Late-running children or pedestrians with developmental disabilities may step out unexpectedly right after flashers turn off.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: What three-step sequence applies when approaching an ice cream or frozen dessert truck displaying flashing red lights and a stop arm?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Excited kids dart toward ice cream trucks without looking, so come to a full stop before creeping past at fifteen max.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: On a dual highway, must a driver on the far side of a safety island or raised median stop for a frozen dessert truck?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Unlike a school bus that slows opposing divided traffic to ten, a raised median excuses stopping for a dessert truck.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: How do you clear the way for a signaling emergency vehicle, and how far back must you stay afterward?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Drafting closer than three hundred feet behind a racing ambulance blinds you to sudden stops or second responders.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How does New Jersey split red warning lights from blue warning lights among emergency responders?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Identified private cars driven by volunteer fire or rescue members answering calls run blue lights rather than red.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: How close may you park to a fire department vehicle in service, and when may you drive across a fire hose?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Crushing a pressurized fire hose cuts water pressure inside a burning building unless an official waves you across.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Keep New Jersey's two emergency-vehicle distances straight — following a signaling rig versus parking near a fire rig in service?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Moving vehicles demand the longer three-hundred-foot cushion, while parked cars stay outside two hundred feet.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: Which stopped vehicles — including disabled civilian cars — trigger New Jersey's Move Over lane-change rule when safe?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Beyond police, tow, and highway trucks, disabled motorists displaying hazards, flares, or triangles also earn an empty adjacent lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: Under New Jersey's Move Over law, what must you do when changing lanes is impossible, illegal, or unsafe?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Forcing an unsafe swerve causes crashes, so drop sensibly below the posted speed and cover the brake.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: What dollar fine range hits a Move Over violation, and when do motor vehicle points get added?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Every violation risks one hundred to five hundred dollars, while racking up three or more convictions triggers license points.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: When patrol lights flash behind your car, what three immediate steps bring you to a safe stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Signaling right away tells the officer you see them while you guide smoothly onto the shoulder or a safe spot.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: Once pulled over by police, what five gear, cabin, window, lighting, and hand positions should you take?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Shifting to park, rolling down your window, flipping on the night dome light, and resting hands on the wheel keeps everyone safe.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: Why shouldn't you dive into the glove box or console during a police stop before the officer asks — and what else keeps things calm?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: Sudden unannounced reaches under seats or into consoles look dangerous, so wait until asked and state what you are doing.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.question_text: When is switching on your vehicle's interior overhead light appropriate?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.teaching_text: Driving long stretches with cabin lights on ruins night vision through windshield glare unless requested during an officer stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: Which three credentials or papers must every New Jersey driver produce at a traffic stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Missing any one of the big three — license, registration, or insurance — adds an avoidable citation.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.question_text: How should you respond to an officer's requests — including stepping out — or to an instruction you did not catch clearly?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.teaching_text: Stepping out when directed is lawful, and asking politely for clarification prevents misunderstandings.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.question_text: If you think a traffic stop or ticket is unfair, where should you challenge it instead of arguing at the roadside?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.teaching_text: Roadside arguments never erase a citation, whereas traffic court or an agency complaint gives you formal review.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: Between which exact sunset and sunrise offsets must New Jersey drivers run their headlights?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Waiting until pitch-black night breaks the law because headlights start thirty minutes after sunset through thirty minutes before sunrise.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Regardless of the clock, which visibility distance, wiper setting, and weather conditions require headlights?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Rain running your wipers, fog, mist, smoke, or visibility dropping to five hundred feet or less all mandate headlights.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: Can parking lights or auxiliary lights legally substitute for headlights when headlights are required?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Dim marker bulbs or aftermarket auxiliary lamps fail legal forward-illumination standards whenever full headlights are required.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.question_text: How are fog lights classified, and which headlight beam setting pairs legally with them in fog?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.teaching_text: Combining low-mounted fog lamps with low beams lights the pavement under fog without bouncing high-beam glare back.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: Where are high beams appropriate, and which two traffic encounters require switching them off?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Blasting high beams into an oncoming windshield or a leading driver's mirrors blinds the person sharing your road.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: Contrast the driving environments calling for high beams against the four everyday situations calling for low beams?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Town streets, heavy traffic, following behind cars, and meeting oncoming headlights all belong strictly on low beams.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.question_text: What happens inside a driver's eyes at night that lets sudden bright headlights blind them momentarily?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.teaching_text: Dark-adapted pupils open wide to gather faint light, then abruptly constrict when blasted by bright beams.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: How many seconds can glare recovery take after oncoming high beams, and how far do you travel at fifty miles per hour meanwhile?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Driving the entire length of a football field effectively blind shows why speed and eye placement matter against glare.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes if an oncoming driver leaves high beams on — and why shouldn't you flash yours back?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Tracking the right pavement edge preserves your sight while flashing high beams back creates two blinded drivers head-on.

sec07-card-sec07-R16.question_text: When do taillights illuminate at night versus in daylight, and how do they show braking?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.teaching_text: Steady red glow marks your rear at night, then flares brighter — day or night — whenever your foot presses the brake.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.question_text: What balance should you strike when adjusting dashboard instrument lights at night?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.teaching_text: Cranking gauges to maximum glow shrinks your night vision outside, while turning them black hides your speedometer.

sec07-card-sec07-R19.question_text: For what sole purpose are spotlights and hazard flashers meant — and what use of spotlights is strictly banned?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.teaching_text: Sweeping a bright spotlight down a travel lane blinds everyone ahead, restricting both tools to genuine emergencies.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: Where must a parked vehicle keep its parking lights switched on?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Unlit rural roadsides lack streetlamps, requiring parking lights anywhere outside business or residential districts.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: What is the maximum legal distance between a parked vehicle and the curb in New Jersey?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: New Jersey enforces a tight six-inch curb rule rather than twelve inches so parked cars never pinch narrow lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: Within how many feet of a fire hydrant is parking prohibited in New Jersey?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Memorize ten feet specifically for New Jersey exams, since neighboring states often test fifteen feet.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: How far must you park from an intersection crosswalk, and what single junction type is exempt?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Keeping twenty-five feet open at street corners lets turning drivers see pedestrians before entering crosswalks.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: Which two traffic controls share New Jersey's fifty-foot no-parking distance?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Both railroad crossings and octagon stop signs demand fifty clear feet so approaching drivers spot them early.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: What no-parking distances apply on the same side of a fire station driveway versus across the street?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Wide-turning engines need twenty feet flanking the apron plus seventy-five clear feet opposite the doors.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Which two different New Jersey locations both enforce a twenty-foot no-parking buffer?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Pair the end of a pedestrian safety zone with a same-side fire station entrance under the twenty-foot rule.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.question_text: From sidewalks, bus zones, and driveways to tunnels, double parking, and disability spots, where is stopping or parking always banned?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.teaching_text: Blocking walkways, driveways, intersections, interstates, elevated spans, tunnels, curbed cars, or unauthorized accessible spots is illegal.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.question_text: Why must you scan for traffic, bikes, and mopeds before opening your street-side door — and which side should passengers exit?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.teaching_text: Swinging a driver door into a passing cyclist or car can make you legally liable, while curb-side exits protect passengers.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.question_text: Where should you pull over and what lights should you activate during mechanical trouble or an emergency?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.teaching_text: Clearing live lanes onto the right shoulder with four-way flashers pulsing warns approaching traffic early.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.question_text: How does New Jersey classify handheld phone or texting use on public roads versus hands-free phone use?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.teaching_text: Police can pull you over solely for holding a phone, and even legal hands-free calls split mental focus.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.question_text: Which five emergencies permit using a handheld phone while driving, and what steering rule still applies?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.teaching_text: Even while reporting fire, crashes, serious road hazards, medical crises, or hazmat spills, keep one hand gripping the wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.question_text: What evidence might a driver have to show in court to prove a handheld call met the emergency exception?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.teaching_text: Claiming an emergency without phone billing logs or official witness statements rarely beats a handheld ticket.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.question_text: What fine tiers — plus third-offense points and possible suspension — hit repeat handheld phone convictions within ten years?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.teaching_text: Fines climb from two-to-four hundred, to four-to-six hundred, to six-to-eight hundred plus three points and possible ninety-day suspension.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.question_text: Which phones and electronic devices are banned for every New Jersey GDL holder behind the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.teaching_text: Unlike adult drivers, graduated license holders cannot use Bluetooth hands-free calls or any handheld electronic device.

sec07-card-sec07-R26.question_text: When are the only two times a school bus driver may use a handheld or hands-free phone?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.teaching_text: Protecting student passengers bans both handheld and hands-free calls whenever the bus is on the highway.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.question_text: How does Kulesh's, Kuberts' and Bolis' Law treat illegal cell phone use in serious or fatal crashes?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.teaching_text: Causing death or serious injury while illegally on your phone supports criminal recklessness under vehicular homicide and assault-by-auto laws.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.question_text: What fine cap and license consequence can hit drivers who toss trash or dangerous objects onto a New Jersey roadway?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.teaching_text: Tossing dangerous objects brings four-figure fines, while throwing litter out of a moving car jeopardizes your license.

sec07-card-sec07-R27.question_text: How must any trash, debris, or rubbish hauled in a vehicle be prepared before driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R27.teaching_text: Highway wind rips uncovered rubbish out of pickup beds, turning loose debris into illegal road hazards.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: Roughly what percentage of a driver's decisions depend on vision, and what happens to that sight after dark?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Because nine out of ten driving choices rely on eyesight, losing depth and contrast after sunset demands extra care.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: How should you match your nighttime speed to the forward reach of your headlights?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Carrying more speed than your beams illuminate means you will hit dark obstacles before your brakes can finish stopping.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: What beam setting and reaction time does the manual's night stopping table assume — and how many feet per second do you cover at sixty miles per hour?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Taking one point five seconds to react in darkness eats up massive ground when sixty covers eighty-eight feet every second.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: On low beams at twenty miles per hour, what reaction, braking, and total stopping distances does the night table list?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Even neighborhood twenty-mile-per-hour cruising burns forty-four reaction feet plus thirty-one braking feet before stopping.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: On low beams at forty miles per hour, what reaction, braking, and total stopping distances does the night table list?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Doubling speed from twenty to forty nearly triples total stopping room through eighty-eight reaction plus one-twenty-three braking feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: On low beams at sixty miles per hour, what reaction, braking, and total stopping distances does the night table list?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Four hundred nine total feet — combining one-thirty-two reaction and two-seventy-seven braking — easily outruns typical low-beam reach.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: On low beams at seventy miles per hour at night, what reaction, braking, and total stopping distances does the table list?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Needing one-fifty-four reaction plus three-seventy-six braking feet proves fast highway night speeds outrun low beams.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: Beyond staying inside headlight reach, what speed, scanning, and space habits keep night driving safe?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Wider buffers and lower night speeds help you catch dark cyclists, pedestrians, animals, signs, and unlit cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: At which four low-light times of day — plus what weather visibility threshold — do headlights belong on?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Flip headlights on for dusk, night, dawn, gloomy dark days, and whenever weather drops sight below five hundred feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: What lighting rule does New Jersey law enforce whenever your windshield wipers are running?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Daytime rain spray hides gray and silver cars in mirrors unless full headlights and taillights illuminate automatically.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: Who holds the right of way in a crosswalk, and does lacking painted lines excuse drivers from stopping?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Pedestrians plus wheelchair and mobility-device users always hold crosswalk priority whether lines are painted or unmarked.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: How many seconds ahead of your vehicle should you scan while driving, and what does that time horizon mean?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Looking twelve travel-seconds down the road spots hazards early enough to steer or slow smoothly without panic.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: At twenty-five miles per hour on a clear city street, how much physical distance does a twelve-second scan cover?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Scanning a full block ahead in town catches double-parked delivery vans and jaywalkers before you reach the corner.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: How do you give yourself the extra reaction time needed in heavy city traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Crowded city blocks throw doors, bikes, and brake lights at you simultaneously, so easing speed buys precious seconds.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: What speed, left-right scan, and foot position apply as you near an intersection — and where should your speed be lowest?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Looking left first catches the closest cross-traffic lane while reaching your slowest roll right at the crosswalk.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: What does an intersection with zero lights or signs mean — even on a wide, smooth, busy road?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Wide pavement never grants automatic right-of-way at an unsigned crossroad where collision prevention rests on you.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: How big a role does speeding play in crashes — and does dry, clear highway weather prevent speed-related wrecks?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Driving past the limit or too fast for traffic ranks among top crash causes even on sunny dry highways.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: Why can wide-open highways lull drivers into trouble, and what three habits counter that danger?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Relaxing on open rural stretches blinds you to unsigned farm crossroads unless you stay alert within the limit.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: Which road features do warning signs announce, and why must you slow down before reaching them rather than braking hard on top of them?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Slamming brakes over a bump, dip, narrow bridge, hill crest, or rail track upsets suspension balance and spins cars.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: How should you respond when deer or livestock stand in a rural or open road, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Startled deer or cattle bolt back across lanes unpredictably instead of holding a straight path.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: What happens to fines for motor vehicle violations committed inside a New Jersey roadway construction zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Every moving violation inside orange construction cones hits your wallet at twice the normal fine.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: How far ahead can a work zone be announced, and what two warnings alert approaching drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Spotting advance signs or flashing work trucks a half-mile early gives plenty of room to merge smoothly.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: How does routing traffic by a detour differ from routing traffic by a work-zone diversion?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Detours send you onto a separate street network, whereas diversions shift lanes or cross medians on the same corridor.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: Which five attention, obedience, lighting, following, and speed rules form New Jersey's work-zone basics?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Switching headlights on helps crews spot you in dust and glare while obeying flaggers and keeping wide gaps.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: Which cabin distractions — even legal ones — should you skip in a work zone, and what attitude keeps crews safe?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: Narrow barrier chutes leave zero drift margin for tuning radios or chatting hands-free beside heavy equipment.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: Which two roadside markers signal that a work zone is over and normal driving may resume?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Accelerating before passing the End Road Work sign or the final temporary control device risks double-fine tickets.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: Roughly how many fatal crashes and serious-injury crashes strike U.S. work zones each year?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: Nearly eight hundred fatal wrecks and past thirty-seven thousand serious-injury crashes yearly show why work-zone focus saves lives.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: Which transmission gear position is the only one that lets an ignition release the key?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Safety interlocks trap the key until you shift fully into Park so parked cars stay anchored.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: What happens if you twist a steering-column ignition to the lock position while the vehicle is still moving?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Clicking the lock pawl into the steering shaft mid-roll freezes your front tires into an unsteerable path.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: What abrupt inputs usually trigger skids, and does recovery differ between front-wheel-drive and rear-wheel-drive cars?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Whether front-wheel or rear-wheel drive, sudden turns, lane darts, or hard braking get corrected the exact same way.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: When the rear of your car slides sideways, what do you do with the gas pedal, steering wheel, and your eyes?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Easing off throttle while steering smoothly where the tail slides and looking toward your target path realigns traction.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: What happens if you yank the wheel sharply away from a skid — and what must you avoid doing with the brakes in a side skid?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Cranking away from the slide or touching the brake pedal locks sideways tires into a full spinout.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.question_text: Once you feel your skidding tires bite and bring the vehicle back under control, what steering step finishes recovery?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.teaching_text: Holding recovery angle too long after grip returns whips the tail into an opposite-direction counter-skid.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: For a highway emergency stop, how does your speed when leaving the travel lane differ between a paved shoulder and an unpaved shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Paved shoulders handle slowing safely out of traffic, whereas soft gravel or dirt shoulders grab fast tires unless slowed first.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: After an emergency stop on the shoulder, where do you place your two flares or warning devices — including pace count?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Setting one flare behind the bumper and another three hundred feet — roughly one-twenty paces — warns fast traffic early.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.question_text: Once stopped on a shoulder, what lighting, standing-position, hood, and white-cloth distress steps apply?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.teaching_text: Never stand blocking your taillights in the dark while raising the hood and tying white cloth on the antenna or left handle.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: If your right wheels accidentally drop onto the highway shoulder, what speed and steering-turn fraction bring you safely back onto pavement?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Jerking back at highway speed catches the pavement lip and flips cars across oncoming lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.question_text: What is the three-step summary for recovering safely after running off the pavement edge?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.teaching_text: Patience on the shoulder beats panic steering every single time tires drop off asphalt.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: Contrast your highway speed when intentionally pulling onto a paved shoulder versus accidentally drifting off the pavement?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Intentional paved exits preserve main-lane flow, whereas accidental drop-offs must scrub down to twenty-five before climbing the lip.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: What sparks most vehicle fires, and what three rules govern your response if your car catches fire?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Toxic smoke and fuel vapors escalate electrical fires rapidly, so get everyone clear and call firefighters instead of fighting it.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: Roughly how long does a car with closed windows and doors float on water, and what is your best escape route?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Water pressure pins submerged doors shut fast, making an open window while still floating on the surface your best exit.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: Compare the manual's three-to-ten-minute float window with the time window it says is plenty to escape?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Knowing three to five calm minutes is plenty inside a three-to-ten-minute float window prevents fatal panic.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.question_text: Why does wearing a seat belt improve survival if your vehicle plunges into water?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.teaching_text: Staying conscious through the initial water slam is the only way you can unbuckle and climb out.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.question_text: Why must you hit power-window switches immediately upon entering water — and what does breaking side or rear glass take?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.teaching_text: Water can short window motors quickly, after which tempered side or rear glass breaks only with a hard heavy object.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.question_text: Which end of a front-engine car sinks first, when will a submerged door finally open, and how do you find the surface?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.teaching_text: Engine weight pulls the nose down, cabin flooding equalizes door pressure, and rising air bubbles point straight up.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: If your car stalls on railroad tracks with zero train in sight, must passengers still evacuate — and whom do you call?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Silent rails turn deadly in seconds, so clear everyone far away first before calling the Crossing Notification sign or nine-one-one.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: When a train bears down on your stalled vehicle, at what angle and in which direction should you run?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Impact blasts shattered car metal forward down the tracks, so running diagonally toward the train dodges flying wreckage.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: If conventional disc and drum brakes fail on the road, what two immediate steps try to slow the car and rebuild pressure?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Dropping to a lower gear adds engine braking while rapid hard pedal pumps can rebuild hydraulic line pressure.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: If pumping failed brakes builds zero pressure, how must you apply the parking brake — and why hold its release?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Keeping your thumb on the release lets you ease off instantly if the rear tires lock into a skid.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: When a tire suddenly goes flat or blows out at speed, what steering, gas, and brake discipline brings you to a safe stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Touching the brake during a blowout yanks the rim hard toward the flat side and flips or spins the car.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Contrast what your right foot does during conventional brake failure versus a tire blowout?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Pumping saves hydraulic failure, whereas touching the brake pedal during a tire blowout destroys straight-line control.

sec09-card-sec09-R22.question_text: What happens to power steering if your engine dies while moving, and how do you get off the road?
sec09-card-sec09-R22.teaching_text: Mechanical steering still links to the front wheels, though turning without engine assist takes much heavier arm force.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: If your accelerator sticks down, what four-step sequence brings the car safely to a stop before shutting off the engine?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Shifting to neutral disconnects racing engine power immediately while keeping power steering alive until you pull off.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: If your hood latches fail and the hood flies up against the windshield, where can you look to guide off the road?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Peeking beneath the raised hood hinge or out your side window along lane paint guides you safely onto the shoulder.

sec09-card-sec09-R23.question_text: What steps should you follow if your headlights abruptly go dark at night?
sec09-card-sec09-R23.teaching_text: If toggling the headlight or dimmer switch fails after stopping safely, marker lights, hazards, or signals keep you visible.

sec09-card-sec09-R24.question_text: What three actions apply if your windshield wipers quit working during rain or snow?
sec09-card-sec09-R24.teaching_text: Driving blind behind a sheet of water is lethal, so slow immediately onto a safe turnout with emergency flashers.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: When a sudden collision threatens ahead or beside you, what are your three evasive choices?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Drivers often freeze onto the brake pedal alone, forgetting steering clear or accelerating out of danger.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: During an emergency stop to dodge a crash, how do you brake with ABS versus conventional non-ABS brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Stomping conventional brakes solid locks the front tires straight ahead so steering inputs do nothing.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: Why do you hold firm pedal pressure with ABS yet pump conventional brakes when steering around a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Antilock sensors pulse automatically to preserve steering, whereas human pumping keeps conventional tires rolling.

sec09-card-sec09-R25.question_text: While swerving to dodge a collision — or steering onto a soft shoulder — what brake mistake must you avoid?
sec09-card-sec09-R25.teaching_text: Combining hard braking with sharp evasive steering overloads front tire grip and triggers a skid.

sec09-card-sec09-R26.question_text: In which two impact-angle scenarios with open road ahead is flooring the gas the right crash-avoidance move?
sec09-card-sec09-R26.teaching_text: When an errant car charges your flank or rear bumper with clear lane ahead, full throttle clears the hit zone.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: If an impact cannot be avoided completely, which direction should you steer and what kind of roadside object should you pick?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: Leaving the pavement into bushes or yielding brush absorbs energy far gentler than oncoming metal or concrete.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.question_text: Rank the three impact targets from least severe to worst when a collision is unavoidable — and what impact angle helps?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.teaching_text: Matching-direction motion cuts closing force, fixed objects beat doubled head-on speed, and glancing blows shed energy.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.question_text: Seconds before a head-on crash while wearing a shoulder belt in an airbag-equipped car, how should you protect yourself?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.teaching_text: Your belt and airbag restrain your torso, while raising arms and hands guards your face from flying glass.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Contrast your last-second head-on crash defense with a shoulder strap and airbags versus having neither?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Without belts or airbags to stop forward launch, throwing yourself across the seat dodges the steering column and glass.

sec09-card-sec09-R27.question_text: When you spot an unavoidable rear-end hit coming in your mirror, what three brake, body, and headrest actions protect you?
sec09-card-sec09-R27.teaching_text: Pressing your skull firmly against the headrest cuts whiplash while braking keeps you out of the car ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-R28.question_text: What steering grip and recovery readiness help if another vehicle is about to strike you from the side?
sec09-card-sec09-R28.teaching_text: Side impacts whip your car into sudden rotation, requiring a firm grip to steer back under control.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.question_text: Which crashes must New Jersey drivers report to police — and what strict rule governs fatalities at the scene?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.teaching_text: Notify police for any injury, fatality, or vehicle or property damage, and never move a body before responders arrive.

sec09-card-sec09-R29.question_text: What two duties apply if you scrape or hit an unattended parked vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-R29.teaching_text: Leaving just a windshield note falls short in New Jersey, where notifying police is mandatory alongside finding the owner.

sec09-card-sec09-R30.question_text: Whether involved in or witnessing a crash, what five roadside steps help secure the scene?
sec09-card-sec09-R30.teaching_text: Parking clear of lanes while alerting police and EMS and warning approaching traffic prevents secondary wrecks.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.question_text: What dollar-damage threshold or injury triggers a ten-day written MVC crash report, what excuses filing it, and whom do you call immediately?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.teaching_text: Damage past five hundred dollars or any injury requires notifying your insurer immediately plus filing within ten days unless police report it.

sec09-card-sec09-R31.question_text: Why doesn't a driver need to mail a separate written MVC report after police investigate — and what medical advice applies if shaken up?
sec09-card-sec09-R31.teaching_text: An official police crash report satisfies MVC filing so you can simply request a copy and get checked promptly.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: How does New Jersey classify driving, and what can follow serious violations alongside fines and jail?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Because driving is a state-granted privilege rather than a constitutional right, violations can bring suspension plus fines and jail.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: Which unpaid tickets, coverage gaps, health issues, crash faults, or ignored notices can cost your driving privilege?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Even unpaid parking tickets, lapsed insurance, or ignoring an MVC letter can strip your driving privilege.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: Are all New Jersey license suspensions automatic, or who decides discretionary ones?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: When statutes do not mandate an automatic suspension, the MVC Chief Administrator or judges weigh each case.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: What check may the MVC Chief Administrator order before deciding whether to suspend a problem driver?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Re-testing a problem driver lets the MVC verify current skill and rule knowledge before pulling the license.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: How many license suspensions over what timeframe label a New Jersey driver a habitual offender?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Picking up a third suspension inside thirty-six months brands you a habitual offender with severe escalated penalties.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.question_text: Falling how far behind on child support or court-ordered health coverage can suspend which licenses?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.teaching_text: Six months of unpaid support or ordered health coverage lets courts suspend both driving and occupational licenses.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: What is New Jersey's minimum age to buy, possess, or drink alcohol, and what about adult suppliers?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Buying for minors backfires hard—both underage drinkers and adults supplying them face serious legal consequences.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: What fine and license hit can strike someone under twenty-one caught buying or drinking at a licensed venue?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Ordering or drinking underage in a bar, restaurant, or liquor store risks five hundred dollars plus lost driving privileges.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: When does an underage alcohol suspension start if the teen isn't licensed yet, and what class may apply?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Having no license yet saves nothing—the suspension clock waits until your eligibility birthday, alongside possible alcohol education.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: How long is the suspension for a first underage offense with BAC from point zero one to under point zero eight?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: The thirty-to-ninety-day suspension starts on whichever date arrives later—conviction day or your license-eligibility date.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: Alongside suspension, what community service and coursework hit a first underage BAC offense?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Expect two to four weeks of community service plus either IDRC attendance or an alcohol-and-highway-safety course.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: What fine, IDRC hours, and jail ceiling apply to a first adult DUI from point zero eight to under point one zero?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Even the lowest adult DUI bracket brings up to four hundred dollars in fines, IDRC detention, and thirty jail days.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: What court-fine bracket applies to a first DUI when BAC reaches point one zero percent or higher?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Crossing point one zero BAC bumps the first-offense court fine bracket up to three hundred through five hundred dollars.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: How do court fines shift when a first-offense BAC climbs from under point one zero to point one zero or above?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Keep that point-one-zero dividing line sharp—fines step from two-fifty-to-four-hundred up to three-hundred-to-five-hundred.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: What annual violation surcharge—and for how many years—hits a first DUI conviction?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Three thousand dollars in state surcharges dwarfs the base court fine on a first New Jersey DUI.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What fees does the IDRC charge for its twelve-hour program versus its forty-eight-hour program?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Offenders pay out of pocket for detention—two hundred sixty-four dollars for twelve hours or three hundred twenty-one for forty-eight.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: Who must report to an Intoxicated Driver Resource Center, and what two steps happen there?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Every alcohol-offense detainee completes highway-safety alcohol education and undergoes screening for deeper substance treatment.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: How are first-, second-, and third-time alcohol offenders split between county and regional IDRCs?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Every New Jersey county runs centers for first and third offenses, whereas second offenses route to three regional sites.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: Which repeat-offender group goes to a regional IDRC rather than their home county's IDRC?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Exam questions target this counterintuitive split—first and third stay county-based while second-timers report regionally.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: How long is the minimum referral treatment program after IDRC screening, and how does it tie to relicensing?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Skipping or failing your sixteen-week treatment referral blocks restoration of your New Jersey license.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: What action on New Jersey roads triggers implied consent to a post-arrest breath test?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Using New Jersey roadways automatically consents to police or hospital breath testing after an intoxicated-driving arrest.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: Where are you taken if you refuse a breath test, and what may medical staff do there?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Refusing to blow into the machine can still end at a hospital with staff drawing a blood sample.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: How much is the yearly violation surcharge—and for how many years—after refusing a breath test?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Breath-test refusal matches a first DUI's steep one-thousand-dollar-a-year surcharge across three straight years.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: On a refusal conviction tied to a first offense, what must happen before driving privileges return?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: You lose driving privileges until an approved ignition interlock breathalyzer is fitted onto your vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Above what BAC reading does an ignition interlock breathalyzer block the engine from starting?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Blowing anything higher than point zero five percent locks the starter before the vehicle ever leaves Park.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How does an ignition interlock's engine-lockout BAC compare with New Jersey's adult DUI limit?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Interlocks enforce a tighter margin than the point-zero-eight DUI law, refusing ignition past point zero five.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: How long must an ignition interlock remain installed after a first DUI from point zero eight to under point one zero?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: In the lowest adult BAC bracket, three months of post-restoration interlock monitoring unlocks full driving.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: How long is an interlock required after restoration on a first DUI from point one zero to under point one five?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Hitting the middle first-offense BAC band stretches post-restoration interlock time to seven through twelve months.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: When and for how long is an interlock mandatory on a first DUI at point one five BAC or higher?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: At point one five or above, the device stays installed throughout suspension and another twelve to fifteen months afterward.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: How does post-restoration interlock time for a breath-test refusal compare with a point-one-five-plus first DUI?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Both top out at fifteen months after restoration, though refusal starts at nine months versus twelve for high BAC.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: How long must an interlock stay installed after a second or later DUI or refusal conviction?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Repeat alcohol or refusal convictions require multi-year interlock monitoring—two to four full years past restoration.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: Under the February 2024 update for qualifying alcohol arrests, why install an interlock voluntarily before conviction?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Installing an interlock voluntarily ahead of conviction under the updated 2024 rule can trim both fines and suspension time.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.question_text: What added penalty applies if you drive after skipping a court-ordered ignition interlock installation?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.teaching_text: Dodging a court-ordered interlock installation tacks an extra full year onto whatever suspension already stands.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: How do fines and jail escalate across first, second, and third offenses for driving while suspended?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.teaching_text: Fines climb five hundred, seven-fifty, one thousand—with up to six extra suspended months first, five jail days second, ten third.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.question_text: What fine, added suspension, and jail range hit driving while suspended for DUI, refusal, or habitual offending?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.teaching_text: Getting caught behind the wheel during an alcohol or habitual suspension stacks one to two extra years plus possible jail.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.question_text: How does jail time jump on a first offense if that DUI- or habitual-suspended driver enters within a thousand feet of a school?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.teaching_text: Driving suspended for DUI or habitual status on school grounds, crossings, or within one thousand feet brings sixty to ninety jail days.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.question_text: When does driving while suspended cross into an indictable fourth-degree crime?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.teaching_text: Driving while suspended for a second or subsequent DUI or refusal conviction elevates straight to a fourth-degree crime.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.question_text: What happens to a vehicle owner who knowingly hands keys to someone suspended for DUI or refusal?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.teaching_text: Lending your car to a DUI-suspended friend risks losing your own license and registration six months, a thousand dollars, and fifteen jail days.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: How do base fines climb across first, second, and third unsafe-driving convictions—plus what court surcharge hits each?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Every unsafe-driving plea tacks a flat two-hundred-fifty-dollar court surcharge onto rising fifty-to-five-hundred base fines.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: When does New Jersey's 'no-point' unsafe-driving offense suddenly post four penalty points?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Wait more than five years or avoid strike three—a third unsafe-driving conviction within five years of the prior drops four points.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: What jail maximum, fine range, and record hit can a first reckless-driving conviction bring?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Even a first reckless-driving conviction risks sixty days behind bars, up to two hundred dollars, and license points.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: By how much over a sixty-five-mile-per-hour limit does speeding trigger doubled fines?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Hitting seventy-five or faster—or committing select moving violations—inside a sixty-five zone doubles your fine.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Which two New Jersey highway settings double moving-violation fines?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Pair highway work zones with ten-plus speeding—and select violations—in sixty-five-mile-per-hour corridors for doubled fines.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: How do fines and points differ when carelessly passing a vulnerable road user causes injury versus no injury?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: No-injury close passes cost one hundred dollars and zero points, jumping to five hundred dollars and two points with injury.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: What fine hits a driver who refuses an officer's request to illuminate the driver's compartment at a stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Refusing to switch on your interior dome light when asked during a night stop carries a fifty-dollar fine.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: What penalties apply for keeping an open alcohol container or unsealed cannabis item in the passenger cabin?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Unsealed booze or cannabis in the cabin costs two hundred dollars first, then two-fifty or ten community-service days.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: What fine applies just for driving without clearing snow or ice off your car—even if nothing falls?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Officers do not have to wait for ice sheets to fly off—driving uncleared alone brings twenty-five to seventy-five dollars.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: How high do fines climb for private drivers versus commercial rigs when dislodged ice causes harm or damage?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Shattering a trailing windshield with roof ice costs private drivers up to a thousand and commercial rigs up to fifteen hundred.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: Leaving a car unauthorized along a limited-access highway for four-plus hours risks what first-time fine and suspension?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Ditching a car four hours on a parkway or freeway risks five hundred dollars and up to two suspended years.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: How high do fines and suspension climb on a repeat highway vehicle-abandonment offense?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Abandoning a highway vehicle a second time doubles the fine ceiling to a thousand and stretches suspension up to five years.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: What fine, jail time, and first-versus-repeat license loss hit an injury or fatal hit-and-run?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Fleeing an injury wreck brings up to five thousand dollars, one-eighty jail days, one year lost first—and permanent loss next.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: Up to what fine, prison term, and mandatory license loss punish auto-insurance fraud?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Faking an insurance claim or application risks five thousand dollars, three prison years, and a mandatory one-year license loss.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: What fine, jail maximum, and privilege loss punish lying on a license or registration form?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Falsifying an MVC form brings two-hundred-to-five-hundred dollars, up to six jail months, and six-month-to-two-year privilege loss.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.question_text: What fine and jail sentence apply to taking someone else's license exam—or hiring a stand-in?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.teaching_text: Both the impostor in the chair and the applicant who sent them face up to five hundred dollars and ninety jail days.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.question_text: Which privileges and first-time fine hit someone convicted of boating DUI on New Jersey waters?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.teaching_text: Operating a boat drunk on New Jersey waters suspends your road driver's license alongside boating privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: When did New Jersey launch GDL, how does it build safer drivers, and what age unlocks an unrestricted license?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Gradual step-by-step practice since 2001 keeps first-time drivers supervised longer before full unrestricted driving at eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: What permit, minimum age, signature, and course enrollment kick off GDL Option A, the early bird road?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Starting at sixteen requires both a parent or guardian signature and active enrollment in approved behind-the-wheel training.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: What form and three proof categories must a teen supply before the instructor can buy a special learner permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Your driving instructor cannot purchase the permit at the MVC until your full identity, address, and SSN packet is ready.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: Who purchases the special learner permit, and how long does that permit remain valid?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Teens and parents cannot buy a sixteen-year-old's special learner permit at the counter themselves—only an approved instructor can.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: Once an instructor purchases a special learner permit, how long does the permit itself stay good?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Two full years gives plenty of runway to finish six-month supervised driving without rushing.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: On Option A, which two MVC screenings must you pass, and when does the MVC validate the permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Passing vision and knowledge checks alone isn't enough—MVC validation waits until your behind-the-wheel course is done.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: What makes up an approved special-permit driving course, and what MVC trip time cannot count toward it?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Waiting in line at the agency for permits or testing never counts toward your six full behind-the-wheel hours.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: After completing six-hour training, which specific MVC facility must validate a special learner permit before practice starts?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: Not every agency branch has a Driver Testing Center attached, so verify the location before heading over.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: When is a permit holder legally allowed to start practice driving on New Jersey roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Practicing in a family car with an unvalidated permit counts as unlicensed driving even with a parent beside you.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: On Option A, who must buy the Special Learner Permit and what milestone unlocks MVC validation?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Questions frequently test both bookends—approved instructor purchase up front and completed behind-the-wheel training before validation.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: What minimum months, total hours, night hours, and plate markers apply to Option A supervised practice?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Every Option A teen logs at least six months and fifty supervised hours—including ten after dark—displaying red decals.
